+	defer r.mu.Unlock()
+	logger, name := r.logger, r.name
+	if logger == nil {
+		if r.cfg.Logger != nil {
+			logger = r.cfg.Logger
+		} else {
+			logger = slog.Default()
+		}
+	}
+	if name == "" {
+		name = cfgFirst(r.cfg.Name, "jsconsumer")
+	}
+	return logger, name
+}
+
+// FloorStationaryFor reports the durable's last observed ack floor (a stream
+// sequence), how long it has been stationary there, and whether any
+// observation exists yet. Exposed so an adopter can publish the stall as a
+// gauge — the signal the ack-floor monitor pages on — from inside the process
+// rather than by polling consumer info a second time.
+//
+// The age is measured from the first observation of that floor value, so a
+// freshly started process under-reports an already-old stall rather than
+// over-reporting it: the breaker can be late, never early.
+func (r *Retry) FloorStationaryFor() (floor uint64, age time.Duration, ok bool) {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	defer r.mu.Unlock()
+	if !r.haveFloor {
+		return 0, 0, false
+	}
+	return r.floor, r.clock().Sub(r.floorSince), true
+}
+
+// observeFloor records one ack-floor reading, restarting the stationary clock
+// when the floor has moved.
+func (r *Retry) observeFloor(floor uint64, at time.Time) {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	defer r.mu.Unlock()
+	if r.haveFloor && r.floor == floor {
+		return
+	}
+	r.haveFloor = true
+	r.floor = floor
+	r.floorSince = at
+	r.stallLogged = false
+	r.gapLogged = false
+}
+
+// pollFloor reads the ack floor until ctx is cancelled or stop is closed
+// (the consume loop winding down). It samples once immediately so a
+// long-lived stall is observed at Start rather than one interval later.
+func (r *Retry) pollFloor(ctx context.Context, stop <-chan struct{}) {
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
+	defer cancel()
+	// Cancel on the consume loop closing too, so an in-flight consumer-info
+	// request cannot hold Runner.Stop open for floorPollTimeout. The watcher
+	// exits with ctx via the deferred cancel.
+	go func() {
+		select {
+		case <-stop:
+			cancel()
+		case <-ctx.Done():
+		}
+	}()
+
+	r.pollOnce(ctx)
+	t := time.NewTicker(r.pollInterval())
+	defer t.Stop()
+	for {
+		select {
+		case <-ctx.Done():
+			return
+		case <-t.C:
+			r.pollOnce(ctx)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func (r *Retry) pollOnce(ctx context.Context) {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	cons := r.cons
+	r.mu.Unlock()
+	if cons == nil {
+		return
+	}
+	infoCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, floorPollTimeout)
+	defer cancel()
+	info, err := cons.Info(infoCtx)
+	if err != nil {
+		if ctx.Err() != nil {
+			return // shutting down; a failed read here is the wind-down, not a fault
+		}
+		logger, name := r.log()
+		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor poll failed", slog.Any("error", err))
+		return
+	}
+	r.observeFloor(info.AckFloor.Stream, r.clock())
+
+	// Report a stall the breaker has armed on but not yet cleared — once per
+	// stationary period. This is the case ENT-1535 had no in-process signal
+	// for, and it stays visible even when no delivery matches the blocker
+	// (a filtered consumer whose floor sits below a gap in the stream), where
+	// the breaker itself would otherwise be a silent no-op.
+	floor, age, ok := r.FloorStationaryFor()
+	if !ok || !r.breakerEnabled() || age < r.cfg.FloorAge {
+		return
+	}
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	first := !r.stallLogged
+	r.stallLogged = true
+	r.mu.Unlock()
+	if !first {
+		return
+	}
+	logger, name := r.log()
+	logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor stationary past FloorAge; breaker armed",
+		slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
+		slog.Duration("stationary_for", age),
+		slog.Uint64("last_delivered", info.Delivered.Stream),
+		slog.Int("num_ack_pending", info.NumAckPending))
+}
+
+// isFloorBlocker reports whether msg is the message pinning a stalled ack
+// floor, and the observed stall. The blocker is the sequence immediately
+// above the floor: the floor is, by definition, the last sequence below which
+// everything is settled, so floor+1 is the one delivery that has to settle
+// before the floor can advance (this is the same identification the incident
+// runbook makes by hand).
+//
+// It deliberately does not generalise to "any sequence above the floor". A
+// message far above a floor pinned by someone else is not the blocker, and
+// dead-lettering it would take a merely-slow event away from a ladder it
+// might still recover on.
+//
+// The exact match assumes the consumer's filter matches densely enough that
+// the blocker really does sit at floor+1 — true where the filter covers the
+// whole stream (repo_refs_v1, where the ENT-1535 blocker sat one sequence
+// above the floor). A narrow filter over a sparse stream can leave a gap
+// there, and then the breaker never identifies a blocker. That failure is
+// safe but silent, so it is logged: see the "no delivery at floor+1" line
+// below and the "breaker armed" line in pollOnce.
+func (r *Retry) isFloorBlocker(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg) (blocker bool, floor uint64, age time.Duration) {
+	if !r.breakerEnabled() {
+		return false, 0, 0
+	}
+	floor, age, ok := r.FloorStationaryFor()
+	if !ok || age < r.cfg.FloorAge {
+		return false, floor, age
+	}
+	meta, err := msg.Metadata()
+	if err != nil || meta == nil {
+		return false, floor, age
+	}
+	if meta.Sequence.Stream == floor+1 {
+		return true, floor, age
+	}
+	r.reportFloorGap(ctx, floor, age, meta.Sequence.Stream)
+	return false, floor, age
+}
+
+// reportFloorGap names, once per stationary period, the first failing
+// delivery seen above a stalled floor that is not floor+1. Either the real
+// blocker is elsewhere (another replica holds it, or it is waiting out a
+// ladder rung) or the consumer's filter leaves a gap at floor+1 and the
+// breaker cannot fire at all. The two look identical from inside the process;
+// printing the sequence the breaker wanted against the one it got is what
+// tells them apart from the logs.
+func (r *Retry) reportFloorGap(ctx context.Context, floor uint64, age time.Duration, seq uint64) {
+	if seq <= floor {
+		return // already settled past; not a candidate blocker at all
+	}
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	first := !r.gapLogged
+	r.gapLogged = true
+	r.mu.Unlock()
+	if !first {
+		return
+	}
+	logger, name := r.log()
+	logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor stalled but no delivery at floor+1; breaker cannot identify the blocker",
+		slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
+		slog.Uint64("want_stream_seq", floor+1),
+		slog.Uint64("got_stream_seq", seq),
+		slog.Duration("stationary_for", age))
+}
+
+// Settle applies the mechanism to a delivery whose handler failed
+// transiently, and is the only disposition call such a handler makes. It
+// picks exactly one of:
+//
+//   - the circuit breaker — this message is pinning an ack floor that has
+//     been stationary past FloorAge, and has already had MinDeliveries
+//     attempts: capture to the DLQ and Ack, whatever the attempt count
+//     (Cause CauseFloorAge);
+//   - exhaustion — this is the final delivery: capture to the DLQ and Ack
+//     (Cause CauseExhausted);
+//   - the ladder — NakWithDelay for redelivery (Outcome OutcomeRetried).
+//
+// reason is recorded on the captured copy's Nats-Dlq-Reason header, prefixed
+// with the cause, so the DLQ says why a message is there and not just that it
+// is.
+//
+// A capture failure is never allowed to become a drop: the original is Nak'd
+// instead and the error returned (settle:dlq_publish_failed), so the message
+// survives, the next delivery retries the capture, and — if the ladder is
+// spent — the ack floor stays pinned and the ack-floor monitor fires, which
+// is ENT-1492's deliberate posture for a degraded DLQ path. An Ack that fails
+// after a successful capture (settle:dlq_ack_failed) leaves the original to
+// redeliver and be captured again; a duplicate in the DLQ beats a lost
+// message.
+//
+// On both error paths the returned Settlement reports OutcomeRetried — the
+// message is still coming back — while keeping the Cause of the terminal
+// branch that could not complete, so the caller's metrics show a DLQ path
+// that is being reached and failing rather than one that is idle.
+func (r *Retry) Settle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
+	delivered := backoff.NumDelivered(msg)
+	blocker, floor, age := r.isFloorBlocker(ctx, msg)
+	tripped := blocker && delivered >= r.cfg.MinDeliveries
+
+	s := Settlement{Delivered: delivered, Floor: floor, FloorAge: age}
+	switch {
+	case tripped:
+		s.Cause = CauseFloorAge
+	case backoff.IsFinalDelivery(msg, r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver):
+		s.Cause = CauseExhausted
+	default:
+		return r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
+	}
+
+	if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, s.Cause, reason); err != nil {
+		// Fall back to the ladder so the message is never lost. Preserve the
+		// cause: the caller's metrics should show that the terminal branch
+		// was reached and could not complete.
+		naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
+		naked.Cause = s.Cause
+		return naked, errors.Join(err, nakErr)
+	}
+	if err := msg.Ack(); err != nil {
+		// The copy is in the DLQ but the original is unsettled: it will
+		// redeliver and be captured again. A duplicate in the DLQ is the
+		// right trade against losing the message or pinning the floor
+		// forever.
+		s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
+		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+		return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
+	logger, name := r.log()
+	logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": dead-lettered",
+		slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
+		slog.String("reason", reason),
+		slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
+		slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor),
+		slog.Duration("floor_stationary_for", s.FloorAge))
+	r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+	return s, nil
+}
+
+// DeadLetter captures msg to the DLQ and Acks it immediately, for a failure
+// the handler knows no redelivery can fix — an unprocessable payload, a
+// reference that will never resolve. It is the non-lossy replacement for a
+// bare Term: same terminal effect on the consumer, but the raw message and
+// its headers survive in the DLQ.
+//
+// As in [Settle], a capture failure Naks rather than dropping, and returns
+// the error.
+func (r *Retry) DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
+	floor, age, _ := r.FloorStationaryFor()
+	s := Settlement{
+		Cause:     CausePermanent,
+		Delivered: backoff.NumDelivered(msg),
+		Floor:     floor,
+		FloorAge:  age,
+	}
+	if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, CausePermanent, reason); err != nil {
+		naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
+		naked.Cause = CausePermanent
+		return naked, errors.Join(err, nakErr)
+	}
+	if err := msg.Ack(); err != nil {
+		s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
+		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+		return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
+	r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+	return s, nil
+}
+
+// capture republishes the raw message and headers to the DLQ subject, tagging
+// the reason with its cause.
+func (r *Retry) capture(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, cause Cause, reason string) error {
+	if err := natsmsg.DeadLetter(ctx, r.cfg.Publisher, r.cfg.DLQSubject, msg, string(cause)+": "+reason); err != nil {
+		logger, name := r.log()
+		logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": settle:dlq_publish_failed",
+			slog.Any("error", err),
+			slog.String("dlq_subject", r.cfg.DLQSubject),
+			slog.String("cause", string(cause)))
+		return fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_publish_failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// nak schedules the next delivery on the ladder and completes s.
+func (r *Retry) nak(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) (Settlement, error) {
+	s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
+	s.Delay = r.cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(s.Delivered)
+	err := msg.NakWithDelay(s.Delay)
+	r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+	if err != nil {
+		return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:nak_failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	return s, nil
+}
+
+func (r *Retry) observe(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) {
+	if r.cfg.OnSettle != nil {
+		r.cfg.OnSettle(ctx, msg, s)
+	}
+}

diff --git a/jsconsumer/retry.go b/jsconsumer/retry.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..52c999a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/jsconsumer/retry.go
@@ -0,0 +1,643 @@
+package jsconsumer
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"log/slog"
+	"sync"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/backoff"
+	"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg"
+)
+
+const (
+	// DefaultFloorAge is how long the durable's ack floor may stay stationary
+	// on one message before the circuit breaker dead-letters it, when
+	// RetryConfig.FloorAge is zero. Sized in ENT-1535's Session-1 forensics:
+	// above ~10m so an ordinary transient that settles by attempt 3 never
+	// trips it, below ~25m so the whole stall — including the monitor's own
+	// evaluation lag — fits the 30-minute SLA.
+	DefaultFloorAge = 15 * time.Minute
+	// DisableFloorAge is the explicit RetryConfig.FloorAge value for "no
+	// circuit breaker": the ladder still runs and MaxDeliver still
+	// dead-letters, but a pinned floor is left to the operator. Any negative
+	// value reads the same way; the named constant lets a caller say so on
+	// purpose.
+	DisableFloorAge = -1 * time.Nanosecond
+	// DefaultMinDeliveries is the number of deliveries a message must already
+	// have burned before the breaker will dead-letter it, when
+	// RetryConfig.MinDeliveries is zero. The forensics found events that
+	// recovered on attempt 4 and none that recovered on 5 or later, so a
+	// message is never dead-lettered on the delivery that first failed —
+	// however long the floor has been pinned, it gets at least one retry.
+	DefaultMinDeliveries = 2
+
+	// Bounds on the derived floor-poll interval when RetryConfig.FloorPoll is
+	// zero: FloorAge/10, clamped. The poll is one consumer-info request, so
+	// the ceiling matters more than the floor.
+	minFloorPoll = time.Second
+	maxFloorPoll = 30 * time.Second
+	// floorPollTimeout bounds one consumer-info request so a NATS blip cannot
+	// wedge the poll loop — and, through it, [Runner.Stop], which joins it.
+	floorPollTimeout = 5 * time.Second
+)
+
+// Outcome is what [Retry.Settle] did with a failed delivery.
+type Outcome string
+
+const (
+	// OutcomeRetried means the delivery was Nak'd for redelivery on the
+	// ladder.
+	OutcomeRetried Outcome = "retried"
+	// OutcomeDeadLettered means the raw message and its headers were captured
+	// to the DLQ subject and the original Acked, releasing the ack floor.
+	OutcomeDeadLettered Outcome = "dead_lettered"
+)
+
+// Cause explains an [OutcomeDeadLettered] settlement; it is empty on a retry.
+type Cause string
+
+const (
+	// CauseFloorAge is the circuit breaker: this message was pinning the
+	// durable's ack floor and the floor had been stationary past FloorAge.
+	CauseFloorAge Cause = "floor_age"
+	// CauseExhausted is the ordinary terminal branch: the delivery cap was
+	// reached (ENT-1492's dead-letter-then-Ack, replacing the unsettled Term).
+	CauseExhausted Cause = "max_deliver"
+	// CausePermanent is a caller-declared unprocessable message, dead-lettered
+	// by [Retry.DeadLetter] without consuming the ladder.
+	CausePermanent Cause = "permanent"
+)
+
+// Settlement reports what [Retry.Settle] chose and the state it chose it
+// from, for the caller's metrics and log lines. FloorAge and Floor are zero
+// when no ack-floor observation was available (the breaker is disabled, or
+// [Start] has not run yet).
+type Settlement struct {
+	Outcome   Outcome
+	Cause     Cause
+	Delay     time.Duration // redelivery delay applied, on OutcomeRetried
+	Delivered int           // this message's delivery count, 1-based
+	Floor     uint64        // last observed ack floor (stream sequence)
+	FloorAge  time.Duration // how long the floor had been stationary there
+}
+
+// RetryConfig describes a [Retry]: the one redelivery ladder, the floor-age
+// circuit breaker, and the dead-letter capture they both terminate into.
+type RetryConfig struct {
+	// Backoff is the redelivery envelope applied to a transient failure. Its
+	// MaxDeliver must be positive and must equal the consumer's
+	// Config.EffectiveMaxDeliver() — the two are cross-checked, because a
+	// policy that disagrees with the broker either never reaches its terminal
+	// branch or reaches it early (COR-762).
+	//
+	// TermOnExhaustion must be false: this package's terminal branch is
+	// dead-letter-then-Ack, never a bare Term (ENT-1492 — a Term does not
+	// settle the message and leaves no record of it).
+	Backoff backoff.Policy
+
+	// FloorAge arms the circuit breaker: once the durable's ack floor has
+	// been stationary this long and the message being settled is the one
+	// pinning it, Settle dead-letters that message immediately, whatever its
+	// attempt count. Zero uses DefaultFloorAge; negative ([DisableFloorAge])
+	// turns the breaker off.
+	FloorAge time.Duration
+	// FloorPoll is how often [Start] reads the durable's ack floor from the
+	// server. Zero derives FloorAge/10, clamped to [1s, 30s]. Must be shorter
+	// than FloorAge — the breaker cannot resolve a stall it never samples.
+	FloorPoll time.Duration
+	// MinDeliveries is how many deliveries a message must have had before the
+	// breaker may dead-letter it. Zero uses DefaultMinDeliveries; 1 lets the
+	// breaker fire on a message's very first failure.
+	MinDeliveries int
+
+	// DLQSubject is where the raw message and its headers are republished
+	// before the original is Acked. Required: without a capture subject there
+	// is no non-lossy way to give up on a message, and this package never
+	// drops one.
+	DLQSubject string
+	// Publisher performs that republish — the same jetstream.JetStream handle
+	// the service already publishes with. Required.
+	Publisher natsmsg.DLQPublisher
+
+	// OnSettle observes every settlement, for the caller's metrics. Domain
+	// metrics stay with the caller, as everywhere else in this module; the
+	// Settlement carries what a counter needs (outcome, cause, floor age).
+	OnSettle func(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement)
+
+	// Name prefixes the Retry's own log lines and Logger receives them. Both
+	// are optional: [Start] fills them from Config.Name and Config.Logger when
+	// unset, so an adopter configures them in one place.
+	Name   string
+	Logger *slog.Logger
+}
+
+// Retry is the single retry mechanism a jsconsumer-hosted handler uses to
+// settle a failed delivery. It owns the redelivery ladder, the floor-age
+// circuit breaker, and the dead-letter capture the two terminate into.
+//
+// # Why the library owns this, and owns it alone
+//
+// A JetStream consumer has two redelivery schedulers: the server-side
+// jetstream.ConsumerConfig.BackOff ladder, and the client's own
+// NakWithDelay. Setting both does not pick one — the server stretches each
+// NAK delay by the BackOff increments, so redeliveries land on neither
+// schedule and the configured ladder becomes dead config. That is what
+// happened on entire-search's search-indexer-refs: its consumer advertised a
+// 5m/10m/30m/1h/4h/12h ladder while ENT-1535's forensics measured redelivery
+// at *failure-log time + the handler's own NakWithDelay*, to ±6ms — a real
+// envelope of 34h22m against a documented 17h45m, and nothing in the system
+// said so.
+//
+// So Config.BackOff and Config.Retry are mutually exclusive (a Start error,
+// not a warning), and adopting a Retry actively clears any ladder already on
+// the durable. Whichever mechanism is configured is the only one running.
+//
+// # What the breaker measures
+//
+// Floor-stationary age, not message stream-age. The two diverge badly under
+// backlog: the same forensics measured 35 minutes of receipt→first-delivery
+// lag on a healthy message, which a stream-age trigger would read as a stall.
+// The ack floor only stops advancing when a message genuinely will not
+// settle, which is the condition worth breaking on.
+//
+// A Retry belongs to exactly one durable consumer; give each consumer its
+// own.
+//
+// # Worst-case pin
+//
+// The breaker acts on a delivery, so the floor can stay pinned for up to
+// FloorAge + the largest ladder rung + AckWait. Construction rejects a rung
+// longer than FloorAge, which bounds it at 2×FloorAge + AckWait; pick rungs
+// well under FloorAge to leave headroom. The defaults with a flat 5-minute
+// rung and a 30-second AckWait bound it at 20m30s.
+//
+// # Wiring
+//
+// The first adopter, entire-search's search-indexer-refs on repo_refs_v1,
+// wires it like this — a flat ladder, so the whole envelope is one number:
+//
+//	retry, err := jsconsumer.NewRetry(jsconsumer.RetryConfig{
+//		Backoff:    backoff.Policy{NakDelay: 5 * time.Minute, MaxDeliver: 5},
+//		DLQSubject: "repo.refs.dlq",   // captured into repo_refs_dlq_v1
+//		Publisher:  js,                // the handle the service already publishes with
+//		OnSettle:   metrics.RefEventSettled,
+//	})
+//	if err != nil {
+//		return err
+//	}
+//	cfg := jsconsumer.Config{
+//		Stream: "repo_refs_v1", Durable: "search-indexer-refs",
+//		Name: "search-indexer-refs", AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 5,
+//		Retry: retry, // and NOT Config.BackOff — Start rejects both
+//	}
+//
+//	handle := func(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, ev RefEvent) {
+//		switch err := index(ctx, ev); {
+//		case err == nil:
+//			_ = msg.Ack()
+//		case errors.Is(err, errUnprocessable):
+//			_, _ = retry.DeadLetter(ctx, msg, err.Error()) // no redelivery can fix it
+//		default:
+//			_, _ = retry.Settle(ctx, msg, err.Error()) // ladder, or breaker, or exhaustion
+//		}
+//	}
+//
+// That configuration bounds a pinned ack floor at 15m + 5m + 30s = 20m30s,
+// inside the 30-minute SLA the ack-floor monitor is written against.
+type Retry struct {
+	cfg RetryConfig
+
+	mu     sync.Mutex
+	cons   jetstream.Consumer
+	name   string
+	logger *slog.Logger
+	// clock reads the current time; a package-internal seam so tests can
+	// drive the stationary clock without sleeping.
+	clock func() time.Time
+
+	haveFloor   bool
+	floor       uint64
+	floorSince  time.Time
+	stallLogged bool
+	gapLogged   bool
+}
+
+// NewRetry validates cfg, applies its defaults, and returns the mechanism.
+// The validation is the point: every rejection here is a configuration that
+// would otherwise run, look configured, and quietly not do what it says.
+func NewRetry(cfg RetryConfig) (*Retry, error) {
+	if cfg.Publisher == nil {
+		return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Publisher is required: dead-letter capture is the only terminal branch, so there is no configuration in which a message may be dropped")
+	}
+	if cfg.DLQSubject == "" {
+		return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.DLQSubject is required: see Publisher")
+	}
+	if cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver <= 0 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.MaxDeliver must be positive, got %d: a non-positive value means unlimited redeliveries to backoff.Policy, so the dead-letter branch would never run", cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver)
+	}
+	if cfg.Backoff.TermOnExhaustion {
+		return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.TermOnExhaustion must be false: this package dead-letters and Acks on exhaustion, and a bare Term neither settles the message nor leaves a record of it (ENT-1492)")
+	}
+	if cfg.Backoff.NakDelay <= 0 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.NakDelay must be positive, got %s: a zero delay redelivers immediately and burns MaxDeliver in a hot loop", cfg.Backoff.NakDelay)
+	}
+	if cfg.Backoff.Factor > 1 && cfg.Backoff.MaxDelay <= 0 {
+		return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.MaxDelay is required with a growing Factor: an uncapped rung cannot be checked against FloorAge")
+	}
+	if cfg.MinDeliveries < 0 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.MinDeliveries must not be negative, got %d", cfg.MinDeliveries)
+	}
+	if cfg.MinDeliveries == 0 {
+		cfg.MinDeliveries = DefaultMinDeliveries
+	}
+	if cfg.MinDeliveries > cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.MinDeliveries (%d) exceeds Backoff.MaxDeliver (%d): the breaker could never fire before the ladder exhausted", cfg.MinDeliveries, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver)
+	}
+	if cfg.FloorAge == 0 {
+		cfg.FloorAge = DefaultFloorAge
+	}
+	if cfg.FloorPoll < 0 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.FloorPoll must not be negative, got %s", cfg.FloorPoll)
+	}
+	r := &Retry{cfg: cfg, clock: time.Now}
+	if r.breakerEnabled() {
+		// The breaker only ever fires on a delivery, so a rung longer than
+		// the threshold means the floor stays pinned for that rung after the
+		// breaker arms — the exact "configured ladder is not the real
+		// envelope" failure this type exists to prevent, just one level up.
+		if rung := cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver); rung > cfg.FloorAge {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff's largest rung (%s) exceeds FloorAge (%s): the breaker acts on a delivery, so the floor would stay pinned for up to FloorAge+%s — shorten the ladder or raise FloorAge", rung, cfg.FloorAge, rung)
+		}
+		if p := r.pollInterval(); p >= cfg.FloorAge {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.FloorPoll (%s) must be shorter than FloorAge (%s): the breaker cannot resolve a stall it never samples", p, cfg.FloorAge)
+		}
+	}
+	return r, nil
+}
+
+// MaxDeliver reports the delivery cap this mechanism is built for; [Config]
+// cross-checks it against the consumer's own.
+func (r *Retry) MaxDeliver() int { return r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver }
+
+// breakerEnabled reports whether the floor-age circuit breaker is armed.
+func (r *Retry) breakerEnabled() bool { return r.cfg.FloorAge > 0 }
+
+// pollInterval is the effective floor-poll cadence: FloorPoll, or FloorAge/10
+// clamped to [minFloorPoll, maxFloorPoll].
+func (r *Retry) pollInterval() time.Duration {
+	if r.cfg.FloorPoll > 0 {
+		return r.cfg.FloorPoll
+	}
+	return max(minFloorPoll, min(r.cfg.FloorAge/10, maxFloorPoll))
+}
+
+// attach binds the live consumer (and the host's log identity, when the
+// RetryConfig left them unset) so the poll loop can read the ack floor.
+// Called by [Start] on every attempt, including [Run]'s recreates.
+func (r *Retry) attach(cons jetstream.Consumer, name string, logger *slog.Logger) {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	defer r.mu.Unlock()
+	r.cons = cons
+	r.name = cfgFirst(r.cfg.Name, name)
+	if r.cfg.Logger != nil {
+		r.logger = r.cfg.Logger
+	} else {
+		r.logger = logger
+	}
+}
+
+func cfgFirst(a, b string) string {
+	if a != "" {
+		return a
+	}
+	return b
+}
+
+func (r *Retry) log() (*slog.Logger, string) {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	defer r.mu.Unlock()
+	logger, name := r.logger, r.name
+	if logger == nil {
+		if r.cfg.Logger != nil {
+			logger = r.cfg.Logger
+		} else {
+			logger = slog.Default()
+		}
+	}
+	if name == "" {
+		name = cfgFirst(r.cfg.Name, "jsconsumer")
+	}
+	return logger, name
+}
+
+// FloorStationaryFor reports the durable's last observed ack floor (a stream
+// sequence), how long it has been stationary there, and whether any
+// observation exists yet. Exposed so an adopter can publish the stall as a
+// gauge — the signal the ack-floor monitor pages on — from inside the process
+// rather than by polling consumer info a second time.
+//
+// The age is measured from the first observation of that floor value, so a
+// freshly started process under-reports an already-old stall rather than
+// over-reporting it: the breaker can be late, never early.
+func (r *Retry) FloorStationaryFor() (floor uint64, age time.Duration, ok bool) {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	defer r.mu.Unlock()
+	if !r.haveFloor {
+		return 0, 0, false
+	}
+	return r.floor, r.clock().Sub(r.floorSince), true
+}
+
+// observeFloor records one ack-floor reading, restarting the stationary clock
+// when the floor has moved.
+func (r *Retry) observeFloor(floor uint64, at time.Time) {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	defer r.mu.Unlock()
+	if r.haveFloor && r.floor == floor {
+		return
+	}
+	r.haveFloor = true
+	r.floor = floor
+	r.floorSince = at
+	r.stallLogged = false
+	r.gapLogged = false
+}
+
+// pollFloor reads the ack floor until ctx is cancelled or stop is closed
+// (the consume loop winding down). It samples once immediately so a
+// long-lived stall is observed at Start rather than one interval later.
+func (r *Retry) pollFloor(ctx context.Context, stop <-chan struct{}) {
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
+	defer cancel()
+	// Cancel on the consume loop closing too, so an in-flight consumer-info
+	// request cannot hold Runner.Stop open for floorPollTimeout. The watcher
+	// exits with ctx via the deferred cancel.
+	go func() {
+		select {
+		case <-stop:
+			cancel()
+		case <-ctx.Done():
+		}
+	}()
+
+	r.pollOnce(ctx)
+	t := time.NewTicker(r.pollInterval())
+	defer t.Stop()
+	for {
+		select {
+		case <-ctx.Done():
+			return
+		case <-t.C:
+			r.pollOnce(ctx)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func (r *Retry) pollOnce(ctx context.Context) {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	cons := r.cons
+	r.mu.Unlock()
+	if cons == nil {
+		return
+	}
+	infoCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, floorPollTimeout)
+	defer cancel()
+	info, err := cons.Info(infoCtx)
+	if err != nil {
+		if ctx.Err() != nil {
+			return // shutting down; a failed read here is the wind-down, not a fault
+		}
+		logger, name := r.log()
+		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor poll failed", slog.Any("error", err))
+		return
+	}
+	r.observeFloor(info.AckFloor.Stream, r.clock())
+
+	// Report a stall the breaker has armed on but not yet cleared — once per
+	// stationary period. This is the case ENT-1535 had no in-process signal
+	// for, and it stays visible even when no delivery matches the blocker
+	// (a filtered consumer whose floor sits below a gap in the stream), where
+	// the breaker itself would otherwise be a silent no-op.
+	floor, age, ok := r.FloorStationaryFor()
+	if !ok || !r.breakerEnabled() || age < r.cfg.FloorAge {
+		return
+	}
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	first := !r.stallLogged
+	r.stallLogged = true
+	r.mu.Unlock()
+	if !first {
+		return
+	}
+	logger, name := r.log()
+	logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor stationary past FloorAge; breaker armed",
+		slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
+		slog.Duration("stationary_for", age),
+		slog.Uint64("last_delivered", info.Delivered.Stream),
+		slog.Int("num_ack_pending", info.NumAckPending))
+}
+
+// isFloorBlocker reports whether msg is the message pinning a stalled ack
+// floor, and the observed stall. The blocker is the sequence immediately
+// above the floor: the floor is, by definition, the last sequence below which
+// everything is settled, so floor+1 is the one delivery that has to settle
+// before the floor can advance (this is the same identification the incident
+// runbook makes by hand).
+//
+// It deliberately does not generalise to "any sequence above the floor". A
+// message far above a floor pinned by someone else is not the blocker, and
+// dead-lettering it would take a merely-slow event away from a ladder it
+// might still recover on.
+//
+// The exact match assumes the consumer's filter matches densely enough that
+// the blocker really does sit at floor+1 — true where the filter covers the
+// whole stream (repo_refs_v1, where the ENT-1535 blocker sat one sequence
+// above the floor). A narrow filter over a sparse stream can leave a gap
+// there, and then the breaker never identifies a blocker. That failure is
+// safe but silent, so it is logged: see the "no delivery at floor+1" line
+// below and the "breaker armed" line in pollOnce.
+func (r *Retry) isFloorBlocker(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg) (blocker bool, floor uint64, age time.Duration) {
+	if !r.breakerEnabled() {
+		return false, 0, 0
+	}
+	floor, age, ok := r.FloorStationaryFor()
+	if !ok || age < r.cfg.FloorAge {
+		return false, floor, age
+	}
+	meta, err := msg.Metadata()
+	if err != nil || meta == nil {
+		return false, floor, age
+	}
+	if meta.Sequence.Stream == floor+1 {
+		return true, floor, age
+	}
+	r.reportFloorGap(ctx, floor, age, meta.Sequence.Stream)
+	return false, floor, age
+}
+
+// reportFloorGap names, once per stationary period, the first failing
+// delivery seen above a stalled floor that is not floor+1. Either the real
+// blocker is elsewhere (another replica holds it, or it is waiting out a
+// ladder rung) or the consumer's filter leaves a gap at floor+1 and the
+// breaker cannot fire at all. The two look identical from inside the process;
+// printing the sequence the breaker wanted against the one it got is what
+// tells them apart from the logs.
+func (r *Retry) reportFloorGap(ctx context.Context, floor uint64, age time.Duration, seq uint64) {
+	if seq <= floor {
+		return // already settled past; not a candidate blocker at all
+	}
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	first := !r.gapLogged
+	r.gapLogged = true
+	r.mu.Unlock()
+	if !first {
+		return
+	}
+	logger, name := r.log()
+	logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor stalled but no delivery at floor+1; breaker cannot identify the blocker",
+		slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
+		slog.Uint64("want_stream_seq", floor+1),
+		slog.Uint64("got_stream_seq", seq),
+		slog.Duration("stationary_for", age))
+}
+
+// Settle applies the mechanism to a delivery whose handler failed
+// transiently, and is the only disposition call such a handler makes. It
+// picks exactly one of:
+//
+//   - the circuit breaker — this message is pinning an ack floor that has
+//     been stationary past FloorAge, and has already had MinDeliveries
+//     attempts: capture to the DLQ and Ack, whatever the attempt count
+//     (Cause CauseFloorAge);
+//   - exhaustion — this is the final delivery: capture to the DLQ and Ack
+//     (Cause CauseExhausted);
+//   - the ladder — NakWithDelay for redelivery (Outcome OutcomeRetried).
+//
+// reason is recorded on the captured copy's Nats-Dlq-Reason header, prefixed
+// with the cause, so the DLQ says why a message is there and not just that it
+// is.
+//
+// A capture failure is never allowed to become a drop: the original is Nak'd
+// instead and the error returned (settle:dlq_publish_failed), so the message
+// survives, the next delivery retries the capture, and — if the ladder is
+// spent — the ack floor stays pinned and the ack-floor monitor fires, which
+// is ENT-1492's deliberate posture for a degraded DLQ path. An Ack that fails
+// after a successful capture (settle:dlq_ack_failed) leaves the original to
+// redeliver and be captured again; a duplicate in the DLQ beats a lost
+// message.
+//
+// On both error paths the returned Settlement reports OutcomeRetried — the
+// message is still coming back — while keeping the Cause of the terminal
+// branch that could not complete, so the caller's metrics show a DLQ path
+// that is being reached and failing rather than one that is idle.
+func (r *Retry) Settle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
+	delivered := backoff.NumDelivered(msg)
+	blocker, floor, age := r.isFloorBlocker(ctx, msg)
+	tripped := blocker && delivered >= r.cfg.MinDeliveries
+
+	s := Settlement{Delivered: delivered, Floor: floor, FloorAge: age}
+	switch {
+	case tripped:
+		s.Cause = CauseFloorAge
+	case backoff.IsFinalDelivery(msg, r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver):
+		s.Cause = CauseExhausted
+	default:
+		return r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
+	}
+
+	if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, s.Cause, reason); err != nil {
+		// Fall back to the ladder so the message is never lost. Preserve the
+		// cause: the caller's metrics should show that the terminal branch
+		// was reached and could not complete.
+		naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
+		naked.Cause = s.Cause
+		return naked, errors.Join(err, nakErr)
+	}
+	if err := msg.Ack(); err != nil {
+		// The copy is in the DLQ but the original is unsettled: it will
+		// redeliver and be captured again. A duplicate in the DLQ is the
+		// right trade against losing the message or pinning the floor
+		// forever.
+		s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
+		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+		return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
+	logger, name := r.log()
+	logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": dead-lettered",
+		slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
+		slog.String("reason", reason),
+		slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
+		slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor),
+		slog.Duration("floor_stationary_for", s.FloorAge))
+	r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+	return s, nil
+}
+
+// DeadLetter captures msg to the DLQ and Acks it immediately, for a failure
+// the handler knows no redelivery can fix — an unprocessable payload, a
+// reference that will never resolve. It is the non-lossy replacement for a
+// bare Term: same terminal effect on the consumer, but the raw message and
+// its headers survive in the DLQ.
+//
+// As in [Settle], a capture failure Naks rather than dropping, and returns
+// the error.
+func (r *Retry) DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
+	floor, age, _ := r.FloorStationaryFor()
+	s := Settlement{
+		Cause:     CausePermanent,
+		Delivered: backoff.NumDelivered(msg),
+		Floor:     floor,
+		FloorAge:  age,
+	}
+	if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, CausePermanent, reason); err != nil {
+		naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
+		naked.Cause = CausePermanent
+		return naked, errors.Join(err, nakErr)
+	}
+	if err := msg.Ack(); err != nil {
+		s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
+		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+		return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
+	r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+	return s, nil
+}
+
+// capture republishes the raw message and headers to the DLQ subject, tagging
+// the reason with its cause.
+func (r *Retry) capture(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, cause Cause, reason string) error {
+	if err := natsmsg.DeadLetter(ctx, r.cfg.Publisher, r.cfg.DLQSubject, msg, string(cause)+": "+reason); err != nil {
+		logger, name := r.log()
+		logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": settle:dlq_publish_failed",
+			slog.Any("error", err),
+			slog.String("dlq_subject", r.cfg.DLQSubject),
+			slog.String("cause", string(cause)))
+		return fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_publish_failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// nak schedules the next delivery on the ladder and completes s.
+func (r *Retry) nak(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) (Settlement, error) {
+	s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
+	s.Delay = r.cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(s.Delivered)
+	err := msg.NakWithDelay(s.Delay)
+	r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
+	if err != nil {
+		return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:nak_failed: %w", err)
+	}
+	return s, nil
+}
+
+func (r *Retry) observe(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) {
+	if r.cfg.OnSettle != nil {
+		r.cfg.OnSettle(ctx, msg, s)
+	}
+}

+// TestSettleReportsAnUnidentifiableBlocker: the breaker identifies the
+// blocker as the sequence immediately above the floor, which assumes the
+// consumer's filter is dense enough for that message to exist. When it isn't
+// — a narrow filter over a sparse stream — the breaker cannot fire, and that
+// must not be silent: the log names the sequence it wanted against the one it
+// saw, which is how a staging exercise tells "wrong predicate" apart from
+// "the real blocker is on another replica".
+func TestSettleReportsAnUnidentifiableBlocker(t *testing.T) {
+	logs := &logCapture{}
+	r, _ := newTestRetry(t, func(c *RetryConfig) { c.Logger = slog.New(logs) })
+	armFloor(r, 2774436, 20*time.Minute)
+
+	for range 3 { // logged once per stationary period, not once per delivery
+		if _, err := r.Settle(t.Context(), deliveredMsg(2774600, 3), "transient"); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("Settle: %v", err)
+		}

+	}

+// logCapture is a thread-safe slog.Handler that counts messages, so a test
+// can assert a log line is emitted once per stationary period rather than
+// once per delivery.
+type logCapture struct {
+	mu   sync.Mutex
+	msgs []string
+}
+
+func (h *logCapture) Enabled(context.Context, slog.Level) bool { return true }
+
+func (h *logCapture) Handle(_ context.Context, r slog.Record) error {
+	h.mu.Lock()
+	h.msgs = append(h.msgs, r.Message)
+	h.mu.Unlock()
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (h *logCapture) WithAttrs([]slog.Attr) slog.Handler { return h }
+func (h *logCapture) WithGroup(string) slog.Handler      { return h }
+
+func (h *logCapture) snapshot() []string {
+	h.mu.Lock()
+	defer h.mu.Unlock()
+	return slices.Clone(h.msgs)
+}
+
+func (h *logCapture) count(msg string) int {
+	n := 0
+	for _, m := range h.snapshot() {
+		if m == msg {
+			n++
+		}
+	}
+	return n
+}

+// TestObserveFloorRestartsTheClockWhenTheFloorMoves: the trigger is

+func TestConfigRejectsBothRetryMechanisms(t *testing.T) {
+	r, _ := newTestRetry(t, nil)
+	cfg := Config{
+		Stream:     "repo_refs_v1",
+		Durable:    "search-indexer-refs",
+		Name:       "search-indexer-refs",
+		MaxDeliver: 5,
+		BackOff:    []time.Duration{5 * time.Minute, 10 * time.Minute},
+		Retry:      r,
+	}
+	_, err := Start(t.Context(), nil, cfg, func(jetstream.Msg) {})
+	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "BackOff or Retry") {
+		t.Fatalf("Start(BackOff+Retry) err = %v, want a mutual-exclusion error", err)
+	}
+}
+
+// TestConfigRejectsRetryMaxDeliverMismatch: with Retry the terminal branch is
+// the DLQ capture, so a policy that disagrees with the broker's cap is a lost
+// message rather than a late one.
+func TestConfigRejectsRetryMaxDeliverMismatch(t *testing.T) {
+	r, _ := newTestRetry(t, nil) // MaxDeliver 5
+	cfg := Config{
+		Stream:     "repo_refs_v1",
+		Durable:    "search-indexer-refs",
+		Name:       "search-indexer-refs",
+		MaxDeliver: 7,
+		Retry:      r,
+	}
+	_, err := Start(t.Context(), nil, cfg, func(jetstream.Msg) {})
+	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "MaxDeliver") {
+		t.Fatalf("Start(mismatched MaxDeliver) err = %v, want a MaxDeliver mismatch error", err)
+	}
+
+	// The consumer's own default counts as its cap, not the raw zero field.
+	cfg.MaxDeliver = 0
+	if _, err := Start(t.Context(), nil, cfg, func(jetstream.Msg) {}); err == nil ||
+		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "consumer's is 8") {
+		t.Fatalf("Start(default MaxDeliver) err = %v, want it compared against EffectiveMaxDeliver", err)
+	}
+}
+
+// TestConfigRejectsUnworkableBackOff keeps the server-ladder escape hatch
+// honest: the server rejects these too, but naming both fields beats a bare
+// API error at consumer creation.
+func TestConfigRejectsUnworkableBackOff(t *testing.T) {
+	base := Config{Stream: "s_v1", Durable: "d", Name: "c"}
+	tests := []struct {
+		name string
+		cfg  Config
+		want string
+	}{
+		{"non-positive rung", func() Config {
+			c := base
+			c.BackOff = []time.Duration{time.Minute, 0}
+			return c
+		}(), "BackOff[1]"},
+		{"more rungs than redeliveries", func() Config {
+			c := base
+			c.MaxDeliver = 2
+			c.BackOff = []time.Duration{time.Minute, time.Minute, time.Minute}
+			return c
+		}(), "only 2 redeliveries"},
+	}
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			_, err := Start(t.Context(), nil, tt.cfg, func(jetstream.Msg) {})
+			if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tt.want) {
+				t.Fatalf("Start() err = %v, want error containing %q", err, tt.want)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// TestProcessDeadLettersUndecodable: with a Retry configured, an undecodable
+// payload is captured rather than Termed — closing the last
+// drop-without-a-record surface in the scaffold. Without one, Process keeps
+// its original Term (see TestProcessTermsUndecodable).
+func TestProcessDeadLettersUndecodable(t *testing.T) {
+	r, pub := newTestRetry(t, nil)
+	cfg := testCfg
+	cfg.Retry = r
+	msg := deliveredMsg(2774437, 1)
+	msg.DataVal = []byte("garbage")
+
+	Process(t.Context(), msg, cfg,
+		func([]byte) (string, error) { return "", errors.New("bad payload") },
+		func(context.Context, trace.Span, jetstream.Msg, string) { t.Error("handle called on a decode error") },
+		nil)
+
+	if msg.Termed {
+		t.Error("undecodable payload Termed with a Retry configured, want dead-lettered")
+	}
+	if !msg.Acked {
+		t.Error("undecodable payload not Acked after capture")
+	}
+	captured := pub.captured()
+	if len(captured) != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("captured %d messages, want 1", len(captured))
+	}
+	if reason := captured[0].Header.Get(natsmsg.DLQReasonHeader); !strings.Contains(reason, "undecodable") {
+		t.Errorf("DLQ reason = %q, want it to say the payload was undecodable", reason)
+	}
+	if string(captured[0].Data) != "garbage" {
+		t.Errorf("DLQ payload = %q, want the raw undecodable bytes", captured[0].Data)
+	}
+}
+
+// TestStartClearsStaleServerBackOff is the ENT-1535 migration hazard, driven
+// end to end: search-indexer-refs already carries a six-rung server ladder on
+// its durable. Adopting a Retry has to WIPE it, or the server keeps stretching
+// the library's NakWithDelay by those increments and the real envelope is
+// again neither ladder.
+func TestStartClearsStaleServerBackOff(t *testing.T) {
+	nc, js := runTestEnv(t)
+	if _, err := js.CreateStream(t.Context(), jetstream.StreamConfig{
+		Name: "repo_refs_v1", Subjects: []string{"repo.refs.>"},
+	}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("create stream: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	// The durable as it exists in prod today.
+	stale := []time.Duration{5 * time.Minute, 10 * time.Minute, 30 * time.Minute, time.Hour}
+	if _, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(t.Context(), "repo_refs_v1", jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
+		Durable:    "search_indexer_refs",
+		AckPolicy:  jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
+		AckWait:    5 * time.Minute,
+		MaxDeliver: 5,
+		BackOff:    stale,
+	}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("create consumer with a server ladder: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	r, _ := newTestRetry(t, nil)
+	run, err := Start(t.Context(), nc, Config{
+		Stream:     "repo_refs_v1",
+		Durable:    "search_indexer_refs",
+		Name:       "search-indexer-refs",
+		AckWait:    5 * time.Minute,
+		MaxDeliver: 5,
+		Retry:      r,
+	}, func(jetstream.Msg) {})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("Start: %v", err)
+	}
+	defer run.Stop()
+
+	cons, err := js.Consumer(t.Context(), "repo_refs_v1", "search_indexer_refs")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("consumer: %v", err)
+	}
+	info, err := cons.Info(t.Context())
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("consumer info: %v", err)
+	}
+	if len(info.Config.BackOff) != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("server BackOff = %v, want it cleared so the library owns redelivery alone", info.Config.BackOff)
+	}
+}
+
+// TestStartObservesTheAckFloor drives the poll loop against a live consumer:
+// the breaker's input is the durable's real ack floor, and Stop joins the
+// poll so the connection it reads through is safe to drain afterwards.
+func TestStartObservesTheAckFloor(t *testing.T) {
+	nc, js := runTestEnv(t)
+	if _, err := js.CreateStream(t.Context(), jetstream.StreamConfig{
+		Name: "repo_refs_v1", Subjects: []string{"repo.refs.>"},
+	}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("create stream: %v", err)
+	}
+	for range 3 {
+		if _, err := js.Publish(t.Context(), "repo.refs.update", []byte("ref")); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("publish: %v", err)
+		}
+	}
+
+	r, _ := newTestRetry(t, func(c *RetryConfig) {
+		c.FloorAge = time.Minute
+		c.FloorPoll = 10 * time.Millisecond
+		c.Backoff.NakDelay = time.Second
+	})
+	acked := make(chan struct{}, 3)
+	run, err := Start(t.Context(), nc, Config{
+		Stream:     "repo_refs_v1",
+		Durable:    "search_indexer_refs",
+		Name:       "search-indexer-refs",
+		MaxDeliver: 5,
+		Retry:      r,
+	}, func(m jetstream.Msg) {
+		if err := m.Ack(); err != nil {
+			t.Errorf("ack: %v", err)
+		}
+		acked <- struct{}{}
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("Start: %v", err)
+	}
+	for range 3 {
+		select {
+		case <-acked:
+		case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
+			t.Fatal("messages did not reach the handler")
+		}
+	}
+
+	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
+	for {
+		floor, _, ok := r.FloorStationaryFor()
+		if ok && floor == 3 {
+			break
+		}
+		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
+			t.Fatalf("ack floor never observed at 3 (got %d, observed=%v)", floor, ok)
+		}
+		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
+	}
+
+	// Stop joins the poll loop, so nothing is still reading through nc.
+	done := make(chan struct{})
+	go func() { run.Stop(); close(done) }()
+	select {
+	case <-done:
+	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
+		t.Fatal("Stop did not join the ack-floor poll")
+	}
+	if r.pollInterval() != 10*time.Millisecond {
+		t.Errorf("pollInterval = %s, want the configured 10ms", r.pollInterval())
+	}
+}
+
+// TestStartWithoutBreakerRunsNoPoll: a Retry with the breaker disabled is
+// still the one retry mechanism, but it costs no consumer-info traffic and
+// Stop has no poll to join.
+func TestStartWithoutBreakerRunsNoPoll(t *testing.T) {
+	nc, js := runTestEnv(t)
+	if _, err := js.CreateStream(t.Context(), jetstream.StreamConfig{
+		Name: "repo_refs_v1", Subjects: []string{"repo.refs.>"},
+	}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("create stream: %v", err)
+	}
+	r, _ := newTestRetry(t, func(c *RetryConfig) { c.FloorAge = DisableFloorAge })
+	run, err := Start(t.Context(), nc, Config{
+		Stream:     "repo_refs_v1",
+		Durable:    "no_breaker",
+		Name:       "no-breaker",
+		MaxDeliver: 5,
+		Retry:      r,
+	}, func(jetstream.Msg) {})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("Start: %v", err)
+	}
+	if run.pollDone != nil {
+		t.Error("Start ran an ack-floor poll with the breaker disabled")
+	}
+	run.Stop()
+	if _, _, ok := r.FloorStationaryFor(); ok {
+		t.Error("floor observed with the breaker disabled")
+	}
+}

   520	//
   521	// reason is recorded on the captured copy's Nats-Dlq-Reason header, prefixed

    14	//
    15	// # Zero-value and unlimited semantics
    16	//

    18	// (0 or [UnlimitedMaxDeliver]) means unlimited redeliveries, so no delivery is
    19	// ever final and NakOrTerm always Naks. Note this reads zero differently from

    22	// an unset consumer MaxDeliver becomes the real default here instead of

    24	// first delivery — base NakDelay, never final — the safe default being another
    25	// retry, not a Term.

    28	// mirror-pipeline's fanoutengine: on the final delivery a Nak is dropped
    29	// silently by the broker (MaxDeliver reached), and on a WorkQueue stream the
    30	// un-acked message then orphans — pinning the oldest-pending-age gauge — until
    31	// StreamMaxAge finally expires it. Terming instead removes it cleanly. Streams

    43	
    44	import (
    45		"fmt"
    46		"math"
    47		"time"
    48	
    49		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
    50	)
    51	
    52	// UnlimitedMaxDeliver is the explicit Policy.MaxDeliver value for unlimited
    53	// redeliveries (matching jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver, where a
    54	// non-positive value disables the delivery cap). The zero value means the same
    55	// thing; the named constant lets a caller say so on purpose.
    56	const UnlimitedMaxDeliver = -1
    57	
    58	// Outcome is the disposition NakOrTerm chose, for the caller's metrics and
    59	// logs.
    60	type Outcome string
    61	
    62	const (
    63		OutcomeNak  Outcome = "nak"
    64		OutcomeTerm Outcome = "term"

    66	
    67	// Policy is the redelivery envelope a consumer applies to transient
    68	// failures. MaxDeliver must match the consumer's on-server MaxDeliver — the
    69	// policy detects the final delivery by comparing against it.

    71		// NakDelay is the base delay before redelivery, and with a zero Factor
    72		// the whole envelope: flat suits failures expected to clear on their own
    73		// timetable, with MaxDeliver bounding the total.
    74		NakDelay time.Duration
    75		// Factor is the optional multiplicative growth per prior delivery: the
    76		// Nth delivery naks with NakDelay × Factor^(N-1), capped at MaxDelay.
    77		// Values ≤ 1 (including the zero value) keep the flat envelope. Growing
    78		// envelopes suit failures that get cheaper to wait out than to retry —
    79		// a downstream in a crash loop, a rate limit — where hammering on the
    80		// flat cadence spends MaxDeliver too fast.
    81		Factor float64
    82		// MaxDelay caps the grown delay; it does nothing for a flat policy.
    83		// Zero with a growing Factor leaves growth bounded only by MaxDeliver
    84		// ending the redeliveries (the computed delay still saturates rather
    85		// than overflowing).
    86		MaxDelay time.Duration

    88		// (jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver). Non-positive (0 or
    89		// UnlimitedMaxDeliver) means unlimited redeliveries — matching the
    90		// jetstream field's semantics — so no delivery is ever final and NakOrTerm
    91		// always Naks.
    92		MaxDeliver int

    94		// work-queue message is removed cleanly rather than orphaning un-acked
    95		// (COR-762). Callers with a DLQ capture before calling NakOrTerm.

   101	// final delivery with TermOnExhaustion set — Term. Without TermOnExhaustion the

   103	// stream's retention decides the message's fate.

   106	// metrics and logs. A disposition error is worth a log line but nothing more:

   108	// work-queue stream means the message lingers exactly as it would have without
   109	// the policy.
   110	func (p Policy) NakOrTerm(msg jetstream.Msg) (Outcome, error) {

   127	// metadata is unavailable — reads as the first delivery. Exposed so a caller
   128	// can log or meter the delay it is about to apply.
   129	func (p Policy) DelayFor(numDelivered int) time.Duration {
   130		if p.Factor <= 1 || numDelivered <= 1 {
   131			return p.NakDelay
   132		}

   135			return p.MaxDelay

   151		}
   152		return 0
   153	}

   162	// retry, not a Term.

    55	// thing; the named constant lets a caller say so on purpose.
    56	const UnlimitedMaxDeliver = -1
    57	
    58	// Outcome is the disposition NakOrTerm chose, for the caller's metrics and
    59	// logs.
    60	type Outcome string
    61	
    62	const (
    63		OutcomeNak  Outcome = "nak"
    64		OutcomeTerm Outcome = "term"
    65	)
    66	
    67	// Policy is the redelivery envelope a consumer applies to transient
    68	// failures. MaxDeliver must match the consumer's on-server MaxDeliver — the
    69	// policy detects the final delivery by comparing against it.

    71		// NakDelay is the base delay before redelivery, and with a zero Factor
    72		// the whole envelope: flat suits failures expected to clear on their own
    73		// timetable, with MaxDeliver bounding the total.
    74		NakDelay time.Duration
    75		// Factor is the optional multiplicative growth per prior delivery: the
    76		// Nth delivery naks with NakDelay × Factor^(N-1), capped at MaxDelay.
    77		// Values ≤ 1 (including the zero value) keep the flat envelope. Growing
    78		// envelopes suit failures that get cheaper to wait out than to retry —
    79		// a downstream in a crash loop, a rate limit — where hammering on the
    80		// flat cadence spends MaxDeliver too fast.
    81		Factor float64
    82		// MaxDelay caps the grown delay; it does nothing for a flat policy.

    84		// ending the redeliveries (the computed delay still saturates rather
    85		// than overflowing).

    97	}

    99	// NakOrTerm applies the policy to a transiently-failed [jetstream.Msg]
   100	// delivery: NakWithDelay (see [Policy.DelayFor]) for redelivery, or — on the
   101	// final delivery with TermOnExhaustion set — Term. Without TermOnExhaustion the

   103	// stream's retention decides the message's fate.

   106	// metrics and logs. A disposition error is worth a log line but nothing more:
   107	// a failed Nak redelivers via AckWait expiry anyway, and a failed Term on a
   108	// work-queue stream means the message lingers exactly as it would have without
   109	// the policy.

   112			if err := msg.Term(); err != nil {
   113				return OutcomeTerm, fmt.Errorf("term on final delivery: %w", err)

   121	}

   123	// DelayFor reports the redelivery delay the policy applies after delivery
   124	// number numDelivered (1 on first delivery): NakDelay for a flat policy,
   125	// NakDelay × Factor^(numDelivered-1) capped at MaxDelay for a growing one.

   127	// metadata is unavailable — reads as the first delivery. Exposed so a caller
   128	// can log or meter the delay it is about to apply.
   129	func (p Policy) DelayFor(numDelivered int) time.Duration {

   131			return p.NakDelay
   132		}

   135			return p.MaxDelay

   139			// negative (a negative NakWithDelay would redeliver immediately).
   140			return math.MaxInt64
   141		}

   145	// NumDelivered reports the JetStream delivery count of a [jetstream.Msg]
   146	// (1 on first delivery), or 0 if metadata is unavailable (e.g. a synthetic test
   147	// message).

   149		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
   150			return int(meta.NumDelivered)
   151		}
   152		return 0
   153	}
   154	
   155	// IsFinalDelivery reports whether this is the last delivery before JetStream
   156	// stops redelivering (NumDelivered has reached MaxDeliver), so a transient
   157	// failure here is terminal rather than another Nak-and-retry. A non-positive
   158	// maxDeliver means unlimited redeliveries (the jetstream.ConsumerConfig

   166		}
   167		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
   168			return meta.NumDelivered >= uint64(maxDeliver)
   169		}
   170		return false
   171	}

1	// Package jsconsumer is the durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold shared by
     2	// Entire's decode-and-dispatch consumers. Each of those used to hand-roll the
     3	// same lifecycle: jetstream.New → CreateOrUpdateConsumer (durable, explicit
     4	// ack, bounded ack-wait, bounded MaxDeliver, filter subject) → Consume → stop
     5	// on context cancel; and the same per-message prologue: open a consumer span
     6	// (re-parented across the NATS hop), decode the payload, and Term on a decode
     7	// error.
     8	//
     9	// This package owns exactly that scaffold and nothing else. Each consumer
    10	// keeps its OWN event type, business dispatch, metrics, and log lines — Start
    11	// takes the consumer's message callback, and Process invokes the consumer's
    12	// handle with the decoded event and the live span. The handler owns the
    13	// message's terminal disposition (Ack/Nak/Term); Process never touches a
    14	// message that decoded.
    15	//
    16	// The one exception to "disposition stays with the handler" is [Retry], the
    17	// scaffold's optional single retry mechanism: the redelivery ladder, the
    18	// floor-age circuit breaker, and the dead-letter capture they terminate into
    19	// (ENT-1535). A handler that configures one calls [Retry.Settle] instead of
    20	// picking a disposition itself, and the package guarantees the consumer has
    21	// exactly one redelivery scheduler — a server-side Config.BackOff and a Retry
    22	// are mutually exclusive, because together neither is the real envelope.
    23	//
    24	// Lifted from entire-api's internal/jsconsumer (COR-929), folding in the
    25	// module's shutdown classification ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr] gates the
    26	// consume-error log so a drain during rollout isn't reported as a fault,
    27	// COR-923) and an optional [natsmsg.KeepInProgress] heartbeat for consumers
    28	// whose handlers legitimately outrun AckWait.
    29	package jsconsumer
    30	
    31	import (
    32		"context"
    33		"errors"
    34		"fmt"
    35		"log/slog"
    36		"sync"
    37		"time"
    38	
    39		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
    40		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
    41		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
    42		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes"
    43		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
    44	
    45		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts"
    46		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg"
    47	)
    48	
    49	const (
    50		// DefaultAckWait is how long JetStream waits for an ack before redelivery
    51		// when Config.AckWait is zero — comfortably longer than an RPC round-trip
    52		// plus a DB upsert, short enough that a stuck message redelivers promptly.
    53		DefaultAckWait = 30 * time.Second
    54		// DefaultMaxDeliver caps redelivery before JetStream stops redelivering a
    55		// message when Config.MaxDeliver is zero.
    56		DefaultMaxDeliver = 8
    57	)
    58	
    59	// Config describes the durable consumer to create and how to trace/log it. The
    60	// filter is given as either FilterSubject (single) or FilterSubjects (multi),
    61	// mirroring jetstream.ConsumerConfig, so a migrated consumer preserves its
    62	// existing on-server filter form exactly.
    63	type Config struct {
    64		Stream         string        // JetStream stream to bind (must already exist)
    65		Durable        string        // durable consumer name, stable across restarts
    66		FilterSubject  string        // set this OR FilterSubjects
    67		FilterSubjects []string      // set this OR FilterSubject
    68		AckWait        time.Duration // 0 → DefaultAckWait (see EffectiveAckWait)
    69		MaxDeliver     int           // 0 → DefaultMaxDeliver (see EffectiveMaxDeliver)
    70		SpanName       string        // per-message consumer span name (e.g. "repolifecycle.consume")
    71		Name           string        // short consumer name, used as the log prefix
    72	
    73		// InactiveThreshold mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.InactiveThreshold:
    74		// how long the durable may go without an active subscription before the
    75		// server deletes it; zero means never (the JetStream default for
    76		// durables). Consumers on interest-retention streams set this so a
    77		// decommissioned durable stops pinning every message it would have
    78		// received, instead of holding them until the stream's MaxAge.
    79		InactiveThreshold time.Duration
    80	
    81		// MaxAckPending mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxAckPending: the
    82		// server-side cap on deliveries outstanding un-acked across ALL replicas
    83		// sharing the durable; zero uses the server default (1000). Distinct
    84		// from MaxMessages below, which caps only this process's client-side
    85		// buffer.
    86		MaxAckPending int
    87	
    88		// BackOff mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.BackOff: the SERVER-side
    89		// redelivery ladder, one delay per redelivery, applied in place of
    90		// AckWait. It is mutually exclusive with Retry — setting both is a Start
    91		// error, not a warning — because the two do not compose: the server
    92		// stretches a handler's NakWithDelay by the BackOff increments, so
    93		// redeliveries land on neither schedule and the configured ladder becomes
    94		// dead config that reads as authoritative. That is ENT-1535's root
    95		// finding, and [Retry] exists to make the combination unrepresentable.
    96		//
    97		// Leave it nil and use Retry for new consumers. It is here so a consumer
    98		// that genuinely wants the server ladder can say so, and so the choice is
    99		// visible in one place.
   100		BackOff []time.Duration
   101	
   102		// Retry is the library-owned retry mechanism: one redelivery ladder, the
   103		// floor-age circuit breaker, and dead-letter capture. When set, [Start]
   104		// runs an ack-floor poll for the breaker, clears any server-side BackOff
   105		// left on the durable, and [Process] dead-letters an undecodable payload
   106		// instead of Terming it. Its MaxDeliver must equal EffectiveMaxDeliver().
   107		//
   108		// Handlers reach it through the closure they build, and call
   109		// [Retry.Settle] as their one disposition for a failed delivery. Nil
   110		// leaves disposition entirely to the handler, as before.
   111		Retry *Retry
   112	
   113		// Tracer opens the per-message consumer span; nil uses the global OTel
   114		// tracer provider.
   115		Tracer trace.Tracer
   116		// Logger receives the scaffold's own log lines (decode-term warnings,
   117		// consume errors); nil uses slog.Default.
   118		Logger *slog.Logger
   119	
   120		// KeepInProgress runs a natsmsg.KeepInProgress heartbeat while handle
   121		// executes, for handlers that legitimately outrun AckWait. The extension
   122		// is capped, so a wedged handler still redelivers — see
   123		// natsmsg.KeepInProgress. The heartbeat stops when handle returns; a tick
   124		// racing the handler's own terminal Ack/Nak/Term is a client-side no-op
   125		// (nats.go marks the message disposed locally) that halts the heartbeat.
   126		//
   127		// Setting this forces the prefetch to one message (see MaxMessages): the
   128		// heartbeat extends only the delivery the handler holds, so anything
   129		// buffered behind a long handler would exhaust its AckWait unextended.
   130		KeepInProgress bool
   131	
   132		// MaxMessages caps how many deliveries the consume loop buffers
   133		// client-side (jetstream.PullMaxMessages); 0 uses the nats.go default
   134		// (500). AckWait runs from server delivery into that buffer, not from
   135		// callback dispatch, and callbacks run serially — so a consumer whose
   136		// handler can approach AckWait should keep this small or queued
   137		// deliveries expire and redeliver concurrently to other replicas.
   138		// KeepInProgress forces it to 1; setting both to conflicting values is a
   139		// Start error.
   140		MaxMessages int
   141	}
   142	
   143	// EffectiveAckWait is the AckWait actually applied to the JetStream consumer:
   144	// Config.AckWait, or DefaultAckWait when zero. Use it — not the raw field —
   145	// anywhere the real value matters, e.g. wiring a natsmsg.KeepInProgress
   146	// heartbeat by hand (a zero ackWait there is a no-op).
   147	func (c Config) EffectiveAckWait() time.Duration {
   148		if c.AckWait == 0 {
   149			return DefaultAckWait
   150		}
   151		return c.AckWait
   152	}
   153	
   154	// EffectiveMaxDeliver is the MaxDeliver actually applied to the JetStream
   155	// consumer: Config.MaxDeliver, or DefaultMaxDeliver when zero. Use it — not
   156	// the raw field — when building a backoff.Policy for this consumer's
   157	// messages: the two packages read zero differently (here it means "default
   158	// to DefaultMaxDeliver"; on the policy it means unlimited redeliveries, the
   159	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig semantics), so passing a zero Config.MaxDeliver
   160	// through verbatim would make TermOnExhaustion never fire on the broker's
   161	// real final delivery and orphan work-queue messages (COR-762).
   162	func (c Config) EffectiveMaxDeliver() int {
   163		if c.MaxDeliver == 0 {
   164			return DefaultMaxDeliver
   165		}
   166		return c.MaxDeliver
   167	}
   168	
   169	// validate rejects the configuration errors no retry can fix; shared by
   170	// [Start] (one-shot) and [Run] (supervised, which must fail fast on these
   171	// rather than retry them forever).
   172	func (c Config) validate(nc *nats.Conn, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
   173		if c.KeepInProgress && c.MaxMessages > 1 {
   174			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): KeepInProgress requires MaxMessages <= 1: the heartbeat extends only the in-flight delivery, so %d buffered messages would exhaust AckWait behind a long handler", c.Name, c.MaxMessages)
   175		}
   176		if c.Stream == "" {
   177			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Stream is required", c.Name)
   178		}
   179		if c.Durable == "" {
   180			// CreateOrUpdateConsumer accepts an empty durable and silently makes
   181			// an ephemeral, server-named consumer — losing the stable
   182			// resume-across-restarts behavior this scaffold promises.
   183			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Durable is required", c.Name)
   184		}
   185		if onMsg == nil {
   186			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): onMsg is required", c.Name)
   187		}
   188		if c.FilterSubject != "" && len(c.FilterSubjects) != 0 {
   189			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): set FilterSubject or FilterSubjects, not both", c.Name)
   190		}
   191		for i, subject := range c.FilterSubjects {
   192			if subject == "" {
   193				return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): FilterSubjects[%d] is empty", c.Name, i)
   194			}
   195		}
   196		if c.AckWait < 0 {
   197			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): AckWait must not be negative", c.Name)
   198		}
   199		if c.MaxDeliver < -1 {
   200			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxDeliver must be -1 (unlimited), 0 (default), or positive", c.Name)
   201		}
   202		if c.MaxMessages < 0 {
   203			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxMessages must not be negative", c.Name)
   204		}
   205		if c.MaxAckPending < -1 {
   206			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxAckPending must be -1 (unlimited), 0 (server default), or positive", c.Name)
   207		}
   208		if c.InactiveThreshold < 0 {
   209			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): InactiveThreshold must not be negative", c.Name)
   210		}
   211		if len(c.BackOff) > 0 && c.Retry != nil {
   212			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): set BackOff or Retry, not both: the server stretches the handler's NakWithDelay by the BackOff increments, so neither ladder is the real redelivery envelope (ENT-1535)", c.Name)
   213		}
   214		for i, d := range c.BackOff {
   215			if d <= 0 {
   216				return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): BackOff[%d] must be positive, got %s", c.Name, i, d)
   217			}
   218		}
   219		if n := len(c.BackOff); n > 0 && c.EffectiveMaxDeliver() > 0 && n > c.EffectiveMaxDeliver() {
   220			// The server rejects this outright; catching it here names the two
   221			// fields instead of returning a bare API error at consumer creation.
   222			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): BackOff has %d rungs but MaxDeliver is %d: there are only %d redeliveries to schedule", c.Name, n, c.EffectiveMaxDeliver(), c.EffectiveMaxDeliver())
   223		}
   224		if c.Retry != nil && c.Retry.MaxDeliver() != c.EffectiveMaxDeliver() {
   225			// A policy that disagrees with the broker either never reaches its
   226			// terminal branch or reaches it early (COR-762) — and with Retry the
   227			// terminal branch is the DLQ capture, so the disagreement is a lost
   228			// message rather than a late one.
   229			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Retry MaxDeliver is %d but the consumer's is %d: they must match or the dead-letter branch misses the broker's final delivery", c.Name, c.Retry.MaxDeliver(), c.EffectiveMaxDeliver())
   230		}
   231		if nc == nil {
   232			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): nil nats conn", c.Name)
   233		}
   234		return nil
   235	}

   251	// isShutdownConsumeErr reports whether a consume error is the benign result
   252	// of the connection going away during shutdown. [nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]
   253	// covers the core nats.go sentinels, but the jetstream consume loop surfaces
   254	// its OWN [jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed] — a distinct value that wraps
   255	// neither — so it must be matched separately or a clean rollout drain still
   256	// logs a warning (the COR-923 noise this suppression exists to remove). As
   257	// with the root classifier, it is only "clean" when ctx is already done; a
   258	// mid-run connection loss is a genuine fault worth logging.
   259	func isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx context.Context, err error) bool {
   260		return nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) ||
   261			(ctx.Err() != nil && errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed))
   262	}

   264	// Runner is a live consume loop. Stop halts it and is idempotent.
   265	type Runner struct {
   266		cc jetstream.ConsumeContext
   267		// closed is cc.Closed(), captured while the subscription is live (the
   268		// same channel is returned on every call, so capturing once avoids any
   269		// post-Stop race) — it closes when the consume loop has fully wound
   270		// down, including an in-flight handler.
   271		closed <-chan struct{}
   272		// watcherDone closes when Start's context-cancellation watcher exits. It is
   273		// intentionally internal: callers synchronize on Stop, while tests pin that
   274		// an explicit Stop does not retain a goroutine until the parent context ends.
   275		watcherDone <-chan struct{}
   276		// pollDone closes when the Config.Retry ack-floor poll exits; nil when no
   277		// breaker is armed. Stop joins it, so the connection the poll reads
   278		// through is safe to drain the moment Stop returns.
   279		pollDone <-chan struct{}
   280		stop     sync.Once
   281	}
   282	
   283	// Stop halts the consume loop and blocks until it has fully wound down —
   284	// including an in-flight handler — so a caller may tear down what handlers
   285	// use (stores, publishers, the NATS connection) the moment it returns: the
   286	// cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering (COR-923). Safe on a nil or
   287	// never-Started Runner, idempotent, and safe for concurrent use — an
   288	// explicit Stop can race the context-cancel stop armed by Start. Must not be
   289	// called from inside the handler; it would deadlock waiting on itself.
   290	func (r *Runner) Stop() {
   291		if r == nil || r.cc == nil {
   292			return
   293		}
   294		r.stop.Do(r.cc.Stop)
   295		<-r.closed
   296		if r.pollDone != nil {
   297			<-r.pollDone
   298		}
   299	}

   301	// Start creates/updates the durable consumer on nc and begins delivering
   302	// messages to onMsg, returning a Runner that Stops when ctx is cancelled. The
   303	// stream must already exist (provisioned declaratively); callers whose cells
   304	// opt in per-stream gate Start behind that opt-in so a cell without the stream
   305	// doesn't error at CreateOrUpdateConsumer.
   306	//
   307	// Consume errors are logged at Warn, except a drain/close during shutdown —
   308	// both the core nats.go sentinels ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]) and jetstream's
   309	// own connection-closed error — which is a clean exit rather than a fault.
   310	func Start(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) (*Runner, error) {
   311		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
   312			return nil, err
   313		}
   314		js, err := jetstream.New(nc)
   315		if err != nil {
   316			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): jetstream.New: %w", cfg.Name, err)
   317		}
   318		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, cfg.Stream, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
   319			Durable:           cfg.Durable,
   320			AckPolicy:         jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
   321			AckWait:           cfg.EffectiveAckWait(),
   322			MaxDeliver:        cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(),
   323			FilterSubject:     cfg.FilterSubject,
   324			FilterSubjects:    cfg.FilterSubjects,
   325			InactiveThreshold: cfg.InactiveThreshold,
   326			MaxAckPending:     cfg.MaxAckPending,
   327			// Always sent, so an update carries it: with Config.Retry set this is
   328			// nil by validation, which CLEARS a server ladder an earlier
   329			// deployment left on the durable. Adopting Retry without that clear
   330			// would leave the two schedulers composing exactly as ENT-1535 found
   331			// them, with the library believing it owned redelivery.
   332			BackOff: cfg.BackOff,
   333		})
   334		if err != nil {
   335			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): create consumer %s/%s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, cfg.Durable, err)
   336		}
   337		consumeOpts := []jetstream.PullConsumeOpt{jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {
   338			if isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx, cerr) {
   339				return
   340			}
   341			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume error", slog.Any("error", cerr))
   342		})}
   343		switch {
   344		case cfg.KeepInProgress:
   345			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(1))
   346		case cfg.MaxMessages > 0:
   347			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(cfg.MaxMessages))
   348		}
   349		cc, err := cons.Consume(onMsg, consumeOpts...)
   350		if err != nil {
   351			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): consume %s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, err)
   352		}
   353		watcherDone := make(chan struct{})
   354		r := &Runner{cc: cc, closed: cc.Closed(), watcherDone: watcherDone}
   355		if cfg.Retry != nil {
   356			cfg.Retry.attach(cons, cfg.Name, cfg.logger())
   357			if cfg.Retry.breakerEnabled() {
   358				pollDone := make(chan struct{})
   359				r.pollDone = pollDone
   360				go func() {
   361					defer close(pollDone)
   362					cfg.Retry.pollFloor(ctx, r.closed)
   363				}()
   364			}
   365		}
   366		go func() {
   367			defer close(watcherDone)
   368			select {
   369			case <-ctx.Done():
   370				r.Stop()
   371			case <-r.closed:
   372			}
   373		}()
   374		return r, nil
   375	}

   377	// isRetryableStartError classifies the narrow set of failures that can become
   378	// healthy without changing Config or replacing nc. Everything else returns to
   379	// the owner so a bad deployment cannot stay alive indefinitely with no
   380	// consumer. Unknown server-side 5xx responses are retried, except known
   381	// permanent JetStream configuration/account errors whose API happens to use a
   382	// 5xx status.
   383	func isRetryableStartError(err error) bool {
   384		if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) ||
   385			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrNoResponders) ||
   386			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) ||
   387			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrDisconnected) {
   388			return true
   389		}
   390	
   391		var jsErr jetstream.JetStreamError
   392		if !errors.As(err, &jsErr) || jsErr.APIError() == nil {
   393			return false
   394		}
   395		apiErr := jsErr.APIError()
   396		switch apiErr.ErrorCode { //nolint:exhaustive // unrecognized 5xx codes are deliberately retryable; all other unknown codes fail closed
   397		case jetstream.JSErrCodeBadRequest,
   398			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerCreate,
   399			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerNameExists,
   400			jetstream.JSErrCodeMaximumConsumersLimit,
   401			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabledForAccount,
   402			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabled,
   403			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerAlreadyExists,
   404			jetstream.JSErrCodeDuplicateFilterSubjects,
   405			jetstream.JSErrCodeOverlappingFilterSubjects,
   406			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerEmptyFilter,
   407			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerExists:
   408			return false
   409		default:
   410			return apiErr.Code >= 500
   411		}
   412	}
