     3	import (
     4		"context"
     5		"errors"
     6		"fmt"
     7		"log/slog"
     8		"sync"
     9		"time"
    10	
    11		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
    12	)
    13	
    14	const (
    15		// DefaultFloorAge is how long a durable's ack floor may stay stalled
    16		// before [FloorMonitor] reports it, when FloorMonitorConfig.FloorAge is
    17		// zero. Sized in ENT-1535's Session-1 forensics: above ~10m so an ordinary
    18		// transient that settles by attempt 3 never reaches it, below ~25m so the
    19		// whole stall — including the monitor's own evaluation lag — fits the
    20		// 30-minute SLA.
    21		DefaultFloorAge = 15 * time.Minute
    22	
    23		// Bounds on the derived poll interval when FloorMonitorConfig.Poll is
    24		// zero: FloorAge/10, clamped. The poll is one consumer-info request, so
    25		// the ceiling matters more than the floor.
    26		minFloorPoll = time.Second
    27		maxFloorPoll = 30 * time.Second
    28		// floorPollTimeout bounds one consumer-info request so a NATS blip cannot
    29		// wedge the poll loop — and, through it, [Runner.Stop], which joins it.
    30		floorPollTimeout = 5 * time.Second
    31	)
    32	
    33	// FloorMonitorConfig describes a [FloorMonitor].
    34	type FloorMonitorConfig struct {
    35		// FloorAge is how long the floor must be stalled before [FloorMonitor.Stalled]
    36		// reports it and the stall is logged. Zero uses DefaultFloorAge.
    37		FloorAge time.Duration
    38		// Poll is how often the durable's consumer info is read. Zero derives
    39		// FloorAge/10, clamped to [1s, 30s]. Must be shorter than FloorAge — a
    40		// stall that is never sampled cannot be resolved.
    41		Poll time.Duration
    42		// Name prefixes the monitor's log lines and Logger receives them. Both are
    43		// optional: [Start] fills them from Config.Name and Config.Logger when
    44		// unset.
    45		Name   string
    46		Logger *slog.Logger
    47	}
    48	
    49	// FloorMonitor is an advisory health signal for one durable consumer: it polls
    50	// the durable's ack floor and reports how long that floor has been STALLED.
    51	//
    52	// It is deliberately separate from disposition. Ack-floor state is
    53	// consumer-global and read here from a client-side snapshot, while the
    54	// decision to give up on a message is message-local — so this type observes
    55	// and reports, and something else decides what that is worth. [Retry] can
    56	// consume it to drive its circuit breaker; an adopter that would rather keep
    57	// that judgement can use the monitor alone, publish [FloorMonitor.FloorStall]
    58	// as a gauge, and call [Retry.DeadLetter] on its own terms.
    59	//
    60	// [Start] attaches the live consumer and runs the poll; [Runner.Stop] joins
    61	// it. A monitor belongs to exactly one durable consumer.
    62	//
    63	// # Stalled is not stationary
    64	//
    65	// The distinction is the whole correctness of anything built on this. A
    66	// caught-up consumer's floor sits still because nothing arrived, and a floor
    67	// that has been still for four idle hours says nothing about the next message
    68	// to arrive: crediting that message with the idle time — and quarantining it
    69	// on its second delivery — would be a false positive of exactly the kind this
    70	// signal exists to avoid. So the clock runs only while the consumer has
    71	// delivered past its own floor, the same floor-versus-last-delivered
    72	// comparison the incident runbook makes by hand, and it restarts the moment
    73	// the consumer catches up.
    74	//
    75	// The age is measured from the first observation of a stall, so a freshly
    76	// started process under-reports an already-old one rather than over-reporting
    77	// it: this signal can be late, never early.
    78	type FloorMonitor struct {
    79		cfg FloorMonitorConfig
    80	
    81		mu     sync.Mutex
    82		cons   jetstream.Consumer
    83		name   string
    84		logger *slog.Logger
    85		// clock reads the current time; a package-internal seam so tests can
    86		// drive the stall clock without sleeping.
    87		clock func() time.Time
    88	
    89		stalled     bool
    90		floor       uint64
    91		floorSince  time.Time
    92		stallLogged bool
    93	}
    94	
    95	// NewFloorMonitor validates cfg, applies its defaults, and returns the
    96	// monitor.
    97	func NewFloorMonitor(cfg FloorMonitorConfig) (*FloorMonitor, error) {
    98		if cfg.FloorAge < 0 {
    99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: FloorMonitorConfig.FloorAge must not be negative, got %s (omit the monitor entirely to disable it)", cfg.FloorAge)
   100		}
   101		if cfg.FloorAge == 0 {
   102			cfg.FloorAge = DefaultFloorAge
   103		}
   104		if cfg.Poll < 0 {
   105			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: FloorMonitorConfig.Poll must not be negative, got %s", cfg.Poll)
   106		}
   107		m := &FloorMonitor{cfg: cfg, clock: time.Now}
   108		if p := m.pollInterval(); p >= cfg.FloorAge {
   109			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: FloorMonitorConfig.Poll (%s) must be shorter than FloorAge (%s): a stall that is never sampled cannot be resolved", p, cfg.FloorAge)
   110		}
   111		return m, nil
   112	}
   113	
   114	// FloorAge reports the configured stall threshold.
   115	func (m *FloorMonitor) FloorAge() time.Duration { return m.cfg.FloorAge }
   116	
   117	// pollInterval is the effective poll cadence: Poll, or FloorAge/10 clamped to
   118	// [minFloorPoll, maxFloorPoll].
   119	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollInterval() time.Duration {
   120		if m.cfg.Poll > 0 {
   121			return m.cfg.Poll
   122		}
   123		return max(minFloorPoll, min(m.cfg.FloorAge/10, maxFloorPoll))
   124	}
   125	
   126	// FloorStall reports the durable's ack floor (a stream sequence), how long it
   127	// has been stalled there, and whether it is stalled at all. Publish it as a
   128	// gauge — it is the signal the ack-floor monitor pages on, available from
   129	// inside the process rather than by polling consumer info a second time.
   130	//
   131	// See the type doc for what "stalled" means, and why it is not the same as
   132	// the floor merely being motionless.
   133	func (m *FloorMonitor) FloorStall() (floor uint64, age time.Duration, stalled bool) {
   134		m.mu.Lock()
   135		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   136		if !m.stalled {
   137			return m.floor, 0, false
   138		}
   139		return m.floor, m.clock().Sub(m.floorSince), true
   140	}
   141	
   142	// Stalled reports whether the floor has been stalled past FloorAge — the
   143	// condition worth acting on, as opposed to any stall at all.
   144	func (m *FloorMonitor) Stalled() bool {
   145		_, age, stalled := m.FloorStall()
   146		return stalled && age >= m.cfg.FloorAge
   147	}
   148	
   149	// observeFloor records one reading of the durable's ack floor against its
   150	// last-delivered sequence, starting the stall clock when work is outstanding
   151	// below the delivered mark and clearing it when the consumer catches up.
   152	//
   153	// delivered <= floor means every delivery this consumer has made is settled:
   154	// there is no blocked message to age, whatever the floor has been doing. Note
   155	// this stays true while a blocker waits out a ladder rung — it has been
   156	// delivered, so Delivered stays above the floor even though nothing is
   157	// ack-pending at that instant, which is why NumAckPending is the wrong gate
   158	// here.
   159	func (m *FloorMonitor) observeFloor(floor, delivered uint64, at time.Time) {
   160		m.mu.Lock()
   161		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   162		caughtUp := delivered <= floor
   163		sameStall := m.stalled && m.floor == floor
   164		m.floor = floor
   165		switch {
   166		case caughtUp:
   167			m.stalled = false
   168		case sameStall:
   169			return // still the same stall; the clock runs on
   170		default:
   171			m.stalled = true
   172			m.floorSince = at
   173		}
   174		m.stallLogged = false
   175	}
   176	
   177	// attach binds the live consumer (and the host's log identity, when the config
   178	// left it unset). Called by [Start] on every attempt, including [Run]'s
   179	// recreates.
   180	func (m *FloorMonitor) attach(cons jetstream.Consumer, name string, logger *slog.Logger) {
   181		m.mu.Lock()
   182		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   183		m.cons = cons
   184		m.name = firstNonEmpty(m.cfg.Name, name)
   185		if m.cfg.Logger != nil {
   186			m.logger = m.cfg.Logger
   187		} else {
   188			m.logger = logger
   189		}
   190	}
   191	
   192	func (m *FloorMonitor) log() (*slog.Logger, string) {
   193		m.mu.Lock()
   194		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   195		logger, name := m.logger, m.name
   196		if logger == nil {
   197			if m.cfg.Logger != nil {
   198				logger = m.cfg.Logger
   199			} else {
   200				logger = slog.Default()
   201			}
   202		}
   203		if name == "" {
   204			name = firstNonEmpty(m.cfg.Name, "jsconsumer")
   205		}
   206		return logger, name
   207	}
   208	
   209	func firstNonEmpty(a, b string) string {
   210		if a != "" {
   211			return a
   212		}
   213		return b
   214	}
   215	
   216	// pollFloor reads the ack floor until ctx is cancelled or stop is closed (the
   217	// consume loop winding down). It samples once immediately so a long-lived
   218	// stall is observed at Start rather than one interval later.
   219	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollFloor(ctx context.Context, stop <-chan struct{}) {
   220		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
   221		defer cancel()
   222		// Cancel on the consume loop closing too, so an in-flight consumer-info
   223		// request cannot hold Runner.Stop open for floorPollTimeout. The watcher
   224		// exits with ctx via the deferred cancel.
   225		go func() {
   226			select {
   227			case <-stop:
   228				cancel()
   229			case <-ctx.Done():
   230			}
   231		}()
   232	
   233		m.pollOnce(ctx)
   234		t := time.NewTicker(m.pollInterval())
   235		defer t.Stop()
   236		for {
   237			select {
   238			case <-ctx.Done():
   239				return
   240			case <-t.C:
   241				m.pollOnce(ctx)
   242			}
   243		}
   244	}
   245	
   246	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollOnce(ctx context.Context) {
   247		m.mu.Lock()
   248		cons := m.cons
   249		m.mu.Unlock()
   250		if cons == nil {
   251			return
   252		}
   253		infoCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, floorPollTimeout)
   254		defer cancel()
   255		info, err := cons.Info(infoCtx)
   256		if err != nil {
   257			if ctx.Err() != nil {
   258				return // shutting down; a failed read here is the wind-down, not a fault
   259			}
   260			logger, name := m.log()
   261			logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor poll failed", slog.Any("error", err))
   262			return
   263		}
   264		m.observeFloor(info.AckFloor.Stream, info.Delivered.Stream, m.clock())
   265	
   266		// Report a stall past the threshold once per stall. This is the signal
   267		// ENT-1535 had none of in-process, and it stays visible whether or not
   268		// anything acts on it.
   269		floor, age, stalled := m.FloorStall()
   270		if !stalled || age < m.cfg.FloorAge {
   271			return
   272		}
   273		m.mu.Lock()
   274		first := !m.stallLogged
   275		m.stallLogged = true
   276		m.mu.Unlock()
   277		if !first {
   278			return
   279		}
   280		logger, name := m.log()
   281		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor stalled past FloorAge",
   282			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
   283			slog.Duration("stalled_for", age),
   284			slog.Uint64("last_delivered", info.Delivered.Stream),
   285			slog.Int("num_ack_pending", info.NumAckPending))
   286	}
   287	
   288	// errMonitorConflict is returned when a Config names one floor monitor and its
   289	// Retry another: there is one durable and one poll loop, so there can only be
   290	// one monitor.
   291	var errMonitorConflict = errors.New("Config.FloorMonitor and Retry's monitor are different: one durable has one ack floor, so both must be the same *FloorMonitor (or leave Config.FloorMonitor nil and let Start use the Retry's)")

1	package jsconsumer
     2	
     3	import (
     4		"context"
     5		"errors"
     6		"fmt"
     7		"log/slog"
     8		"sync"
     9		"time"
    10	
    11		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
    12	
    13		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/backoff"
    14		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg"
    15	)
    16	
    17	const (
    18		// DefaultMinDeliveries is the number of deliveries a message must already
    19		// have burned before the breaker will dead-letter it, when
    20		// RetryConfig.MinDeliveries is zero. The forensics found events that
    21		// recovered on attempt 4 and none that recovered on 5 or later, so a
    22		// message is never dead-lettered on the delivery that first failed —
    23		// however long the floor has been stalled, it gets at least one retry.
    24		DefaultMinDeliveries = 2
    25		// DefaultCaptureReserve is how many deliveries are held back for retrying
    26		// a failed dead-letter capture when RetryConfig.CaptureReserve is zero.
    27		// One spare delivery turns "the DLQ was briefly unreachable at exactly
    28		// the wrong moment" from a stranded message into a retry.
    29		DefaultCaptureReserve = 1
    30		// NoCaptureReserve is the explicit RetryConfig.CaptureReserve value for
    31		// "spend every delivery on the handler". The ladder then exhausts on the
    32		// broker's own final delivery, so a capture that fails there strands the
    33		// message ([OutcomeStranded]) — acceptable only where the whole delivery
    34		// budget is needed and a stranded message is alerted on.
    35		NoCaptureReserve = -1
    36	)
    37	
    38	// Outcome is what [Retry.Settle] did with a failed delivery.
    39	type Outcome string
    40	
    41	const (
    42		// OutcomeRetried means the delivery was Nak'd for redelivery on the
    43		// ladder.
    44		OutcomeRetried Outcome = "retried"
    45		// OutcomeDeadLettered means the raw message and its headers were captured
    46		// to the DLQ subject and the original Acked, releasing the ack floor.
    47		OutcomeDeadLettered Outcome = "dead_lettered"
    48		// OutcomeStranded means the capture failed with no deliveries left to
    49		// retry it: the broker will drop a Nak at this point, so nothing in the
    50		// system will touch this message again. It is unsettled, it is pinning the
    51		// ack floor, and it needs an operator — the non-lossy break-glass in
    52		// runbooks/nats-poison-ref-event.md. Alert on this; it is the one outcome
    53		// no automation clears.
    54		OutcomeStranded Outcome = "stranded"
    55	)
    56	
    57	// Cause explains an [OutcomeDeadLettered] settlement; it is empty on a retry.
    58	type Cause string
    59	
    60	const (
    61		// CauseFloorAge is the circuit breaker: this message was pinning the
    62		// durable's ack floor and the floor had been stalled past FloorAge.
    63		CauseFloorAge Cause = "floor_age"
    64		// CauseExhausted is the ordinary terminal branch: the delivery cap was
    65		// reached (ENT-1492's dead-letter-then-Ack, replacing the unsettled Term).
    66		CauseExhausted Cause = "max_deliver"
    67		// CausePermanent is a caller-declared unprocessable message, dead-lettered
    68		// by [Retry.DeadLetter] without consuming the ladder.
    69		CausePermanent Cause = "permanent"
    70	)
    71	
    72	// Settlement reports what [Retry.Settle] chose and the state it chose it
    73	// from, for the caller's metrics and log lines. FloorAge and Floor are zero
    74	// when no ack-floor observation was available (the breaker is disabled, or
    75	// [Start] has not run yet).
    76	type Settlement struct {
    77		Outcome   Outcome
    78		Cause     Cause
    79		Delay     time.Duration // redelivery delay applied, on OutcomeRetried
    80		Delivered int           // this message's delivery count, 1-based
    81		Floor     uint64        // last observed ack floor (stream sequence)
    82		FloorAge  time.Duration // how long the floor had been stalled there

    84		// message, whether or not the breaker acted on it — so an adopter running
    85		// BreakerObserveOnly can count what the breaker WOULD have dead-lettered
    86		// before letting it.
    87		BreakerTripped bool
    88	}
    89	
    90	// RetryConfig describes a [Retry]: the one redelivery ladder, the floor-age
    91	// circuit breaker, and the dead-letter capture they both terminate into.
    92	type RetryConfig struct {
    93		// Backoff is the redelivery envelope applied to a transient failure. Its
    94		// MaxDeliver must be positive and must equal the consumer's
    95		// Config.EffectiveMaxDeliver() — the two are cross-checked, because a
    96		// policy that disagrees with the broker either never reaches its terminal
    97		// branch or reaches it early (COR-762).
    98		//
    99		// TermOnExhaustion must be false: this package's terminal branch is
   100		// dead-letter-then-Ack, never a bare Term (ENT-1492 — a Term does not
   101		// settle the message and leaves no record of it).
   102		Backoff backoff.Policy
   103	
   104		// Monitor arms the circuit breaker: once the [FloorMonitor] reports the

   438	// Settle applies the mechanism to a delivery whose handler failed
   439	// transiently, and is the only disposition call such a handler makes. It
   440	// picks exactly one of:

   443	//     been stalled past FloorAge, and has already had MinDeliveries attempts:

   446	//     the Settlement and the message stays on the ladder;

   476	func (r *Retry) Settle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   477		delivered := backoff.NumDelivered(msg)

   493			// and in the log, but the message keeps its remaining deliveries.

   496				logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": breaker would dead-letter this message (observe only)",

   498					slog.Int("delivered", delivered),
   499					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
   500					slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", age))
   501			}

   503		}

   505		if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, s.Cause, reason); err != nil {

   508				// "retried" would be a lie. Leave it unsettled and name the state.
   509				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   510				logger, name := r.log()
   511				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; dead-letter capture failed with no deliveries left",

   513					slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   514					slog.String("reason", reason),
   515					slog.Int("delivered", delivered),
   516					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor))

   519			}

   521			// retried. Preserve the cause: the terminal branch was reached and
   522			// could not complete.

   524			naked.Cause = s.Cause

   529			// redeliver and be captured again. A duplicate in the DLQ is the

   532			s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried

   539			slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   540			slog.String("reason", reason),

   542			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor),
   543			slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", s.FloorAge))

   548	// DeadLetter captures msg to the DLQ and Acks it immediately, for a failure
   549	// the handler knows no redelivery can fix — an unprocessable payload, a
   550	// reference that will never resolve. It is the non-lossy replacement for a
   551	// bare Term: same terminal effect on the consumer, but the raw message and
   552	// its headers survive in the DLQ.
   553	//
   554	// As in [Settle], a capture failure Naks rather than dropping, and returns
   555	// the error.
   556	//
   557	// This is also the seam for an adopter that wants the stall signal without
   558	// the library's automatic disposition: build a [FloorMonitor], leave
   559	// RetryConfig.Monitor nil, and call DeadLetter from your own quarantine rule.
   560	func (r *Retry) DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   561		var floor uint64
   562		var age time.Duration
   563		if r.cfg.Monitor != nil {
   564			floor, age, _ = r.cfg.Monitor.FloorStall()
   565		}
   566		s := Settlement{
   567			Cause:     CausePermanent,
   568			Delivered: backoff.NumDelivered(msg),
   569			Floor:     floor,
   570			FloorAge:  age,
   571		}
   572		if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, CausePermanent, reason); err != nil {
   573			if s.Delivered > 0 && s.Delivered >= r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver {
   574				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   575				logger, name := r.log()
   576				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; dead-letter capture failed with no deliveries left",
   577					slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("reason", reason), slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered))
   578				r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   579				return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:stranded: %w", err)
   580			}
   581			naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
   582			naked.Cause = CausePermanent
   583			return naked, errors.Join(err, nakErr)
   584		}
   585		if err := msg.Ack(); err != nil {
   586			s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
   587			r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   588			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
   589		}
   590		s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
   591		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   592		return s, nil
   593	}

   595	// capture republishes the raw message and headers to the DLQ subject, tagging
   596	// the reason with its cause.
   597	func (r *Retry) capture(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, cause Cause, reason string) error {
   598		if err := natsmsg.DeadLetter(ctx, r.cfg.Publisher, r.cfg.DLQSubject, msg, string(cause)+": "+reason); err != nil {
   599			logger, name := r.log()
   600			logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": settle:dlq_publish_failed",
   601				slog.Any("error", err),
   602				slog.String("dlq_subject", r.cfg.DLQSubject),
   603				slog.String("cause", string(cause)))
   604			return fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_publish_failed: %w", err)
   605		}
   606		return nil
   607	}
   608	
   609	// nak schedules the next delivery on the ladder and completes s.
   610	func (r *Retry) nak(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) (Settlement, error) {
   611		s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
   612		s.Delay = r.cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(s.Delivered)
   613		err := msg.NakWithDelay(s.Delay)

   615		if err != nil {
   616			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:nak_failed: %w", err)
   617		}
   618		return s, nil
   619	}

   621	func (r *Retry) observe(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) {
   622		if r.cfg.OnSettle != nil {
   623			r.cfg.OnSettle(ctx, msg, s)
   624		}
   625	}

+  capture both terminate into. A JetStream consumer has two redelivery
+  schedulers — the server's `ConsumerConfig.BackOff` and the handler's own
+  `NakWithDelay` — and setting both does not pick one: the server stretches
+  each NAK delay by the BackOff increments, so the configured ladder becomes
+  dead config that still reads as authoritative (ENT-1535 measured a real
+  34h22m envelope against a documented 17h45m). `Config.BackOff` and
+  `Config.Retry` are therefore mutually exclusive — a `Start` error — and
+  adopting a `Retry` clears any ladder already on the durable.
+

+  message survives and the stall stays visible — and `CaptureReserve` holds
+  back deliveries specifically to retry it. When even those are spent the
+  message is reported as `OutcomeStranded`, not dressed up as a retry: a Nak
+  at the broker's cap is dropped, so nothing will touch it again and it needs
+  the break-glass runbook. Alert on that outcome.
+- **`jsconsumer.FloorMonitor`** — the durable's ack-floor health signal,
+  separate from disposition on purpose: ack-floor state is consumer-global
+  while giving up on a message is message-local, so this type observes and
+  reports and something else decides what that is worth. `Start` polls it and
+  `Stop` joins the poll. Publish `FloorStall` as a gauge, drive your own
+  quarantine rule off `Stalled()` + `Retry.DeadLetter`, or hand it to
+  `RetryConfig.Monitor` and let the breaker act on it.

+  badly under backlog, where 35 minutes of receipt→first-delivery lag on a
+  perfectly healthy message would read as a stall. Stalled is also not the
+  same as *stationary* — the clock runs only while the consumer has delivered

   381	// message far above a floor pinned by someone else is not the blocker, and
   382	// dead-lettering it would take a merely-slow event away from a ladder it
   383	// might still recover on.
   384	//
   385	// The exact match assumes the consumer's filter matches densely enough that
   386	// the blocker really does sit at floor+1 — true where the filter covers the
   387	// whole stream (repo_refs_v1, where the ENT-1535 blocker sat one sequence
   388	// above the floor). A narrow filter over a sparse stream can leave a gap
   389	// there, and then the breaker never identifies a blocker. That failure is
   390	// safe but silent, so it is logged: see the "no delivery at floor+1" line
   391	// below and [FloorMonitor]'s own "ack floor stalled past FloorAge" line.
   392	func (r *Retry) isFloorBlocker(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg) (blocker bool, floor uint64, age time.Duration) {
   393		mon := r.cfg.Monitor
   394		if mon == nil {
   395			return false, 0, 0
   396		}
   397		floor, age, stalled := mon.FloorStall()
   398		if !stalled || age < mon.FloorAge() {
   399			return false, floor, age
   400		}
   401		meta, err := msg.Metadata()
   402		if err != nil || meta == nil {
   403			return false, floor, age
   404		}
   405		if meta.Sequence.Stream == floor+1 {
   406			return true, floor, age
   407		}
   408		r.reportFloorGap(ctx, floor, age, meta.Sequence.Stream)
   409		return false, floor, age
   410	}
   411	
   412	// reportFloorGap names, once per stall, the first failing
   413	// delivery seen above a stalled floor that is not floor+1. Either the real
   414	// blocker is elsewhere (another replica holds it, or it is waiting out a
   415	// ladder rung) or the consumer's filter leaves a gap at floor+1 and the
   416	// breaker cannot fire at all. The two look identical from inside the process;
   417	// printing the sequence the breaker wanted against the one it got is what
   418	// tells them apart from the logs.
   419	func (r *Retry) reportFloorGap(ctx context.Context, floor uint64, age time.Duration, seq uint64) {
   420		if seq <= floor {
   421			return // already settled past; not a candidate blocker at all
   422		}
   423		r.mu.Lock()
   424		first := !r.gapLogged || r.gapLoggedFor != floor
   425		r.gapLogged, r.gapLoggedFor = true, floor
   426		r.mu.Unlock()
   427		if !first {
   428			return
   429		}
   430		logger, name := r.log()
   431		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor stalled but no delivery at floor+1; breaker cannot identify the blocker",
   432			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
   433			slog.Uint64("want_stream_seq", floor+1),
   434			slog.Uint64("got_stream_seq", seq),
   435			slog.Duration("stalled_for", age))
   436	}
   437	
   438	// Settle applies the mechanism to a delivery whose handler failed
   439	// transiently, and is the only disposition call such a handler makes. It
   440	// picks exactly one of:
   441	//
   442	//   - the circuit breaker — this message is pinning an ack floor that has
   443	//     been stalled past FloorAge, and has already had MinDeliveries attempts:
   444	//     capture to the DLQ and Ack, whatever the attempt count (Cause
   445	//     CauseFloorAge). Under BreakerObserveOnly the condition is reported on
   446	//     the Settlement and the message stays on the ladder;
   447	//   - exhaustion — the ladder is spent (delivery MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve or
   448	//     later): capture to the DLQ and Ack (Cause CauseExhausted);
   449	//   - the ladder — NakWithDelay for redelivery (Outcome OutcomeRetried).
   450	//
   451	// reason is recorded on the captured copy's Nats-Dlq-Reason header, prefixed
   452	// with the cause, so the DLQ says why a message is there and not just that it
   453	// is.
   454	//
   455	// # When the capture itself fails
   456	//
   457	// A capture failure is never allowed to become a drop, and the Settlement
   458	// says which of two very different things happened:
   459	//
   460	//   - Deliveries remain (CaptureReserve is doing its job): the original is
   461	//     Nak'd, the error returned is settle:dlq_publish_failed, and the
   462	//     Settlement reports OutcomeRetried with the Cause of the terminal branch
   463	//     that could not complete — so the caller's metrics show a DLQ path being
   464	//     reached and failing rather than one sitting idle. The next delivery
   465	//     retries the capture.
   466	//   - No deliveries remain: a Nak here is dropped by the broker, so nothing
   467	//     will retry. The Settlement reports [OutcomeStranded] and the message is
   468	//     left unsettled, pinning the ack floor so the monitor fires — ENT-1492's
   469	//     deliberate posture for a degraded DLQ path, and the one state this
   470	//     package cannot resolve on its own. It is reported as what it is rather
   471	//     than dressed up as a retry.
   472	//
   473	// An Ack that fails after a successful capture (settle:dlq_ack_failed) leaves
   474	// the original to redeliver and be captured again; a duplicate in the DLQ
   475	// beats a lost message, and the Settlement reports OutcomeRetried.
   476	func (r *Retry) Settle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   477		delivered := backoff.NumDelivered(msg)
   478		blocker, floor, age := r.isFloorBlocker(ctx, msg)
   479	
   480		s := Settlement{
   481			Delivered:      delivered,
   482			Floor:          floor,
   483			FloorAge:       age,
   484			BreakerTripped: blocker && delivered >= r.cfg.MinDeliveries,
   485		}
   486		switch {
   487		case s.BreakerTripped && !r.cfg.BreakerObserveOnly:
   488			s.Cause = CauseFloorAge
   489		case r.ladderSpent(delivered):
   490			s.Cause = CauseExhausted
   491		default:
   492			// Includes the observe-only trip: the condition is on the Settlement
   493			// and in the log, but the message keeps its remaining deliveries.
   494			if s.BreakerTripped {
   495				logger, name := r.log()
   496				logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": breaker would dead-letter this message (observe only)",
   497					slog.String("reason", reason),
   498					slog.Int("delivered", delivered),
   499					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
   500					slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", age))
   501			}
   502			return r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
   503		}
   504	
   505		if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, s.Cause, reason); err != nil {
   506			if delivered > 0 && delivered >= r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver {
   507				// Out of deliveries: a Nak is dropped by the broker, so saying
   508				// "retried" would be a lie. Leave it unsettled and name the state.
   509				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   510				logger, name := r.log()
   511				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; dead-letter capture failed with no deliveries left",
   512					slog.Any("error", err),
   513					slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   514					slog.String("reason", reason),
   515					slog.Int("delivered", delivered),
   516					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor))
   517				r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   518				return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:stranded: %w", err)
   519			}
   520			// Deliveries remain — fall back to the ladder so the capture is
   521			// retried. Preserve the cause: the terminal branch was reached and
   522			// could not complete.
   523			naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
   524			naked.Cause = s.Cause
   525			return naked, errors.Join(err, nakErr)
   526		}
   527		if err := msg.Ack(); err != nil {
   528			// The copy is in the DLQ but the original is unsettled: it will
   529			// redeliver and be captured again. A duplicate in the DLQ is the
   530			// right trade against losing the message or pinning the floor
   531			// forever.
   532			s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
   533			r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   534			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
   535		}
   536		s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
   537		logger, name := r.log()
   538		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": dead-lettered",
   539			slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   540			slog.String("reason", reason),
   541			slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   542			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor),
   543			slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", s.FloorAge))
   544		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   545		return s, nil
   546	}
   547	
   548	// DeadLetter captures msg to the DLQ and Acks it immediately, for a failure
   549	// the handler knows no redelivery can fix — an unprocessable payload, a
   550	// reference that will never resolve. It is the non-lossy replacement for a
   551	// bare Term: same terminal effect on the consumer, but the raw message and
   552	// its headers survive in the DLQ.
   553	//
   554	// As in [Settle], a capture failure Naks rather than dropping, and returns
   555	// the error.
   556	//
   557	// This is also the seam for an adopter that wants the stall signal without
   558	// the library's automatic disposition: build a [FloorMonitor], leave
   559	// RetryConfig.Monitor nil, and call DeadLetter from your own quarantine rule.
   560	func (r *Retry) DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   561		var floor uint64
   562		var age time.Duration
   563		if r.cfg.Monitor != nil {
   564			floor, age, _ = r.cfg.Monitor.FloorStall()
   565		}
   566		s := Settlement{
   567			Cause:     CausePermanent,
   568			Delivered: backoff.NumDelivered(msg),
   569			Floor:     floor,
   570			FloorAge:  age,
   571		}
   572		if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, CausePermanent, reason); err != nil {
   573			if s.Delivered > 0 && s.Delivered >= r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver {
   574				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   575				logger, name := r.log()
   576				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; dead-letter capture failed with no deliveries left",
   577					slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("reason", reason), slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered))
   578				r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   579				return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:stranded: %w", err)
   580			}
   581			naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
   582			naked.Cause = CausePermanent
   583			return naked, errors.Join(err, nakErr)
   584		}
   585		if err := msg.Ack(); err != nil {
   586			s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
   587			r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   588			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
   589		}
   590		s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
   591		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   592		return s, nil
   593	}
   594	
   595	// capture republishes the raw message and headers to the DLQ subject, tagging
   596	// the reason with its cause.
   597	func (r *Retry) capture(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, cause Cause, reason string) error {
   598		if err := natsmsg.DeadLetter(ctx, r.cfg.Publisher, r.cfg.DLQSubject, msg, string(cause)+": "+reason); err != nil {
   599			logger, name := r.log()
   600			logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": settle:dlq_publish_failed",
   601				slog.Any("error", err),
   602				slog.String("dlq_subject", r.cfg.DLQSubject),
   603				slog.String("cause", string(cause)))
   604			return fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_publish_failed: %w", err)
   605		}
   606		return nil
   607	}
   608	
   609	// nak schedules the next delivery on the ladder and completes s.
   610	func (r *Retry) nak(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) (Settlement, error) {
   611		s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
   612		s.Delay = r.cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(s.Delivered)
   613		err := msg.NakWithDelay(s.Delay)
   614		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   615		if err != nil {
   616			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:nak_failed: %w", err)
   617		}
   618		return s, nil
   619	}
   620	
   621	func (r *Retry) observe(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) {
   622		if r.cfg.OnSettle != nil {
   623			r.cfg.OnSettle(ctx, msg, s)
   624		}
   625	}

   179	// the durable. Whichever mechanism is configured is the only one running.
   180	//
   181	// # What the breaker measures
   182	//
   183	// Floor-stationary age, not message stream-age. The two diverge badly under
   184	// backlog: the same forensics measured 35 minutes of receipt→first-delivery
   185	// lag on a healthy message, which a stream-age trigger would read as a stall.
   186	// The ack floor only stops advancing when a message genuinely will not
   187	// settle, which is the condition worth breaking on.
   188	//
   189	// The signal itself lives in [FloorMonitor], deliberately: ack-floor state is
   190	// consumer-global and this decision is message-local, so the observation is a
   191	// separate, independently usable thing and RetryConfig.Monitor is what opts
   192	// into acting on it. Leave that nil and Settle is purely message-local — the
   193	// ladder and exhaustion, nothing inferred about the consumer as a whole.
   194	//
   195	// Acting on it is a heuristic, and two limits follow that this package cannot
   196	// resolve from inside, so both are made loud rather than assumed away: the
   197	// blocker is identified as the sequence at floor+1, which a filter sparse
   198	// enough to leave a gap there defeats (logged, see [Retry.Settle]); and a
   199	// stall held by another replica is indistinguishable from one this process
   200	// could act on. RetryConfig.BreakerObserveOnly exists to measure both against
   201	// real traffic before the breaker is trusted to Ack anything.
   202	//
   203	// A Retry belongs to exactly one durable consumer; give each consumer its
   204	// own.
   205	//
   206	// # Worst-case pin
   207	//
   208	// The breaker acts on a delivery, so the floor can stay pinned for up to
   209	// FloorAge + the largest ladder rung + AckWait. Construction rejects a rung
   210	// longer than FloorAge, which bounds it at 2×FloorAge + AckWait; pick rungs
   211	// well under FloorAge to leave headroom.
   212	//
   213	// The ladder's own reach is a second, independent bound, and the one that
   214	// applies with the breaker in observe-only mode or disabled: the DLQ is
   215	// reached at delivery Backoff.MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve, so budget
   216	// (MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve-1) rungs of wall-clock for it.
   217	//
   218	// # Wiring
   219	//
   220	// The first adopter, entire-search's search-indexer-…2212 tokens truncated…q, age)
    89	}

    91	// armStall drives the monitor to the state a real poll loop would have built
    92	// up: floor pinned at seq, stalled for age. It sets the state rather than
    93	// replaying observations so a test can re-arm the same floor with a different
    94	// age; observeFloor's own transitions are covered by the TestObserveFloor*
    95	// cases.
    96	func armStall(m *FloorMonitor, seq uint64, age time.Duration) {
    97		now := time.Now()
    98		m.mu.Lock()
    99		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   100		m.clock = func() time.Time { return now }
   101		m.stalled, m.floor, m.floorSince, m.stallLogged = true, seq, now.Add(-age), false
   102	}

   273	// TestSettleBreakerDeadLettersTheFloorBlocker is the ENT-1535 remedy: the
   274	// blocker at floor+1, on a floor stationary past the threshold, is captured
   275	// and Acked at delivery 2 — nowhere near the delivery cap that would
   276	// otherwise take ~43 minutes to reach.
   277	func TestSettleBreakerDeadLettersTheFloorBlocker(t *testing.T) {
   278		var got Settlement
   279		r, pub := newTestRetry(t, func(c *RetryConfig) {
   280			c.OnSettle = func(_ context.Context, _ jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) { got = s }
   281		})
   282		armFloor(r, 2774436, 16*time.Minute)
   283		msg := deliveredMsg(2774437, 2)
   284	
   285		s, err := r.Settle(t.Context(), msg, "re-queuing: update")
   286		if err != nil {
   287			t.Fatalf("Settle: %v", err)
   288		}
   289		if s.Outcome != OutcomeDeadLettered || s.Cause != CauseFloorAge {
   290			t.Fatalf("Settlement = %+v, want dead_lettered/floor_age", s)
   291		}
   292		if !msg.Acked {
   293			t.Error("blocker not Acked; the ack floor stays pinned")
   294		}
   295		if msg.Termed {
   296			t.Error("blocker Termed; a Term does not settle the message (ENT-1492)")
   297		}
   298		if len(msg.NakDelays) != 0 || msg.Naks != 0 {
   299			t.Errorf("blocker also naked (%d delayed, %d plain), want none", len(msg.NakDelays), msg.Naks)
   300		}
   301		if s.Floor != 2774436 || s.FloorAge != 16*time.Minute {
   302			t.Errorf("Settlement floor state = %d/%s, want 2774436/16m0s", s.Floor, s.FloorAge)
   303		}
   304		if got != s {
   305			t.Errorf("OnSettle saw %+v, want %+v", got, s)
   306		}

   308		captured := pub.captured()
   309		if len(captured) != 1 {
   310			t.Fatalf("captured %d messages, want 1", len(captured))

   312		c := captured[0]

   314			t.Errorf("DLQ subject = %q, want repo.refs.dlq", c.Subject)
   315		}
   316		if string(c.Data) != "ref-event" {
   317			t.Errorf("DLQ payload = %q, want the raw message", c.Data)

   320			t.Error("DLQ copy lost the original headers")
   321		}
   322		if reason := c.Header.Get(natsmsg.DLQReasonHeader); !strings.HasPrefix(reason, string(CauseFloorAge)+": ") {
   323			t.Errorf("DLQ reason = %q, want it prefixed with the cause", reason)

   369	// TestSettleReportsAnUnidentifiableBlocker: the breaker identifies the
   370	// blocker as the sequence immediately above the floor, which assumes the
   371	// consumer's filter is dense enough for that message to exist. When it isn't
   372	// — a narrow filter over a sparse stream — the breaker cannot fire, and that
   373	// must not be silent: the log names the sequence it wanted against the one it
   374	// saw, which is how a staging exercise tells "wrong predicate" apart from
   375	// "the real blocker is on another replica".
   376	func TestSettleReportsAnUnidentifiableBlocker(t *testing.T) {
   377		logs := &logCapture{}
   378		r, _ := newTestRetry(t, func(c *RetryConfig) { c.Logger = slog.New(logs) })
   379		armFloor(r, 2774436, 20*time.Minute)
   380	
   381		for range 3 { // logged once per stationary period, not once per delivery
   382			if _, err := r.Settle(t.Context(), deliveredMsg(2774600, 3), "transient"); err != nil {
   383				t.Fatalf("Settle: %v", err)
   384			}
   385		}
   386		const want = "search-indexer-refs: ack floor stalled but no delivery at floor+1; breaker cannot identify the blocker"
   387		if n := logs.count(want); n != 1 {
   388			t.Fatalf("logged the unidentifiable-blocker warning %d times, want exactly 1; saw %v", n, logs.snapshot())
   389		}
   390	
   391		// A message already below the floor is not a candidate blocker and says
   392		// nothing about a gap.
   393		r.gapLogged = false
   394		if _, err := r.Settle(t.Context(), deliveredMsg(2774400, 3), "transient"); err != nil {
   395			t.Fatalf("Settle: %v", err)
   396		}
   397		if logs.count(want) != 1 {
   398			t.Error("a settled-past sequence was reported as a floor gap")
   399		}

   402	// logCapture is a thread-safe slog.Handler that counts messages, so a test
   403	// can assert a log line is emitted once per stationary period rather than
   404	// once per delivery.
   405	type logCapture struct {
   406		mu   sync.Mutex
   407		msgs []string
   408	}
   409	
   410	func (h *logCapture) Enabled(context.Context, slog.Level) bool { return true }
   411	
   412	func (h *logCapture) Handle(_ context.Context, r slog.Record) error {
   413		h.mu.Lock()
   414		h.msgs = append(h.msgs, r.Message)
   415		h.mu.Unlock()
   416		return nil
   417	}
   418	
   419	func (h *logCapture) WithAttrs([]slog.Attr) slog.Handler { return h }
   420	func (h *logCapture) WithGroup(string) slog.Handler      { return h }
   421	
   422	func (h *logCapture) snapshot() []string {
   423		h.mu.Lock()
   424		defer h.mu.Unlock()
   425		return slices.Clone(h.msgs)
   426	}
   427	
   428	func (h *logCapture) count(msg string) int {
   429		n := 0
   430		for _, m := range h.snapshot() {
   431			if m == msg {
   432				n++
   433			}
   434		}
   435		return n
   436	}

   455	// TestObserveFloorRestartsTheClockWhenTheFloorMoves: an advancing floor —
   456	// however slowly — is not a stall, and re-observing the same stalled floor
   457	// must not restart the clock either.
   458	func TestObserveFloorRestartsTheClockWhenTheFloorMoves(t *testing.T) {
   459		r, _ := newTestRetry(t, nil)

   465		now = base.Add(10 * time.Minute)
   466		r.cfg.Monitor.observeFloor(100, 200, now) // same stall: the clock keeps running
   467		if _, age, _ := r.cfg.Monitor.FloorStall(); age != 10*time.Minute {
   468			t.Fatalf("age after re-observing the same floor = %s, want 10m0s", age)
   469		}
   470	
   471		r.cfg.Monitor.observeFloor(101, 200, now) // floor advanced: clock restarts
   472		floor, age, ok := r.cfg.Monitor.FloorStall()

   475		}

   477		// And the breaker is disarmed again for the new floor.
   478		msg := deliveredMsg(102, 2)
   479		if _, err := r.Settle(t.Context(), msg, "transient"); err != nil {
   480			t.Fatalf("Settle: %v", err)

   487	// TestObserveFloorIgnoresACaughtUpConsumer is the false positive that makes
   488	// the difference between a poison remedy and a message shredder: a quiet
   489	// consumer's floor sits still because NOTHING ARRIVED, not because anything
   490	// is stuck. Crediting the next message to arrive with that idle time would
   491	// dead-letter it on its second delivery. The stall clock therefore runs only
   492	// while the consumer has delivered past its own floor, and starts when the
   493	// gap opens — not when the floor last moved.
   494	func TestObserveFloorIgnoresACaughtUpConsumer(t *testing.T) {
   495		r, pub := newTestRetry(t, nil)
   496		base := time.Now()
   497		now := base
   498		r.cfg.Monitor.clock = func() time.Time { return now }
   499	
   500		// Four idle hours, fully caught up: floor stationary, but not stalled.
   501		r.cfg.Monitor.observeFloor(100, 100, base)
   502		now = base.Add(4 * time.Hour)
   503		r.cfg.Monitor.observeFloor(100, 100, now)
   504		if _, age, stalled := r.cfg.Monitor.FloorStall(); stalled {
   505			t.Fatalf("a caught-up consumer reported as stalled for %s", age)
   506		}
   507	
   508		// A message finally arrives at floor+1 and fails twice. The breaker must
   509		// not fire: the clock starts now, not four hours ago.
   510		r.cfg.Monitor.observeFloor(100, 101, now)
   511		msg := deliveredMsg(101, 2)
   512		if _, err := r.Settle(t.Context(), msg, "transient"); err != nil {
   513			t.Fatalf("Settle: %v", err)
   514		}
   515		if msg.Acked || len(pub.captured()) != 0 {
   516			t.Fatal("breaker dead-lettered a message credited with the consumer's idle time")
   517		}
   518	
   519		// Once the gap has genuinely persisted past the threshold, it fires.
   520		now = now.Add(16 * time.Minute)
   521		blocker := deliveredMsg(101, 3)
   522		if _, err := r.Settle(t.Context(), blocker, "re-queuing: update"); err != nil {
   523			t.Fatalf("Settle: %v", err)
   524		}
   525		if !blocker.Acked || len(pub.captured()) != 1 {
   526			t.Error("breaker did not fire on a stall that really had persisted")
   527		}

content.text:
Much better—the revised architecture is broadly the right approach. The idle-floor bug and failed-capture retry path are fixed, and `FloorMonitor` is now cleanly separable from message disposition. I still wouldn’t ship it unchanged.

1. **[P1] Filtered consumers still cannot identify the blocker** — [retry.go:405](/Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/retry.go:405)

   It still compares stream sequence with `floor+1`. For a filtered consumer, consumer sequence 2 may correspond to stream sequence 200. My probe reproduced the breaker remaining inactive on the actual blocker. Store `AckFloor.Consumer` and compare it with `msg.Metadata().Sequence.Consumer`; retain stream sequence only for telemetry.

2. **[P2] Final-delivery Ack failure is still mislabeled as a retry** — [retry.go:527](/Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/retry.go:527)

   The capture reserve fixes failed publishing, but not failed acknowledgment after a successful capture. At `MaxDeliver`, `Ack()` failure returns `OutcomeRetried`, yet NATS permits no next delivery. The live probe produced two deliveries and no third. This should report a stranded/uncertain settlement, or use bounded `DoubleAck` to confirm settlement.

3. **[P2] `Run` does not join the monitor before recreating** — [jsconsumer.go:508](/Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/jsconsumer.go:508)

   When the consume loop closes naturally, `Run` cancels the attempt but does not call `Stop` or wait for `pollDone`. It can attach the shared monitor to a new consumer while the old poll is still exiting, allowing stale consumer information to overwrite the new state. Join the old runner before the retry delay/recreation.

One rollout concern: `BreakerObserveOnly` is opt-in, while supplying `RetryConfig.Monitor` enables automatic DLQ+Ack by default. Since the docs call observe-only the rollout position, I’d prefer an explicit mode whose zero value is disabled/observe-only, with automatic action requiring an affirmative value.

The original tree passes `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, lint, build, and `git diff --check`. Temporary probes reproduced findings 1 and 2 and were removed.

Overall verdict: the design direction is now sound; fix the sequence identity and final-Ack classification before shipping. The lifecycle join and safer rollout mode should also be addressed before enabling automatic quarantine.

   407	// failingFor reports the wall-clock time a message on delivery number
   408	// `delivered` has spent failing, from the ladder it has been riding: the sum
   409	// of the rungs already served. It is message-local and exact for a flat
   410	// ladder — delivery 4 of a 5-minute ladder has been failing at least 15
   411	// minutes — and conservative in general, since it counts only the scheduled
   412	// waits and not the handler time or AckWait around them. Under-counting is
   413	// the right direction: it can make the breaker late, never early.
   414	func (r *Retry) failingFor(delivered int) time.Duration {
   415		var total time.Duration
   416		for n := 1; n < delivered; n++ {
   417			total += r.cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(n)
   418		}
   419		return total
   420	}
   421	
   422	// shouldQuarantine reports whether msg may be dead-lettered on the strength of
   423	// a stalled ack floor, along with the stall it was judged against.
   424	//
   425	// # Why this is a conjunction and not an identification
   426	//
   427	// The obvious rule — "dead-letter the message pinning the floor" — needs the
   428	// blocker's identity, and JetStream's consumer info does not carry it. The
   429	// two candidate inferences both fail against a live server:
   430	//
   431	//   - AckFloor.Stream+1 is the blocker only when the floor was last computed
   432	//     by the server's pending scan. After the consumer fully drains, the floor
   433	//     jumps to the delivered high-water mark, and a poison message arriving
   434	//     behind non-matching subjects then sits well above floor+1 (measured:
   435	//     floor 2, blocker at stream 6). A filtered consumer hits this routinely.
   436	//   - AckFloor.Consumer+1 is worse. The server only recomputes that floor when
   437	//     the message AT the floor is acked, so it pins to the blocker's FIRST
   438	//     delivery and goes stale the moment it is redelivered (measured: floor
   439	//     stuck at 1 while the blocker's redeliveries ran 4, 5, 6). It matches on
   440	//     delivery 1 and never again — so any MinDeliveries above 1 disables the
   441	//     breaker entirely.
   442	//
   443	// So this does not guess which message is responsible. It requires three
   444	// facts that are each independently true, and acts only when all three hold:
   445	//
   446	//  1. the consumer is genuinely stuck — the monitor reports the ack floor
   447	//     stalled past FloorAge (consumer-global, advisory);
   448	//  2. this message is part of what is stuck — its stream sequence is above
   449	//     the ack floor, so it is un-settled (exact, and free of any assumption
   450	//     about filters or gaps);
   451	//  3. this message has itself been failing at least as long as the stall —
   452	//     from its own delivery count against the ladder (message-local, exact).
   453	//
   454	// A message satisfying all three has burned FloorAge of retries, on its own,
   455	// while the consumer demonstrably made no progress. Whether or not it is the
   456	// head-of-line blocker, it is not a message that is about to recover: the
   457	// ENT-1535 forensics found recoveries at attempt 4 and none at 5 or later.
   458	// If it IS the blocker the floor is released; if it is not, a message that
   459	// has been failing for a quarter of an hour is captured to the DLQ with full
   460	// provenance and can be replayed.
   461	func (r *Retry) shouldQuarantine(msg jetstream.Msg, delivered int) (ok bool, floor uint64, age time.Duration) {
   462		mon := r.cfg.Monitor
   463		if mon == nil {
   464			return false, 0, 0
   465		}
   466		floor, age, stalled := mon.FloorStall()
   467		if !stalled || age < mon.FloorAge() {
   468			return false, floor, age
   469		}
   470		meta, err := msg.Metadata()
   471		if err != nil || meta == nil {
   472			return false, floor, age
   473		}
   474		if meta.Sequence.Stream <= floor {
   475			return false, floor, age // already settled past; not part of the stall
   476		}
   477		if delivered < r.cfg.MinDeliveries {
   478			return false, floor, age
   479		}
   480		return r.failingFor(delivered) >= mon.FloorAge(), floor, age
   481	}
   482	
   483	// Settle applies the mechanism to a delivery whose handler failed
   484	// transiently, and is the only disposition call such a handler makes. It
   485	// picks exactly one of:
   486	//
   487	//   - the circuit breaker — the consumer's ack floor has been stalled past
   488	//     FloorAge and this message has itself been failing that long (see
   489	//     shouldQuarantine): capture to the DLQ and Ack, well before the ladder
   490	//     would have run out (Cause
   491	//     CauseFloorAge). Under [BreakerObserve] the condition is reported on
   492	//     the Settlement and the message stays on the ladder;
   493	//   - exhaustion — the ladder is spent (delivery MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve or
   494	//     later): capture to the DLQ and Ack (Cause CauseExhausted);
   495	//   - the ladder — NakWithDelay for redelivery (Outcome OutcomeRetried).
   496	//
   497	// reason is recorded on the captured copy's Nats-Dlq-Reason header, prefixed
   498	// with the cause, so the DLQ says why a message is there and not just that it
   499	// is.
   500	//
   501	// # When the capture itself fails
   502	//
   503	// A capture failure is never allowed to become a drop, and the Settlement
   504	// says which of two very different things happened:
   505	//
   506	//   - Deliveries remain (CaptureReserve is doing its job): the original is
   507	//     Nak'd, the error returned is settle:dlq_publish_failed, and the
   508	//     Settlement reports OutcomeRetried with the Cause of the terminal branch
   509	//     that could not complete — so the caller's metrics show a DLQ path being
   510	//     reached and failing rather than one sitting idle. The next delivery
   511	//     retries the capture.
   512	//   - No deliveries remain: a Nak here is dropped by the broker, so nothing
   513	//     will retry. The Settlement reports [OutcomeStranded] and the message is
   514	//     left unsettled, pinning the ack floor so the monitor fires — ENT-1492's
   515	//     deliberate posture for a degraded DLQ path, and the one state this
   516	//     package cannot resolve on its own. It is reported as what it is rather
   517	//     than dressed up as a retry.
   518	//
   519	// An Ack that fails after a successful capture (settle:dlq_ack_failed) leaves
   520	// the original to redeliver and be captured again; a duplicate in the DLQ
   521	// beats a lost message, and the Settlement reports OutcomeRetried.
   522	func (r *Retry) Settle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   523		delivered := backoff.NumDelivered(msg)
   524		quarantine, floor, age := r.shouldQuarantine(msg, delivered)
   525	
   526		s := Settlement{
   527			Delivered:      delivered,
   528			Floor:          floor,
   529			FloorAge:       age,
   530			FailingFor:     r.failingFor(delivered),
   531			BreakerTripped: quarantine,
   532		}
   533		switch {
   534		case quarantine && r.cfg.Breaker == BreakerEnforce:
   535			s.Cause = CauseFloorAge
   536		case r.ladderSpent(delivered):
   537			s.Cause = CauseExhausted
   538		default:
   539			// Includes the observe-only trip: the condition is on the Settlement
   540			// and in the log, but the message keeps its remaining deliveries.
   541			if quarantine {
   542				logger, name := r.log()
   543				logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": breaker would dead-letter this message (observe only)",
   544					slog.String("reason", reason),
   545					slog.Int("delivered", delivered),
   546					slog.Duration("failing_for", s.FailingFor),
   547					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
   548					slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", age))
   549			}
   550			return r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
   551		}
   552		return r.terminate(ctx, msg, s, reason)
   553	}
   554	
   555	// terminate runs the capture-then-settle sequence shared by [Settle]'s two
   556	// terminal branches and [Retry.DeadLetter], and classifies every way it can
   557	// fall short. s must already carry its Cause.
   558	func (r *Retry) terminate(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   559		logger, name := r.log()
   560		spent := s.Delivered > 0 && s.Delivered >= r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver
   561	
   562		if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, s.Cause, reason); err != nil {
   563			if spent {
   564				// Out of deliveries: a Nak is dropped by the broker, so saying
   565				// "retried" would be a lie. Leave it unsettled and name the state.
   566				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   567				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; dead-letter capture failed with no deliveries left",
   568					slog.Any("error", err),
   569					slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   570					slog.String("reason", reason),
   571					slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   572					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor))
   573				r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   574				return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:stranded: %w", err)
   575			}
   576			// Deliveries remain — fall back to the ladder so the capture is
   577			// retried. Preserve the cause: the terminal branch was reached and
   578			// could not complete.
   579			naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
   580			naked.Cause = s.Cause
   581			return naked, errors.Join(err, nakErr)
   582		}
   583		s.Captured = true
   584	
   585		// DoubleAck, not Ack: a plain Ack is fire-and-forget, so a lost one leaves
   586		// the floor pinned with nothing reporting it. Waiting for the server's
   587		// confirmation is what makes the settlement a fact rather than a hope, and
   588		// it costs one round-trip on a path that only runs when a message is being
   589		// given up on.
   590		ackCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, dlqAckTimeout)
   591		defer cancel()
   592		if err := msg.DoubleAck(ackCtx); err != nil {
   593			if spent {
   594				// The copy is safe in the DLQ, but the original is unsettled and
   595				// no further delivery is coming: it will pin the ack floor until
   596				// the stream's retention expires it. Captured distinguishes this
   597				// from a stranding with nothing captured — the data is recoverable,
   598				// the consumer is not.
   599				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   600				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; captured to the DLQ but the ack failed with no deliveries left",
   601					slog.Any("error", err),
   602					slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   603					slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   604					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor))
   605				r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   606				return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
   607			}
   608			// A delivery remains: the message redelivers and is captured again.
   609			// A duplicate in the DLQ beats a pinned floor.
   610			s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
   611			r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   612			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
   613		}
   614	
   615		s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
   616		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": dead-lettered",
   617			slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   618			slog.String("reason", reason),
   619			slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   620			slog.Duration("failing_for", s.FailingFor),
   621			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor),
   622			slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", s.FloorAge))
   623		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   624		return s, nil
   625	}
   626	
   627	// DeadLetter captures msg to the DLQ and Acks it immediately, for a failure
   628	// the handler knows no redelivery can fix — an unprocessable payload, a
   629	// reference that will never resolve. It is the non-lossy replacement for a
   630	// bare Term: same terminal effect on the consumer, but the raw message and
   631	// its headers survive in the DLQ.
   632	//
   633	// As in [Settle], a capture failure Naks rather than dropping, and returns
   634	// the error.
   635	//
   636	// This is also the seam for an adopter that wants the stall signal without
   637	// the library's automatic disposition: build a [FloorMonitor], leave
   638	// RetryConfig.Monitor nil, and call DeadLetter from your own quarantine rule.
   639	func (r *Retry) DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   640		var floor uint64
   641		var age time.Duration
   642		if r.cfg.Monitor != nil {
   643			floor, age, _ = r.cfg.Monitor.FloorStall()
   644		}
   645		delivered := backoff.NumDelivered(msg)
   646		return r.terminate(ctx, msg, Settlement{
   647			Cause:      CausePermanent,
   648			Delivered:  delivered,
   649			FailingFor: r.failingFor(delivered),
   650			Floor:      floor,
   651			FloorAge:   age,
   652		}, reason)
   653	}
   654	
   655	// capture republishes the raw message and headers to the DLQ subject, tagging
   656	// the reason with its cause.
   657	func (r *Retry) capture(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, cause Cause, reason string) error {
   658		if err := natsmsg.DeadLetter(ctx, r.cfg.Publisher, r.cfg.DLQSubject, msg, string(cause)+": "+reason); err != nil {
   659			logger, name := r.log()
   660			logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": settle:dlq_publish_failed",
   661				slog.Any("error", err),
   662				slog.String("dlq_subject", r.cfg.DLQSubject),
   663				slog.String("cause", string(cause)))
   664			return fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_publish_failed: %w", err)
   665		}
   666		return nil
   667	}
   668	
   669	// nak schedules the next delivery on the ladder and completes s.
   670	func (r *Retry) nak(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) (Settlement, error) {

   672		s.Delay = r.cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(s.Delivered)

   678		return s, nil
   679	}

   682		if r.cfg.OnSettle != nil {
   683			r.cfg.OnSettle(ctx, msg, s)
   684		}
   685	}

   510	//     reached and failing rather than one sitting idle. The next delivery

   513	//     will retry. The Settlement reports [OutcomeStranded] and the message is

   528			Floor:          floor,

   540			// and in the log, but the message keeps its remaining deliveries.

   555	// terminate runs the capture-then-settle sequence shared by [Settle]'s two
   556	// terminal branches and [Retry.DeadLetter], and classifies every way it can
   557	// fall short. s must already carry its Cause.
   558	func (r *Retry) terminate(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   559		logger, name := r.log()
   560		spent := s.Delivered > 0 && s.Delivered >= r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver
   561	
   562		if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, s.Cause, reason); err != nil {
   563			if spent {
   564				// Out of deliveries: a Nak is dropped by the broker, so saying
   565				// "retried" would be a lie. Leave it unsettled and name the state.
   566				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   567				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; dead-letter capture failed with no deliveries left",
   568					slog.Any("error", err),
   569					slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   570					slog.String("reason", reason),
   571					slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   572					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor))
   573				r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   574				return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:stranded: %w", err)
   575			}
   576			// Deliveries remain — fall back to the ladder so the capture is
   577			// retried. Preserve the cause: the terminal branch was reached and
   578			// could not complete.
   579			naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
   580			naked.Cause = s.Cause

   582		}

   586		// the floor pinned with nothing reporting it. Waiting for the server's
   587		// confirmation is what makes the settlement a fact rather than a hope, and

   595				// no further delivery is coming: it will pin the ack floor until
   596				// the stream's retention expires it. Captured distinguishes this
   597				// from a stranding with nothing captured — the data is recoverable,
   598				// the consumer is not.
   599				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   600				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; captured to the DLQ but the ack failed with no deliveries left",

   602					slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   603					slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   604					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor))

   607			}

   613		}

   615		s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered

   618			slog.String("reason", reason),

   620			slog.Duration("failing_for", s.FailingFor),
   621			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor),
   622			slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", s.FloorAge))

   657	func (r *Retry) capture(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, cause Cause, reason string) error {
   658		if err := natsmsg.DeadLetter(ctx, r.cfg.Publisher, r.cfg.DLQSubject, msg, string(cause)+": "+reason); err != nil {

   660			logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": settle:dlq_publish_failed",
   661				slog.Any("error", err),

   663				slog.String("cause", string(cause)))

   665		}
   666		return nil
   667	}

   669	// nak schedules the next delivery on the ladder and completes s.
   670	func (r *Retry) nak(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) (Settlement, error) {
   671		s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried

   673		err := msg.NakWithDelay(s.Delay)

   677		}
   678		return s, nil
   679	}

   682		if r.cfg.OnSettle != nil {
   683			r.cfg.OnSettle(ctx, msg, s)
   684		}
   685	}

   611			r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   612			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
   613		}
   614	
   615		s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
   616		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": dead-lettered",
   617			slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   618			slog.String("reason", reason),
   619			slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   620			slog.Duration("failing_for", s.FailingFor),
   621			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor),
   622			slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", s.FloorAge))
   623		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   624		return s, nil
   625	}
   626	
   627	// DeadLetter captures msg to the DLQ and Acks it immediately, for a failure
   628	// the handler knows no redelivery can fix — an unprocessable payload, a
   629	// reference that will never resolve. It is the non-lossy replacement for a
   630	// bare Term: same terminal effect on the consumer, but the raw message and
   631	// its headers survive in the DLQ.
   632	//
   633	// As in [Settle], a capture failure Naks rather than dropping, and returns
   634	// the error.
   635	//
   636	// This is also the seam for an adopter that wants the stall signal without
   637	// the library's automatic disposition: build a [FloorMonitor], leave
   638	// RetryConfig.Monitor nil, and call DeadLetter from your own quarantine rule.
   639	func (r *Retry) DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   640		var floor uint64
   641		var age time.Duration
   642		if r.cfg.Monitor != nil {
   643			floor, age, _ = r.cfg.Monitor.FloorStall()
   644		}
   645		delivered := backoff.NumDelivered(msg)
   646		return r.terminate(ctx, msg, Settlement{
   647			Cause:      CausePermanent,
   648			Delivered:  delivered,
   649			FailingFor: r.failingFor(delivered),
   650			Floor:      floor,
   651			FloorAge:   age,
   652		}, reason)
   653	}
   654	
   655	// capture republishes the raw message and headers to the DLQ subject, tagging
   656	// the reason with its cause.
   657	func (r *Retry) capture(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, cause Cause, reason string) error {
   658		if err := natsmsg.DeadLetter(ctx, r.cfg.Publisher, r.cfg.DLQSubject, msg, string(cause)+": "+reason); err != nil {
   659			logger, name := r.log()
   660			logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": settle:dlq_publish_failed",
   661				slog.Any("error", err),
   662				slog.String("dlq_subject", r.cfg.DLQSubject),
   663				slog.String("cause", string(cause)))
   664			return fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_publish_failed: %w", err)
   665		}
   666		return nil
   667	}
   668	
   669	// nak schedules the next delivery on the ladder and completes s.
   670	func (r *Retry) nak(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) (Settlement, error) {
   671		s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
   672		s.Delay = r.cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(s.Delivered)
   673		err := msg.NakWithDelay(s.Delay)
   674		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   675		if err != nil {
   676			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:nak_failed: %w", err)
   677		}
   678		return s, nil
   679	}
   680	
   681	func (r *Retry) observe(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) {
   682		if r.cfg.OnSettle != nil {
   683			r.cfg.OnSettle(ctx, msg, s)
   684		}
   685	}
