     4		"context"
     5		"errors"
     6		"fmt"
     7		"log/slog"
     8		"sync"
     9		"time"
    10	
    11		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
    12	)
    13	
    14	const (
    15		// DefaultFloorAge is how long a durable's ack floor may stay stalled
    16		// before [FloorMonitor] reports it, when FloorMonitorConfig.FloorAge is
    17		// zero. Sized in ENT-1535's Session-1 forensics: above ~10m so an ordinary
    18		// transient that settles by attempt 3 never reaches it, below ~25m so the
    19		// whole stall — including the monitor's own evaluation lag — fits the
    20		// 30-minute SLA.
    21		DefaultFloorAge = 15 * time.Minute
    22	
    23		// Bounds on the derived poll interval when FloorMonitorConfig.Poll is
    24		// zero: FloorAge/10, clamped. The poll is one consumer-info request, so
    25		// the ceiling matters more than the floor.
    26		minFloorPoll = time.Second
    27		maxFloorPoll = 30 * time.Second
    28		// floorPollTimeout bounds one consumer-info request so a NATS blip cannot
    29		// wedge the poll loop — and, through it, [Runner.Stop], which joins it.
    30		floorPollTimeout = 5 * time.Second
    31	)
    32	
    33	// FloorMonitorConfig describes a [FloorMonitor].
    34	type FloorMonitorConfig struct {
    35		// FloorAge is how long the floor must be stalled before [FloorMonitor.Stalled]
    36		// reports it and the stall is logged. Zero uses DefaultFloorAge.
    37		FloorAge time.Duration
    38		// Poll is how often the durable's consumer info is read. Zero derives
    39		// FloorAge/10, clamped to [1s, 30s]. Must be shorter than FloorAge — a
    40		// stall that is never sampled cannot be resolved.
    41		Poll time.Duration
    42		// Name prefixes the monitor's log lines and Logger receives them. Both are
    43		// optional: [Start] fills them from Config.Name and Config.Logger when
    44		// unset.
    45		Name   string
    46		Logger *slog.Logger
    47	}
    48	
    49	// FloorMonitor is an advisory health signal for one durable consumer: it polls
    50	// the durable's ack floor and reports how long that floor has been STALLED.
    51	//
    52	// It is deliberately separate from disposition. Ack-floor state is
    53	// consumer-global and read here from a client-side snapshot, while the
    54	// decision to give up on a message is message-local — so this type observes
    55	// and reports, and something else decides what that is worth. [Retry] can
    56	// consume it to drive its circuit breaker; an adopter that would rather keep
    57	// that judgement can use the monitor alone, publish [FloorMonitor.FloorStall]
    58	// as a gauge, and call [Retry.DeadLetter] on its own terms.
    59	//
    60	// [Start] attaches the live consumer and runs the poll; [Runner.Stop] joins
    61	// it. A monitor belongs to exactly one durable consumer.
    62	//
    63	// # Stalled is not stationary
    64	//
    65	// The distinction is the whole correctness of anything built on this. A
    66	// caught-up consumer's floor sits still because nothing arrived, and a floor
    67	// that has been still for four idle hours says nothing about the next message
    68	// to arrive: crediting that message with the idle time — and quarantining it
    69	// on its second delivery — would be a false positive of exactly the kind this
    70	// signal exists to avoid. So the clock runs only while the consumer has
    71	// delivered past its own floor, the same floor-versus-last-delivered
    72	// comparison the incident runbook makes by hand, and it restarts the moment
    73	// the consumer catches up.
    74	//
    75	// The age is measured from the first observation of a stall, so a freshly
    76	// started process under-reports an already-old one rather than over-reporting
    77	// it: this signal can be late, never early.
    78	type FloorMonitor struct {
    79		cfg FloorMonitorConfig
    80	
    81		mu     sync.Mutex
    82		cons   jetstream.Consumer
    83		name   string
    84		logger *slog.Logger
    85		// clock reads the current time; a package-internal seam so tests can
    86		// drive the stall clock without sleeping.
    87		clock func() time.Time
    88	
    89		stalled     bool
    90		floor       uint64
    91		floorSince  time.Time
    92		stallLogged bool
    93	
    94		// polls counts live pollFloor invocations, and maxPolls the high-water
    95		// mark. A monitor belongs to one consumer, so two concurrent polls means a
    96		// caller reattached it while an earlier poll was still running — an
    97		// in-flight consumer-info reply from the OLD consumer can then land after
    98		// the reattach and overwrite fresh state with stale. It is a lifecycle
    99		// bug rather than a data race, so nothing else would catch it; [Run]'s
   100		// recreate path is the one that has to get this right.
   101		polls, maxPolls int
   102	}
   103	
   104	// NewFloorMonitor validates cfg, applies its defaults, and returns the
   105	// monitor.
   106	func NewFloorMonitor(cfg FloorMonitorConfig) (*FloorMonitor, error) {
   107		if cfg.FloorAge < 0 {
   108			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: FloorMonitorConfig.FloorAge must not be negative, got %s (omit the monitor entirely to disable it)", cfg.FloorAge)
   109		}
   110		if cfg.FloorAge == 0 {
   111			cfg.FloorAge = DefaultFloorAge
   112		}
   113		if cfg.Poll < 0 {
   114			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: FloorMonitorConfig.Poll must not be negative, got %s", cfg.Poll)
   115		}
   116		m := &FloorMonitor{cfg: cfg, clock: time.Now}
   117		if p := m.pollInterval(); p >= cfg.FloorAge {
   118			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: FloorMonitorConfig.Poll (%s) must be shorter than FloorAge (%s): a stall that is never sampled cannot be resolved", p, cfg.FloorAge)
   119		}
   120		return m, nil
   121	}
   122	
   123	// FloorAge reports the configured stall threshold.
   124	func (m *FloorMonitor) FloorAge() time.Duration { return m.cfg.FloorAge }
   125	
   126	// pollInterval is the effective poll cadence: Poll, or FloorAge/10 clamped to
   127	// [minFloorPoll, maxFloorPoll].
   128	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollInterval() time.Duration {
   129		if m.cfg.Poll > 0 {
   130			return m.cfg.Poll
   131		}
   132		return max(minFloorPoll, min(m.cfg.FloorAge/10, maxFloorPoll))
   133	}
   134	
   135	// FloorStall reports the durable's ack floor (a stream sequence), how long it
   136	// has been stalled there, and whether it is stalled at all. Publish it as a
   137	// gauge — it is the signal the ack-floor monitor pages on, available from
   138	// inside the process rather than by polling consumer info a second time.
   139	//
   140	// See the type doc for what "stalled" means, and why it is not the same as
   141	// the floor merely being motionless.
   142	func (m *FloorMonitor) FloorStall() (floor uint64, age time.Duration, stalled bool) {
   143		m.mu.Lock()
   144		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   145		if !m.stalled {
   146			return m.floor, 0, false
   147		}
   148		return m.floor, m.clock().Sub(m.floorSince), true
   149	}
   150	
   151	// Stalled reports whether the floor has been stalled past FloorAge — the
   152	// condition worth acting on, as opposed to any stall at all.
   153	func (m *FloorMonitor) Stalled() bool {
   154		_, age, stalled := m.FloorStall()
   155		return stalled && age >= m.cfg.FloorAge
   156	}
   157	
   158	// observeFloor records one reading of the durable's ack floor against its
   159	// last-delivered sequence, starting the stall clock when work is outstanding
   160	// below the delivered mark and clearing it when the consumer catches up.
   161	//
   162	// delivered <= floor means every delivery this consumer has made is settled:
   163	// there is no blocked message to age, whatever the floor has been doing. Note
   164	// this stays true while a blocker waits out a ladder rung — it has been
   165	// delivered, so Delivered stays above the floor even though nothing is
   166	// ack-pending at that instant, which is why NumAckPending is the wrong gate
   167	// here.
   168	func (m *FloorMonitor) observeFloor(floor, delivered uint64, at time.Time) {
   169		m.mu.Lock()
   170		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   171		caughtUp := delivered <= floor
   172		sameStall := m.stalled && m.floor == floor
   173		m.floor = floor
   174		switch {
   175		case caughtUp:
   176			m.stalled = false
   177		case sameStall:
   178			return // still the same stall; the clock runs on
   179		default:
   180			m.stalled = true
   181			m.floorSince = at
   182		}
   183		m.stallLogged = false
   184	}
   185	
   186	// attach binds the live consumer (and the host's log identity, when the config
   187	// left it unset). Called by [Start] on every attempt, including [Run]'s
   188	// recreates.
   189	func (m *FloorMonitor) attach(cons jetstream.Consumer, name string, logger *slog.Logger) {
   190		m.mu.Lock()
   191		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   192		m.cons = cons
   193		m.name = firstNonEmpty(m.cfg.Name, name)
   194		if m.cfg.Logger != nil {
   195			m.logger = m.cfg.Logger
   196		} else {
   197			m.logger = logger
   198		}
   199	}
   200	
   201	func (m *FloorMonitor) log() (*slog.Logger, string) {
   202		m.mu.Lock()
   203		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   204		logger, name := m.logger, m.name
   205		if logger == nil {
   206			if m.cfg.Logger != nil {
   207				logger = m.cfg.Logger
   208			} else {
   209				logger = slog.Default()
   210			}
   211		}
   212		if name == "" {
   213			name = firstNonEmpty(m.cfg.Name, "jsconsumer")
   214		}
   215		return logger, name
   216	}
   217	
   218	func firstNonEmpty(a, b string) string {
   219		if a != "" {
   220			return a
   221		}
   222		return b
   223	}
   224	
   225	// pollFloor reads the ack floor until ctx is cancelled or stop is closed (the
   226	// consume loop winding down). It samples once immediately so a long-lived
   227	// stall is observed at Start rather than one interval later.
   228	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollFloor(ctx context.Context, stop <-chan struct{}) {
   229		m.mu.Lock()
   230		m.polls++
   231		m.maxPolls = max(m.maxPolls, m.polls)
   232		m.mu.Unlock()
   233		defer func() {
   234			m.mu.Lock()
   235			m.polls--
   236			m.mu.Unlock()
   237		}()
   238	
   239		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
   240		defer cancel()
   241		// Cancel on the consume loop closing too, so an in-flight consumer-info
   242		// request cannot hold Runner.Stop open for floorPollTimeout. The watcher
   243		// exits with ctx via the deferred cancel.
   244		go func() {
   245			select {
   246			case <-stop:
   247				cancel()
   248			case <-ctx.Done():
   249			}
   250		}()
   251	
   252		m.pollOnce(ctx)
   253		t := time.NewTicker(m.pollInterval())
   254		defer t.Stop()
   255		for {
   256			select {
   257			case <-ctx.Done():
   258				return
   259			case <-t.C:
   260				m.pollOnce(ctx)
   261			}
   262		}
   263	}
   264	
   265	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollOnce(ctx context.Context) {
   266		m.mu.Lock()
   267		cons := m.cons
   268		m.mu.Unlock()
   269		if cons == nil {
   270			return
   271		}
   272		infoCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, floorPollTimeout)
   273		defer cancel()
   274		info, err := cons.Info(infoCtx)
   275		if err != nil {
   276			if ctx.Err() != nil {
   277				return // shutting down; a failed read here is the wind-down, not a fault
   278			}
   279			logger, name := m.log()
   280			logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor poll failed", slog.Any("error", err))
   281			return
   282		}
   283		m.observeFloor(info.AckFloor.Stream, info.Delivered.Stream, m.clock())
   284	
   285		// Report a stall past the threshold once per stall. This is the signal
   286		// ENT-1535 had none of in-process, and it stays visible whether or not
   287		// anything acts on it.
   288		floor, age, stalled := m.FloorStall()
   289		if !stalled || age < m.cfg.FloorAge {
   290			return
   291		}
   292		m.mu.Lock()
   293		first := !m.stallLogged
   294		m.stallLogged = true
   295		m.mu.Unlock()
   296		if !first {
   297			return
   298		}
   299		logger, name := m.log()
   300		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor stalled past FloorAge",
   301			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
   302			slog.Duration("stalled_for", age),
   303			slog.Uint64("last_delivered", info.Delivered.Stream),
   304			slog.Int("num_ack_pending", info.NumAckPending))
   305	}
   306	
   307	// errMonitorConflict is returned when a Config names one floor monitor and its
   308	// Retry another: there is one durable and one poll loop, so there can only be
   309	// one monitor.
   310	var errMonitorConflict = errors.New("Config.FloorMonitor and Retry's monitor are different: one durable has one ack floor, so both must be the same *FloorMonitor (or leave Config.FloorMonitor nil and let Start use the Retry's)")

diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index b6d15f8..a171744 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -123,7 +123,59 @@ and `jsconsumer` add the OpenTelemetry API; all three use `nats.go/jetstream`):
   Term-on-undecodable → dispatch to the handler, which owns the message's
   disposition). AckExplicit, bounded AckWait and MaxDeliver, optional
   InactiveThreshold / MaxAckPending, shutdown-aware consume-error logging,
-  optional `KeepInProgress` heartbeat.
+  optional `KeepInProgress` heartbeat. Also `Retry` — see below.
+- **`jsconsumer.Retry`** — the consumer's *single* retry mechanism: one
+  redelivery ladder, a **floor-age circuit breaker**, and the dead-letter
+  capture both terminate into. A JetStream consumer has two redelivery
+  schedulers — the server's `ConsumerConfig.BackOff` and the handler's own
+  `NakWithDelay` — and setting both does not pick one: the server stretches
+  each NAK delay by the BackOff increments, so the configured ladder becomes
+  dead config that still reads as authoritative (ENT-1535 measured a real
+  34h22m envelope against a documented 17h45m). `Config.BackOff` and
+  `Config.Retry` are therefore mutually exclusive — a `Start` error — and
+  adopting a `Retry` clears any ladder already on the durable.
+
+  Never a drop, and never a bare `Term`. A failed capture Naks instead, so the
+  message survives and the stall stays visible — and `CaptureReserve` holds
+  back deliveries specifically to retry it. When even those are spent the
+  message is reported as `OutcomeStranded`, not dressed up as a retry: a Nak
+  at the broker's cap is dropped, so nothing will touch it again and it needs
+  the break-glass runbook. Alert on that outcome.
+- **`jsconsumer.FloorMonitor`** — the durable's ack-floor health signal,
+  separate from disposition on purpose: ack-floor state is consumer-global
+  while giving up on a message is message-local, so this type observes and
+  reports and something else decides what that is worth. `Start` polls it and
+  `Stop` joins the poll. Publish `FloorStall` as a gauge, drive your own
+  quarantine rule off `Stalled()` + `Retry.DeadLetter`, or hand it to
+  `RetryConfig.Monitor` and let the breaker act on it.
+
+  It triggers on **floor-stall age**, not message stream-age: the two diverge
+  badly under backlog, where 35 minutes of receipt→first-delivery lag on a
+  perfectly healthy message would read as a stall. Stalled is also not the
+  same as *stationary* — the clock runs only while the consumer has delivered
+  past its own floor, so an idle consumer's motionless floor never accrues
+  time to charge the next arriving message with. Once the floor has been
+  stalled past `FloorAge` (default 15m), `Settle` captures the raw message and
+  headers to the DLQ and Acks the original, well before the ladder would.
+
+  It does **not** try to name the blocker. JetStream's consumer info cannot
+  identify it: `AckFloor.Stream+1` is the blocker only while the server last
+  computed the floor from a pending scan — after a drain the floor jumps to
+  the delivered high-water mark, so a poison message arriving behind
+  non-matching subjects sits well above it (measured on a live server: floor
+  2, blocker at stream 6), which any filtered consumer hits routinely. And
+  `AckFloor.Consumer+1` is worse: the server only recomputes that floor when
+  the message *at* the floor is acked, so it pins to the blocker's first
+  delivery and goes stale the moment it is redelivered. Instead the breaker
+  requires three independently-true facts — the consumer is stalled, this
+  message is above the ack floor, and this message has itself been failing at
+  least `FloorAge` (from its own delivery count against the ladder). Gap-proof,
+  redelivery-proof, and no inference about which message is responsible.
+
+  Acting on it is still a judgement over consumer-global state, so the
+  `Breaker` mode's zero value is `BreakerObserve`: evaluate and report the

    18		// DefaultMinDeliveries is the number of deliveries a message must already
    19		// have burned before the breaker will dead-letter it, when
    20		// RetryConfig.MinDeliveries is zero. The forensics found events that
    21		// recovered on attempt 4 and none that recovered on 5 or later, so a
    22		// message is never dead-lettered on the delivery that first failed —
    23		// however long the floor has been stalled, it gets at least one retry.
    24		DefaultMinDeliveries = 2
    25		// DefaultCaptureReserve is how many deliveries are held back for retrying
    26		// a failed dead-letter capture when RetryConfig.CaptureReserve is zero.
    27		// One spare delivery turns "the DLQ was briefly unreachable at exactly
    28		// the wrong moment" from a stranded message into a retry.
    29		DefaultCaptureReserve = 1

    31		// "spend every delivery on the handler". The ladder then exhausts on the
    32		// broker's own final delivery, so a capture that fails there strands the
    33		// message ([OutcomeStranded]) — acceptable only where the whole delivery
    34		// budget is needed and a stranded message is alerted on.
    35		NoCaptureReserve = -1
    36	
    37		// dlqAckTimeout bounds the DoubleAck confirming a dead-lettered message is
    38		// settled. Without a bound a NATS blip would hang the handler on the one
    39		// path that must not hang: the message is already captured, and all that
    40		// remains is releasing the ack floor.
    41		dlqAckTimeout = 15 * time.Second
    42	)
    43

    45	type Outcome string
    46

    48		// OutcomeRetried means the delivery was Nak'd for redelivery on the
    49		// ladder.
    50		OutcomeRetried Outcome = "retried"

    53		OutcomeDeadLettered Outcome = "dead_lettered"

    55		// retry it: the broker will drop a Nak at this point, so nothing in the

   197	// Retry is the single retry mechanism a jsconsumer-hosted handler uses to
   198	// settle a failed delivery. It owns the redelivery ladder, the floor-age
   199	// circuit breaker, and the dead-letter capture the two terminate into.

   202	//
   203	// A JetStream consumer has two redelivery schedulers: the server-side
   204	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig.BackOff ladder, and the client's own
   205	// NakWithDelay. Setting both does not pick one — the server stretches each
   206	// NAK delay by the BackOff increments, so redeliveries land on neither
   207	// schedule and the configured ladder becomes dead config. That is what
   208	// happened on entire-search's search-indexer-refs: its consumer advertised a
   209	// 5m/10m/30m/1h/4h/12h ladder while ENT-1535's forensics measured redelivery
   210	// at *failure-log time + the handler's own NakWithDelay*, to ±6ms — a real
   211	// envelope of 34h22m against a documented 17h45m, and nothing in the system
   212	// said so.

   215	// not a warning), and adopting a Retry actively clears any ladder already on
   216	// the durable. Whichever mechanism is configured is the only one running.

   218	// # What the breaker measures

   221	// backlog: the same forensics measured 35 minutes of receipt→first-delivery
   222	// lag on a healthy message, which a stream-age trigger would read as a stall.
   223	// The ack floor only stops advancing when a message genuinely will not
   224	// settle, which is the condition worth breaking on.

   227	// consumer-global and this decision is message-local, so the observation is a
   228	// separate, independently usable thing and RetryConfig.Monitor is what opts
   229	// into acting on it. Leave that nil and Settle is purely message-local — the
   230	// ladder and exhaustion, nothing inferred about the consumer as a whole.

   232	// Acting on it is still a judgement over consumer-global state, and one limit
   233	// remains that this package cannot resolve from inside: a stall held by
   234	// another replica's message is indistinguishable from one this process could
   235	// clear, so enforcing may quarantine a message that was failing alongside the
   236	// blocker rather than being it. That message goes to the DLQ with full
   237	// provenance and is replayable, which is the trade — but [BreakerObserve]
   238	// exists to measure the rate against real traffic first.

   242	//

   246	// FloorAge + the largest ladder rung + AckWait. Construction rejects a rung
   247	// longer than FloorAge, which bounds it at 2×FloorAge + AckWait; pick rungs
   248	// well under FloorAge to leave headroom.

   251	// applies with the breaker in observe-only mode or disabled: the DLQ is
   252	// reached at delivery Backoff.MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve, so budget
   253	// (MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve-1) rungs of wall-clock for it.

   305	// NewRetry validates cfg, applies its defaults, and returns the mechanism.
   306	// The validation is the point: every rejection here is a configuration that
   307	// would otherwise run, look configured, and quietly not do what it says.
   308	func NewRetry(cfg RetryConfig) (*Retry, error) {
   309		if cfg.Publisher == nil {
   310			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Publisher is required: dead-letter capture is the only terminal branch, so there is no configuration in which a message may be dropped")
   311		}
   312		if cfg.DLQSubject == "" {
   313			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.DLQSubject is required: see Publisher")
   314		}
   315		if cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver <= 0 {
   316			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.MaxDeliver must be positive, got %d: a non-positive value means unlimited redeliveries to backoff.Policy, so the dead-letter branch would never run", cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver)
   317		}
   318		if cfg.Backoff.TermOnExhaustion {
   319			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.TermOnExhaustion must be false: this package dead-letters and Acks on exhaustion, and a bare Term neither settles the message nor leaves a record of it (ENT-1492)")
   320		}
   321		if cfg.Backoff.NakDelay <= 0 {
   322			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.NakDelay must be positive, got %s: a zero delay redelivers immediately and burns MaxDeliver in a hot loop", cfg.Backoff.NakDelay)
   323		}
   324		if cfg.Backoff.Factor > 1 && cfg.Backoff.MaxDelay <= 0 {
   325			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.MaxDelay is required with a growing Factor: an uncapped rung cannot be checked against the monitor's FloorAge")
   326		}
   327		if cfg.MinDeliveries < 0 {
   328			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.MinDeliveries must not be negative, got %d", cfg.MinDeliveries)
   329		}
   330		if cfg.MinDeliveries == 0 {
   331			cfg.MinDeliveries = DefaultMinDeliveries
   332		}
   333		switch {
   334		case cfg.CaptureReserve == 0:
   335			cfg.CaptureReserve = DefaultCaptureReserve
   336		case cfg.CaptureReserve == NoCaptureReserve:
   337			cfg.CaptureReserve = 0
   338		case cfg.CaptureReserve < 0:
   339			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.CaptureReserve must be -1 (NoCaptureReserve), 0 (default), or positive, got %d", cfg.CaptureReserve)
   340		}
   341		if cfg.CaptureReserve >= cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver {
   342			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.CaptureReserve (%d) leaves no deliveries for the handler out of Backoff.MaxDeliver (%d)", cfg.CaptureReserve, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver)
   343		}
   344		if cfg.MinDeliveries > cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-cfg.CaptureReserve {
   345			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.MinDeliveries (%d) exceeds the ladder's %d deliveries (Backoff.MaxDeliver %d less CaptureReserve %d): the breaker could never fire before the ladder exhausted", cfg.MinDeliveries, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-cfg.CaptureReserve, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver, cfg.CaptureReserve)
   346		}
   347		if cfg.Monitor != nil {
   348			// The breaker only ever fires on a delivery, so a rung longer than
   349			// the threshold means the floor stays pinned for that rung after the
   350			// breaker arms — the exact "configured ladder is not the real
   351			// envelope" failure this type exists to prevent, just one level up.
   352			if rung, age := cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver), cfg.Monitor.FloorAge(); rung > age {
   353				return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff's largest rung (%s) exceeds the monitor's FloorAge (%s): the breaker acts on a delivery, so the floor would stay pinned for up to FloorAge+%s — shorten the ladder or raise FloorAge", rung, age, rung)
   354			}
   355		}
   356		return &Retry{cfg: cfg}, nil
   357	}

   359	// MaxDeliver reports the delivery cap this mechanism is built for; [Config]
   360	// cross-checks it against the consumer's own.
   361	func (r *Retry) MaxDeliver() int { return r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver }

   363	// Monitor reports the ack-floor signal driving this mechanism's circuit
   364	// breaker, or nil when Settle is purely message-local. [Start] polls it when
   365	// Config.FloorMonitor is unset.

   368	// ladderSpent reports whether the handler's share of the delivery budget is
   369	// used up, so the next step is the DLQ. It stops CaptureReserve deliveries
   370	// short of the broker's own cap, leaving those to retry a failed capture.

   372	// is another retry, matching backoff.IsFinalDelivery.
   373	func (r *Retry) ladderSpent(delivered int) bool {

   397			} else {

   399			}

   198	// settle a failed delivery. It owns the redelivery ladder, the floor-age
   199	// circuit breaker, and the dead-letter capture the two terminate into.

   202	//
   203	// A JetStream consumer has two redelivery schedulers: the server-side
   204	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig.BackOff ladder, and the client's own
   205	// NakWithDelay. Setting both does not pick one — the server stretches each
   206	// NAK delay by the BackOff increments, so redeliveries land on neither
   207	// schedule and the configured ladder becomes dead config. That is what
   208	// happened on entire-search's search-indexer-refs: its consumer advertised a

   211	// envelope of 34h22m against a documented 17h45m, and nothing in the system
   212	// said so.

   215	// not a warning), and adopting a Retry actively clears any ladder already on
   216	// the durable. Whichever mechanism is configured is the only one running.

   229	// into acting on it. Leave that nil and Settle is purely message-local — the
   230	// ladder and exhaustion, nothing inferred about the consumer as a whole.

   233	// remains that this package cannot resolve from inside: a stall held by
   234	// another replica's message is indistinguishable from one this process could
   235	// clear, so enforcing may quarantine a message that was failing alongside the
   236	// blocker rather than being it. That message goes to the DLQ with full
   237	// provenance and is replayable, which is the trade — but [BreakerObserve]
   238	// exists to measure the rate against real traffic first.

   246	// FloorAge + the largest ladder rung + AckWait. Construction rejects a rung
   247	// longer than FloorAge, which bounds it at 2×FloorAge + AckWait; pick rungs
   248	// well under FloorAge to leave headroom.

   251	// applies with the breaker in observe-only mode or disabled: the DLQ is
   252	// reached at delivery Backoff.MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve, so budget
   253	// (MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve-1) rungs of wall-clock for it.

   305	// NewRetry validates cfg, applies its defaults, and returns the mechanism.
   306	// The validation is the point: every rejection here is a configuration that
   307	// would otherwise run, look configured, and quietly not do what it says.
   308	func NewRetry(cfg RetryConfig) (*Retry, error) {

   310			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Publisher is required: dead-letter capture is the only terminal branch, so there is no configuration in which a message may be dropped")
   311		}
   312		if cfg.DLQSubject == "" {
   313			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.DLQSubject is required: see Publisher")
   314		}
   315		if cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver <= 0 {
   316			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.MaxDeliver must be positive, got %d: a non-positive value means unlimited redeliveries to backoff.Policy, so the dead-letter branch would never run", cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver)

   320		}
   321		if cfg.Backoff.NakDelay <= 0 {
   322			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.NakDelay must be positive, got %s: a zero delay redelivers immediately and burns MaxDeliver in a hot loop", cfg.Backoff.NakDelay)

   329		}

   336		case cfg.CaptureReserve == NoCaptureReserve:

   340		}
   341		if cfg.CaptureReserve >= cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver {
   342			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.CaptureReserve (%d) leaves no deliveries for the handler out of Backoff.MaxDeliver (%d)", cfg.CaptureReserve, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver)
   343		}
   344		if cfg.MinDeliveries > cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-cfg.CaptureReserve {
   345			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.MinDeliveries (%d) exceeds the ladder's %d deliveries (Backoff.MaxDeliver %d less CaptureReserve %d): the breaker could never fire before the ladder exhausted", cfg.MinDeliveries, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-cfg.CaptureReserve, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver, cfg.CaptureReserve)
   346		}

   349			// the threshold means the floor stays pinned for that rung after the
   350			// breaker arms — the exact "configured ladder is not the real
   351			// envelope" failure this type exists to prevent, just one level up.
   352			if rung, age := cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver), cfg.Monitor.FloorAge(); rung > age {

   354			}
   355		}
   356		return &Retry{cfg: cfg}, nil
   357	}

   359	// MaxDeliver reports the delivery cap this mechanism is built for; [Config]
   360	// cross-checks it against the consumer's own.
   361	func (r *Retry) MaxDeliver() int { return r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver }
   362	
   363	// Monitor reports the ack-floor signal driving this mechanism's circuit
   364	// breaker, or nil when Settle is purely message-local. [Start] polls it when
   365	// Config.FloorMonitor is unset.
   366	func (r *Retry) Monitor() *FloorMonitor { return r.cfg.Monitor }
   367	
   368	// ladderSpent reports whether the handler's share of the delivery budget is
   369	// used up, so the next step is the DLQ. It stops CaptureReserve deliveries
   370	// short of the broker's own cap, leaving those to retry a failed capture.
   371	// A delivered count of 0 (no metadata) is never exhaustion — the safe default
   372	// is another retry, matching backoff.IsFinalDelivery.
   373	func (r *Retry) ladderSpent(delivered int) bool {
   374		return delivered > 0 && delivered >= r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-r.cfg.CaptureReserve
   375	}
   376	
   377	// attach binds the host's log identity, when the RetryConfig left it unset.
   378	// Called by [Start] on every attempt, including [Run]'s recreates.
   379	func (r *Retry) attach(name string, logger *slog.Logger) {
   380		r.mu.Lock()
   381		defer r.mu.Unlock()
   382		r.name = firstNonEmpty(r.cfg.Name, name)
   383		if r.cfg.Logger != nil {
   384			r.logger = r.cfg.Logger
   385		} else {
   386			r.logger = logger
   387		}
   388	}
   389	
   390	func (r *Retry) log() (*slog.Logger, string) {
   391		r.mu.Lock()
   392		defer r.mu.Unlock()
   393		logger, name := r.logger, r.name
   394		if logger == nil {
   395			if r.cfg.Logger != nil {
   396				logger = r.cfg.Logger
   397			} else {
   398				logger = slog.Default()
   399			}
   400		}

   628	// the handler knows no redelivery can fix — an unprocessable payload, a
   629	// reference that will never resolve. It is the non-lossy replacement for a
   630	// bare Term: same terminal effect on the consumer, but the raw message and
   631	// its headers survive in the DLQ.

   677		}

   679	}

   682		if r.cfg.OnSettle != nil {
   683			r.cfg.OnSettle(ctx, msg, s)
   684		}
   685	}

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

I re-reviewed the current diff (`d29a0c…` against `143ec67`). The previous issues are fixed, but I found one new blocker.

- **[P1] Delivery count is not elapsed failure time.** [`failingFor`](</Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/retry.go:407>) assumes every redelivery followed the configured `NakWithDelay` ladder. JetStream also increments `NumDelivered` after `AckWait` expires—for example, when a handler crashes before calling `Settle`. My integration probe produced four deliveries in **68 ms**, but the code inferred `FailingFor=3s` and dead-lettered the fresh message during an older floor stall. This invalidates the “never early” safety claim and could quarantine many recoverable messages. Enforcement needs a durable first-failure timestamp; otherwise this should remain observe-only or be explicitly delivery-count-based.

- **[P2] Enforce mode can silently operate without a monitor.** [`NewRetry`](</Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/retry.go:308>) accepts `BreakerEnforce` with `Monitor=nil`, after which [`shouldQuarantine`](</Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/retry.go:461>) always returns false. A monitor supplied only through `Config.FloorMonitor` still does not drive the retry breaker. Reject enforce-without-monitor and unknown `BreakerMode` values during validation.

The earlier idle-floor, filtered-sequence, final-ack, lifecycle, and rollout-safety findings are resolved.

- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go build ./...`
- `mise run lint`
- `git diff --check`

Verdict: **request changes**, primarily because the elapsed-age inference is unsafe.

1	package jsconsumer
     2	
     3	import (
     4		"context"
     5		"errors"
     6		"fmt"
     7		"log/slog"
     8		"sync"
     9		"time"
    10	
    11		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
    12	
    13		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/backoff"
    14		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg"
    15	)
    16	
    17	const (
    18		// DefaultMinDeliveries is the number of deliveries a message must already
    19		// have burned before the breaker will dead-letter it, when
    20		// RetryConfig.MinDeliveries is zero. The forensics found events that
    21		// recovered on attempt 4 and none that recovered on 5 or later, so a
    22		// message is never dead-lettered on the delivery that first failed —
    23		// however long the floor has been stalled, it gets at least one retry.
    24		DefaultMinDeliveries = 2
    25		// DefaultCaptureReserve is how many deliveries are held back for retrying
    26		// a failed dead-letter capture when RetryConfig.CaptureReserve is zero.
    27		// One spare delivery turns "the DLQ was briefly unreachable at exactly
    28		// the wrong moment" from a stranded message into a retry.
    29		DefaultCaptureReserve = 1
    30		// NoCaptureReserve is the explicit RetryConfig.CaptureReserve value for
    31		// "spend every delivery on the handler". The ladder then exhausts on the
    32		// broker's own final delivery, so a capture that fails there strands the
    33		// message ([OutcomeStranded]) — acceptable only where the whole delivery
    34		// budget is needed and a stranded message is alerted on.
    35		NoCaptureReserve = -1
    36	
    37		// dlqAckTimeout bounds the DoubleAck confirming a dead-lettered message is
    38		// settled. Without a bound a NATS blip would hang the handler on the one
    39		// path that must not hang: the message is already captured, and all that
    40		// remains is releasing the ack floor.
    41		dlqAckTimeout = 15 * time.Second
    42	
    43		// maxTrackedFailures caps the per-message failure clocks a Retry holds. A
    44		// consumer failing more distinct messages than this at once is having a
    45		// systemic outage, not a poison-message incident, and the breaker being
    46		// late for some of them is the least of it.
    47		maxTrackedFailures = 4096
    48	)
    49	
    50	// stallSignal is the TRIGGER half of the breaker, kept as an interface so the
    51	// action half never depends on how a stall is detected. [FloorMonitor] is the
    52	// client-side implementation; JetStream could plausibly grow a native
    53	// equivalent (a MaxPendingAge-style consumer option), and slotting that in
    54	// should not touch the capture-and-settle path below — the server will never
    55	// know our DLQ topology, so the action stays ours whatever the trigger becomes.
    56	type stallSignal interface {
    57		// FloorStall reports the ack floor, how long it has been stalled, and
    58		// whether it is stalled at all.
    59		FloorStall() (floor uint64, age time.Duration, stalled bool)
    60		// FloorAge is the threshold past which the stall is worth acting on.
    61		FloorAge() time.Duration
    62	}
    63	
    64	var _ stallSignal = (*FloorMonitor)(nil)
    65	
    66	// Outcome is what [Retry.Settle] did with a failed delivery.
    67	type Outcome string
    68	
    69	const (
    70		// OutcomeRetried means the delivery was Nak'd for redelivery on the
    71		// ladder.
    72		OutcomeRetried Outcome = "retried"
    73		// OutcomeDeadLettered means the raw message and its headers were captured
    74		// to the DLQ subject and the original Acked, releasing the ack floor.
    75		OutcomeDeadLettered Outcome = "dead_lettered"
    76		// OutcomeStranded means the capture failed with no deliveries left to
    77		// retry it: the broker will drop a Nak at this point, so nothing in the
    78		// system will touch this message again. It is unsettled, it is pinning the
    79		// ack floor, and it needs an operator — the non-lossy break-glass in
    80		// runbooks/nats-poison-ref-event.md. Alert on this; it is the one outcome
    81		// no automation clears.
    82		OutcomeStranded Outcome = "stranded"
    83	)
    84	
    85	// Cause explains an [OutcomeDeadLettered] settlement; it is empty on a retry.
    86	type Cause string
    87	
    88	const (
    89		// CauseFloorAge is the circuit breaker: this message was pinning the
    90		// durable's ack floor and the floor had been stalled past FloorAge.
    91		CauseFloorAge Cause = "floor_age"
    92		// CauseExhausted is the ordinary terminal branch: the delivery cap was
    93		// reached (ENT-1492's dead-letter-then-Ack, replacing the unsettled Term).
    94		CauseExhausted Cause = "max_deliver"
    95		// CausePermanent is a caller-declared unprocessable message, dead-lettered
    96		// by [Retry.DeadLetter] without consuming the ladder.
    97		CausePermanent Cause = "permanent"
    98	)
    99	
   100	// Settlement reports what [Retry.Settle] chose and the state it chose it
   101	// from, for the caller's metrics and log lines. FloorAge and Floor are zero
   102	// when no ack-floor observation was available (the breaker is disabled, or
   103	// [Start] has not run yet).
   104	type Settlement struct {
   105		Outcome   Outcome
   106		Cause     Cause
   107		Delay     time.Duration // redelivery delay applied, on OutcomeRetried
   108		Delivered int           // this message's delivery count, 1-based
   109		Floor     uint64        // last observed ack floor (stream sequence)
   110		FloorAge  time.Duration // how long the floor had been stalled there
   111		// FailingFor is how long this message has been failing, MEASURED from the
   112		// first failure this process observed — the message-local half of the
   113		// breaker's condition. It is not inferred from the delivery count, which
   114		// JetStream also increments on AckWait expiry (see Retry.noteFailure), and
   115		// it restarts on process restart.
   116		FailingFor time.Duration
   117		// BreakerTripped reports that the quarantine condition was met for this
   118		// message, whether or not the breaker acted on it — so an adopter running
   119		// [BreakerObserve] can count what enforcing WOULD have dead-lettered.
   120		BreakerTripped bool
   121		// Captured reports that the raw message reached the DLQ. It is the field
   122		// that separates the two strandings: with Captured the data is safe and
   123		// only the original needs clearing, without it nothing was preserved and
   124		// the stream copy is all that remains.
   125		Captured bool
   126	}
   127	
   128	// BreakerMode is whether a [Retry] acts on its [FloorMonitor]'s stall signal.
   129	// The zero value observes; dead-lettering on a stall requires saying so.
   130	type BreakerMode int
   131	
   132	const (
   133		// BreakerObserve evaluates the quarantine condition and reports it —
   134		// through Settlement.BreakerTripped, OnSettle and a log line — without
   135		// touching the message, which stays on the ladder. This is the zero value:
   136		// handing a Retry a monitor buys the measurement, never an automatic
   137		// disposition you did not ask for.
   138		//
   139		// It is a faithful dry run, not a looser one: a trip consumes the same
   140		// one-per-stall-window budget it would consume when enforcing, so the
   141		// counts an adopter collects here are the counts enforcing would produce
   142		// — not the far larger number of messages that merely satisfied the
   143		// conditions.
   144		BreakerObserve BreakerMode = iota
   145		// BreakerEnforce dead-letters and Acks a message that meets the condition.
   146		// Adopt it once BreakerObserve has shown the trip rate against real
   147		// traffic — idle stretches, filtered streams, restarts, replica splits, a
   148		// DLQ outage.
   149		BreakerEnforce
   150	)
   151	
   152	func (m BreakerMode) String() string {
   153		if m == BreakerEnforce {
   154			return "enforce"
   155		}
   156		return "observe"
   157	}
   158	
   159	// RetryConfig describes a [Retry]: the one redelivery ladder, the floor-age
   160	// circuit breaker, and the dead-letter capture they both terminate into.
   161	type RetryConfig struct {
   162		// Backoff is the redelivery envelope applied to a transient failure. Its
   163		// MaxDeliver must be positive and must equal the consumer's
   164		// Config.EffectiveMaxDeliver() — the two are cross-checked, because a
   165		// policy that disagrees with the broker either never reaches its terminal

   242	// Retry is the single retry mechanism a jsconsumer-hosted handler uses to
   243	// settle a failed delivery. It owns the redelivery ladder, the floor-age
   244	// circuit breaker, and the dead-letter capture the two terminate into.
   245	//
   246	// # Why the library owns this, and owns it alone
   247	//
   248	// A JetStream consumer has two redelivery schedulers: the server-side
   249	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig.BackOff ladder, and the client's own
   250	// NakWithDelay. Setting both does not pick one — the server stretches each
   251	// NAK delay by the BackOff increments, so redeliveries land on neither
   252	// schedule and the configured ladder becomes dead config. That is what
   253	// happened on entire-search's search-indexer-refs: its consumer advertised a
   254	// 5m/10m/30m/1h/4h/12h ladder while ENT-1535's forensics measured redelivery
   255	// at *failure-log time + the handler's own NakWithDelay*, to ±6ms — a real
   256	// envelope of 34h22m against a documented 17h45m, and nothing in the system
   257	// said so.
   258	//
   259	// So Config.BackOff and Config.Retry are mutually exclusive (a Start error,
   260	// not a warning), and adopting a Retry actively clears any ladder already on
   261	// the durable. Whichever mechanism is configured is the only one running.
   262	//
   263	// # What the breaker measures
   264	//
   265	// Floor-stationary age, not message stream-age. The two diverge badly under
   266	// backlog: the same forensics measured 35 minutes of receipt→first-delivery
   267	// lag on a healthy message, which a stream-age trigger would read as a stall.
   268	// The ack floor only stops advancing when a message genuinely will not
   269	// settle, which is the condition worth breaking on.
   270	//
   271	// The signal itself lives in [FloorMonitor], deliberately: ack-floor state is
   272	// consumer-global and this decision is message-local, so the observation is a
   273	// separate, independently usable thing and RetryConfig.Monitor is what opts
   274	// into acting on it. Leave that nil and Settle is purely message-local — the
   275	// ladder and exhaustion, nothing inferred about the consumer as a whole.
   276	//
   277	// Acting on it is still a judgement over consumer-global state, and one limit
   278	// remains that this package cannot resolve from inside: a stall held by
   279	// another replica's message is indistinguishable from one this process could
   280	// clear, so enforcing may quarantine a message that was failing alongside the
   281	// blocker rather than being it. Two things bound that. The message goes to
   282	// the DLQ with full provenance and is replayable; and the breaker claims at
   283	// most one message per stall window, so a wrong guess costs one message per
   284	// FloorAge rather than a drained consumer (see spendQuarantineBudgetLocked).
   285	// [BreakerObserve] measures the rate against real traffic first.
   286	//
   287	// # Non-goal: a handler that dies on the poison message
   288	//
   289	// If the handler panics, OOMs, or otherwise takes the process down instead of
   290	// returning, this package never sees the failure. Settle is the only entry
   291	// point to every disposition it owns — ladder, exhaustion and breaker alike —
   292	// so a message that kills its handler is not retried late or quarantined
   293	// late; it is not settled at all, by any of them. That is a property of the
   294	// callback contract, not of how elapsed failure time is computed, and it
   295	// would be equally true of a breaker that inferred time from the delivery
   296	// count.
   297	//
   298	// This is deliberate, and it is consistent with the module's existing posture
   299	// that a panicking loop is fatal rather than something to recover and carry
   300	// on from (see nuts.ShutdownGroup). Swallowing a panic here to dead-letter
   301	// the message would hide the bug that caused it and leave the handler's own
   302	// state unreconciled — the wrong trade for a library that does not know what
   303	// the handler was in the middle of.
   304	//
   305	// The failure stays loud rather than silent. [FloorMonitor] polls
   306	// independently of message flow, so it keeps reporting the stall for as long
   307	// as the process lives; the ack-floor monitor still pages; and a crash-looping
   308	// pod is itself an alerting surface. What does not happen is automatic
   309	// remediation, and that is the intended boundary: a consumer whose handler
   310	// cannot survive its input needs the crash fixed, not the evidence Acked away.
   311	//
   312	// A related and much milder case: because the failure clock is per-process,
   313	// frequent restarts for unrelated reasons (a rollout, an OOM elsewhere) reset
   314	// it, so the breaker is late by however much of the window was lost. Late is
   315	// the safe direction, and it is the same conservatism [FloorMonitor] applies
   316	// to the stall itself.
   317	//
   318	// # Trigger and action
   319	//
   320	// The two halves are kept apart. The trigger — "the floor has been stalled
   321	// this long" — is behind the stallSignal interface, because JetStream could
   322	// plausibly grow a native equivalent one day. The action — capture to a DLQ,
   323	// then settle — never will be native: the server does not know our DLQ
   324	// topology. A future native trigger slots in without touching the capture
   325	// path.
   326	//
   327	// A Retry belongs to exactly one durable consumer; give each consumer its
   328	// own.
   329	//
   330	// # Worst-case pin
   331	//
   332	// The breaker acts on a delivery, so the floor can stay pinned for up to
   333	// FloorAge + the largest ladder rung + AckWait. Construction rejects a rung
   334	// longer than FloorAge, which bounds it at 2×FloorAge + AckWait; pick rungs
   335	// well under FloorAge to leave headroom.
   336	//
   337	// The ladder's own reach is a second, independent bound, and the one that
   338	// applies with the breaker in observe-only mode or disabled: the DLQ is
   339	// reached at delivery Backoff.MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve, so budget
   340	// (MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve-1) rungs of wall-clock for it.
   341	//
   342	// # Wiring
   343	//
   344	// The first adopter, entire-search's search-indexer-refs on repo_refs_v1,
   345	// wires it like this — a flat ladder, so the whole envelope is one number:
   346	//
   347	//	floor, err := jsconsumer.NewFloorMonitor(jsconsumer.FloorMonitorConfig{}) // 15m
   348	//	if err != nil {
   349	//		return err
   350	//	}
   351	//	retry, err := jsconsumer.NewRetry(jsconsumer.RetryConfig{
   352	//		Backoff:    backoff.Policy{NakDelay: 5 * time.Minute, MaxDeliver: 6},
   353	//		DLQSubject: "repo.refs.dlq",   // captured into repo_refs_dlq_v1
   354	//		Publisher:  js,                // the handle the service already publishes with
   355	//		OnSettle:   metrics.RefEventSettled,
   356	//		Monitor:    floor,             // omit to keep Settle message-local
   357	//		Breaker:    jsconsumer.BreakerEnforce, // the zero value only observes
   358	//	})
   359	//	if err != nil {
   360	//		return err
   361	//	}
   362	//	cfg := jsconsumer.Config{
   363	//		Stream: "repo_refs_v1", Durable: "search-indexer-refs",
   364	//		Name: "search-indexer-refs", AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 6,
   365	//		Retry: retry, // and NOT Config.BackOff — Start rejects both
   366	//	}
   367	//
   368	//	handle := func(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, ev RefEvent) {
   369	//		switch err := index(ctx, ev); {
   370	//		case err == nil:
   371	//			_ = msg.Ack()
   372	//		case errors.Is(err, errUnprocessable):
   373	//			_, _ = retry.DeadLetter(ctx, msg, err.Error()) // no redelivery can fix it
   374	//		default:
   375	//			_, _ = retry.Settle(ctx, msg, err.Error()) // ladder, or breaker, or exhaustion
   376	//		}
   377	//	}
   378	//
   379	// That bounds a pinned ack floor at 15m + 5m + 30s = 20m30s, inside the
   380	// 30-minute SLA the ack-floor monitor is written against. The ladder alone —
   381	// what governs under [BreakerObserve], or with no Monitor — reaches the DLQ
   382	// on delivery 5 of 6, four 5-minute rungs (~20m), with the sixth delivery
   383	// held back to retry a failed capture.
   384	type Retry struct {
   385		cfg RetryConfig
   386		// failureTTL is how long a message's failure clock is kept after its last
   387		// observed failure: a full ladder plus the stall window, so a message
   388		// still riding the ladder is never forgotten mid-flight.
   389		failureTTL time.Duration
   390	
   391		mu     sync.Mutex
   392		name   string
   393		logger *slog.Logger
   394		// monitor is cfg.Monitor behind the trigger interface, so nothing below
   395		// depends on the stall coming from a client-side poll. Nil when the
   396		// breaker is not armed.
   397		monitor stallSignal
   398		// clock reads the current time; a package-internal seam so tests can drive
   399		// the failure clock without sleeping.
   400		clock func() time.Time
   401		// failing is when this process first, and last, saw each stream sequence
   402		// fail — the measured basis for the breaker's message-local condition.
   403		failing map[uint64]failureRecord
   404		// quarantined is when the breaker last claimed a message, and the ack
   405		// floor it was stalled at, which together ration the breaker to one
   406		// message per stall window. See spendQuarantineBudgetLocked.
   407		quarantined      time.Time
   408		quarantinedFloor uint64
   409		haveQuarantined  bool
   410	}

   412	type failureRecord struct{ first, last time.Time }

   414	// NewRetry validates cfg, applies its defaults, and returns the mechanism.
   415	// The validation is the point: every rejection here is a configuration that
   416	// would otherwise run, look configured, and quietly not do what it says.
   417	func NewRetry(cfg RetryConfig) (*Retry, error) {
   418		if cfg.Publisher == nil {
   419			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Publisher is required: dead-letter capture is the only terminal branch, so there is no configuration in which a message may be dropped")
   420		}
   421		if cfg.DLQSubject == "" {
   422			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.DLQSubject is required: see Publisher")
   423		}
   424		if cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver <= 0 {
   425			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.MaxDeliver must be positive, got %d: a non-positive value means unlimited redeliveries to backoff.Policy, so the dead-letter branch would never run", cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver)
   426		}
   427		if cfg.Backoff.TermOnExhaustion {
   428			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.TermOnExhaustion must be false: this package dead-letters and Acks on exhaustion, and a bare Term neither settles the message nor leaves a record of it (ENT-1492)")
   429		}
   430		if cfg.Backoff.NakDelay <= 0 {
   430		if cfg.Backoff.NakDelay <= 0 {
   431			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.NakDelay must be positive, got %s: a zero delay redelivers immediately and burns MaxDeliver in a hot loop", cfg.Backoff.NakDelay)
   432		}
   433		if cfg.Backoff.Factor > 1 && cfg.Backoff.MaxDelay <= 0 {
   434			return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff.MaxDelay is required with a growing Factor: an uncapped rung cannot be checked against the monitor's FloorAge")
   435		}
   436		if cfg.MinDeliveries < 0 {
   437			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.MinDeliveries must not be negative, got %d", cfg.MinDeliveries)
   438		}
   439		if cfg.MinDeliveries == 0 {
   440			cfg.MinDeliveries = DefaultMinDeliveries
   441		}
   442		switch {
   443		case cfg.CaptureReserve == 0:
   444			cfg.CaptureReserve = DefaultCaptureReserve
   445		case cfg.CaptureReserve == NoCaptureReserve:
   446			cfg.CaptureReserve = 0
   447		case cfg.CaptureReserve < 0:
   448			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.CaptureReserve must be -1 (NoCaptureReserve), 0 (default), or positive, got %d", cfg.CaptureReserve)
   449		}
   450		if cfg.CaptureReserve >= cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver {
   451			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.CaptureReserve (%d) leaves no deliveries for the handler out of Backoff.MaxDeliver (%d)", cfg.CaptureReserve, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver)
   452		}
   453		if cfg.MinDeliveries > cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-cfg.CaptureReserve {
   454			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.MinDeliveries (%d) exceeds the ladder's %d deliveries (Backoff.MaxDeliver %d less CaptureReserve %d): the breaker could never fire before the ladder exhausted", cfg.MinDeliveries, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-cfg.CaptureReserve, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver, cfg.CaptureReserve)
   455		}
   456		switch cfg.Breaker {
   457		case BreakerObserve:
   458		case BreakerEnforce:
   459			if cfg.Monitor == nil {
   460				return nil, errors.New("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Breaker is BreakerEnforce but Monitor is nil: there is no stall signal to enforce on, so the breaker would silently never fire — supply the FloorMonitor here (Config.FloorMonitor alone drives the poll, not this mechanism's disposition)")
   461			}
   462		default:
   463			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Breaker is %d, want BreakerObserve or BreakerEnforce", cfg.Breaker)
   464		}
   465		if cfg.RecoverBy < 0 {
   466			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.RecoverBy must not be negative, got %d", cfg.RecoverBy)
   467		}
   468		if cfg.RecoverBy == 0 {
   469			cfg.RecoverBy = cfg.MinDeliveries
   470		}
   471		if cfg.RecoverBy > cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-cfg.CaptureReserve {
   472			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.RecoverBy (%d) exceeds the ladder's %d deliveries: recovery is expected after the ladder has already given up", cfg.RecoverBy, cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-cfg.CaptureReserve)
   473		}
   474		if cfg.Monitor != nil {
   475			// The ladder and the threshold are one schedule. A message riding the
   476			// ladder accumulates failure time rung by rung, so if the wait to its
   477			// expected recovery reaches the breaker's threshold, the breaker can
   478			// quarantine a transient that was still going to succeed.
   479			if cum, age := cumulativeDelay(cfg.Backoff, cfg.RecoverBy), cfg.Monitor.FloorAge(); cum >= age {
   480				return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: the ladder reaches delivery %d (RecoverBy) after %s, at or past the monitor's FloorAge (%s): a transient still inside its recovery window could be dead-lettered — shorten the ladder, lower RecoverBy, or raise FloorAge", cfg.RecoverBy, cum, age)
   481			}
   482			// The breaker only ever fires on a delivery, so a rung longer than
   483			// the threshold means the floor stays pinned for that rung after the
   484			// breaker arms — the exact "configured ladder is not the real
   485			// envelope" failure this type exists to prevent, just one level up.
   486			if rung, age := cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver), cfg.Monitor.FloorAge(); rung > age {
   487				return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: RetryConfig.Backoff's largest rung (%s) exceeds the monitor's FloorAge (%s): the breaker acts on a delivery, so the floor would stay pinned for up to FloorAge+%s — shorten the ladder or raise FloorAge", rung, age, rung)
   488			}
   489		}
   490		// Keep a failure clock for a full ladder plus the stall window, so a
   491		// message still riding the ladder is never swept mid-flight.
   492		ttl := 2 * time.Minute
   493		for n := 1; n <= cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver; n++ {
   494			ttl += cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(n)
   495		}
   496		if cfg.Monitor != nil {
   497			ttl += cfg.Monitor.FloorAge()
   498		}
   499		r := &Retry{cfg: cfg, failureTTL: ttl, clock: time.Now}
   500		if cfg.Monitor != nil {
   501			r.monitor = cfg.Monitor
   502		}
   503		return r, nil
   504	}

   506	// cumulativeDelay is the total scheduled wait a message has served by the time
   507	// it is delivered for the nth time: the rungs 1..n-1. Used at construction to
   508	// check the ladder against the breaker threshold. It is NOT used at runtime to
   509	// judge a message — see [Retry.noteFailure] for why elapsed failure time is
   510	// measured rather than inferred from a delivery count.
   511	func cumulativeDelay(p backoff.Policy, n int) time.Duration {
   512		var total time.Duration
   513		for i := 1; i < n; i++ {
   514			total += p.DelayFor(i)
   515		}
   516		return total
   517	}

   519	// MaxDeliver reports the delivery cap this mechanism is built for; [Config]
   520	// cross-checks it against the consumer's own.
   521	func (r *Retry) MaxDeliver() int { return r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver }

   523	// Monitor reports the ack-floor signal driving this mechanism's circuit
   524	// breaker, or nil when Settle is purely message-local. [Start] polls it when
   525	// Config.FloorMonitor is unset.
   526	func (r *Retry) Monitor() *FloorMonitor { return r.cfg.Monitor }
   527	
   528	// ladderSpent reports whether the handler's share of the delivery budget is
   529	// used up, so the next step is the DLQ. It stops CaptureReserve deliveries
   530	// short of the broker's own cap, leaving those to retry a failed capture.
   531	// A delivered count of 0 (no metadata) is never exhaustion — the safe default
   532	// is another retry, matching backoff.IsFinalDelivery.
   533	func (r *Retry) ladderSpent(delivered int) bool {
   534		return delivered > 0 && delivered >= r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver-r.cfg.CaptureReserve
   535	}

   567	// noteFailure records that this process has seen the message at stream
   568	// sequence seq fail, and reports how long it has been failing — measured from
   569	// the first failure this process observed, never inferred.
   570	//
   571	// The inference this replaces was wrong in the one direction that matters.
   572	// Summing the ladder rungs a message "must have" served assumes every
   573	// redelivery came from a NakWithDelay, and JetStream also increments
   574	// NumDelivered on AckWait expiry: a handler that panics, a pod killed
   575	// mid-flight, an eviction under MaxAckPending. Four crash-deliveries can land
   576	// in milliseconds, and the ladder arithmetic would score them as three rungs
   577	// — dead-lettering a message that had barely arrived, on the strength of a
   578	// stall it had nothing to do with. Measuring beats inferring.
   579	//
   580	// The clock is per-process, so it resets on restart and does not follow a
   581	// message across replicas. Both make the breaker LATE, which is the safe
   582	// direction and the same conservatism [FloorMonitor] applies to the stall
   583	// itself: this can be late, never early.
   584	func (r *Retry) noteFailure(seq uint64, now time.Time) time.Duration {
   585		r.mu.Lock()
   586		defer r.mu.Unlock()
   587		if r.failing == nil {
   588			r.failing = make(map[uint64]failureRecord)
   589		}
   590		rec, seen := r.failing[seq]
   591		if !seen {
   592			rec.first = now
   593		}
   594		rec.last = now
   595		r.failing[seq] = rec
   596		if len(r.failing) > maxTrackedFailures {
   597			r.sweepFailuresLocked(now)
   598		}
   599		return now.Sub(rec.first)
   600	}

   602	// forgetFailure drops a message's clock once it has been settled for good.
   603	func (r *Retry) forgetFailure(seq uint64) {
   604		r.mu.Lock()
   605		defer r.mu.Unlock()
   606		delete(r.failing, seq)
   607	}

   609	// sweepFailuresLocked drops clocks for messages that have stopped coming
   610	// back. A message that recovers is simply never settled again, so nothing
   611	// else would remove its entry; anything untouched for longer than a full
   612	// ladder plus the stall window has either succeeded or moved to another
   613	// replica. If the sweep does not free enough, the oldest-touched entries go
   614	// too — losing a clock only costs the breaker some lateness.
   615	func (r *Retry) sweepFailuresLocked(now time.Time) {
   616		for seq, rec := range r.failing {
   617			if now.Sub(rec.last) > r.failureTTL {
   618				delete(r.failing, seq)
   619			}
   620		}
   621		for len(r.failing) > maxTrackedFailures*3/4 {
   622			var oldestSeq uint64
   623			var oldest time.Time
   624			for seq, rec := range r.failing {
   625				if oldest.IsZero() || rec.last.Before(oldest) {
   626					oldestSeq, oldest = seq, rec.last
   627				}
   628			}
   629			delete(r.failing, oldestSeq)
   630		}
   631	}
   632	
   633	// shouldQuarantine reports whether msg may be dead-lettered on the strength of
   634	// a stalled ack floor, along with the stall it was judged against.
   635	//
   636	// # Why this is a conjunction and not an identification
   637	//
   638	// The obvious rule — "dead-letter the message pinning the floor" — needs the
   639	// blocker's identity, and JetStream's consumer info does not carry it. The
   640	// two candidate inferences both fail against a live server:
   641	//
   642	//   - AckFloor.Stream+1 is the blocker only when the floor was last computed
   643	//     by the server's pending scan. After the consumer fully drains, the floor
   644	//     jumps to the delivered high-water mark, and a poison message arriving
   645	//     behind non-matching subjects then sits well above floor+1 (measured:
   646	//     floor 2, blocker at stream 6). A filtered consumer hits this routinely.
   647	//   - AckFloor.Consumer+1 is worse. The server only recomputes that floor when
   648	//     the message AT the floor is acked, so it pins to the blocker's FIRST
   649	//     delivery and goes stale the moment it is redelivered (measured: floor
   650	//     stuck at 1 while the blocker's redeliveries ran 4, 5, 6). It matches on
   651	//     delivery 1 and never again — so any MinDeliveries above 1 disables the
   652	//     breaker entirely.
   653	//
   654	// So this does not guess which message is responsible. It requires three
   655	// facts that are each independently true, and acts only when all three hold:
   656	//
   657	//  1. the consumer is genuinely stuck — the monitor reports the ack floor
   658	//     stalled past FloorAge (consumer-global, advisory);
   659	//  2. this message is part of what is stuck — its stream sequence is above
   660	//     the ack floor, so it is un-settled (exact, and free of any assumption
   661	//     about filters or gaps);
   662	//  3. this message has itself been failing at least as long as the stall —
   663	//     from its own delivery count against the ladder (message-local, exact).
   664	//
   665	// A message satisfying all three has burned FloorAge of retries, on its own,
   666	// while the consumer demonstrably made no progress. Whether or not it is the
   667	// head-of-line blocker, it is not a message that is about to recover: the
   668	// ENT-1535 forensics found recoveries at attempt 4 and none at 5 or later.
   669	// If it IS the blocker the floor is released; if it is not, a message that
   670	// has been failing for a quarter of an hour is captured to the DLQ with full
   671	// provenance and can be replayed.
   672	func (r *Retry) shouldQuarantine(msg jetstream.Msg, delivered int, failingFor time.Duration, now time.Time) (ok bool, floor uint64, age time.Duration) {
   673		mon := r.monitor
   674		if mon == nil {
   675			return false, 0, 0
   676		}
   677		floor, age, stalled := mon.FloorStall()
   678		if !stalled || age < mon.FloorAge() {
   679			return false, floor, age
   680		}
   681		meta, err := msg.Metadata()
   682		if err != nil || meta == nil {
   683			return false, floor, age
   684		}
   685		if meta.Sequence.Stream <= floor {
   686			return false, floor, age // already settled past; not part of the stall
   687		}
   688		if delivered < r.cfg.MinDeliveries {
   689			return false, floor, age
   690		}
   691		if failingFor < mon.FloorAge() {
   692			return false, floor, age
   693		}
   694		r.mu.Lock()
   695		defer r.mu.Unlock()
   696		return r.spendQuarantineBudgetLocked(floor, mon.FloorAge(), now), floor, age
   697	}
   698	
   699	// spendQuarantineBudgetLocked rations the breaker to one message per stall
   700	// window, and is what makes it a poison-message remedy rather than a mass
   701	// dead-lettering engine.
   702	//
   703	// Without it, a systemic outage — entiredb down for an hour — trips every one
   704	// of the conditions for EVERY message in flight: the floor is stalled, they
   705	// are all above it, and they have all been failing longer than the threshold.
   706	// The breaker would empty the consumer into the DLQ. The floor+1 rule this
   707	// replaced had selectivity for free by only ever matching one message; the
   708	// conjunction has to buy it back explicitly.
   709	//
   710	// One claim per window, and the window resets when the ack floor MOVES. A
   711	// blocker that really was holding the floor is therefore cleared, the floor
   712	// advances, and the next one becomes eligible immediately — successive
   713	// floor-holders drain at the rate the stall clock allows (a few per hour at
   714	// the default threshold). A claim that did NOT move the floor was aimed at
   715	// the wrong message, and the next attempt waits out a full window rather than
   716	// working through the backlog one Ack at a time.
   717	//
   718	// It also bounds the blast radius of a false positive to one message per
   719	// FloorAge, whatever the cause.
   720	func (r *Retry) spendQuarantineBudgetLocked(floor uint64, window time.Duration, now time.Time) bool {
   721		switch {
   722		case !r.haveQuarantined, floor != r.quarantinedFloor, now.Sub(r.quarantined) >= window:
   723		default:
   724			return false
   725		}
   726		r.haveQuarantined = true
   727		r.quarantined = now
   728		r.quarantinedFloor = floor
   729		return true
   730	}
   730	}
   731	
   732	// Settle applies the mechanism to a delivery whose handler failed
   733	// transiently, and is the only disposition call such a handler makes. It
   734	// picks exactly one of:
   735	//
   736	//   - the circuit breaker — the consumer's ack floor has been stalled past
   737	//     FloorAge and this message has itself been failing that long (see
   738	//     shouldQuarantine): capture to the DLQ and Ack, well before the ladder
   739	//     would have run out (Cause
   740	//     CauseFloorAge). Under [BreakerObserve] the condition is reported on
   741	//     the Settlement and the message stays on the ladder;
   742	//   - exhaustion — the ladder is spent (delivery MaxDeliver-CaptureReserve or
   743	//     later): capture to the DLQ and Ack (Cause CauseExhausted);
   744	//   - the ladder — NakWithDelay for redelivery (Outcome OutcomeRetried).
   745	//
   746	// reason is recorded on the captured copy's Nats-Dlq-Reason header, prefixed
   747	// with the cause, so the DLQ says why a message is there and not just that it
   748	// is.
   749	//
   750	// # When the capture itself fails
   751	//
   752	// A capture failure is never allowed to become a drop, and the Settlement
   753	// says which of two very different things happened:
   754	//
   755	//   - Deliveries remain (CaptureReserve is doing its job): the original is
   756	//     Nak'd, the error returned is settle:dlq_publish_failed, and the
   757	//     Settlement reports OutcomeRetried with the Cause of the terminal branch
   758	//     that could not complete — so the caller's metrics show a DLQ path being
   759	//     reached and failing rather than one sitting idle. The next delivery
   760	//     retries the capture.
   761	//   - No deliveries remain: a Nak here is dropped by the broker, so nothing
   762	//     will retry. The Settlement reports [OutcomeStranded] and the message is
   763	//     left unsettled, pinning the ack floor so the monitor fires — ENT-1492's
   764	//     deliberate posture for a degraded DLQ path, and the one state this
   765	//     package cannot resolve on its own. It is reported as what it is rather
   766	//     than dressed up as a retry.
   767	//
   768	// An Ack that fails after a successful capture (settle:dlq_ack_failed) leaves
   769	// the original to redeliver and be captured again; a duplicate in the DLQ
   770	// beats a lost message, and the Settlement reports OutcomeRetried.
   771	func (r *Retry) Settle(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   772		delivered := backoff.NumDelivered(msg)
   773		now := r.clock()
   774		failingFor := r.noteFailure(streamSeq(msg), now)
   775		quarantine, floor, age := r.shouldQuarantine(msg, delivered, failingFor, now)
   776	
   777		s := Settlement{
   778			Delivered:      delivered,
   779			Floor:          floor,
   780			FloorAge:       age,
   781			FailingFor:     failingFor,
   782			BreakerTripped: quarantine,
   783		}
   784		switch {
   785		case quarantine && r.cfg.Breaker == BreakerEnforce:
   786			s.Cause = CauseFloorAge
   787		case r.ladderSpent(delivered):
   788			s.Cause = CauseExhausted
   789		default:
   790			// Includes the observe-only trip: the condition is on the Settlement
   791			// and in the log, but the message keeps its remaining deliveries.
   792			if quarantine {
   793				logger, name := r.log()
   794				logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": breaker would dead-letter this message (observe only)",
   795					slog.String("reason", reason),
   796					slog.Int("delivered", delivered),
   797					slog.Duration("failing_for", s.FailingFor),
   798					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
   799					slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", age))
   800			}
   801			return r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
   802		}
   803		return r.terminate(ctx, msg, s, reason)
   804	}
   805	
   806	// terminate runs the capture-then-settle sequence shared by [Settle]'s two
   807	// terminal branches and [Retry.DeadLetter], and classifies every way it can
   808	// fall short. s must already carry its Cause.
   809	func (r *Retry) terminate(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   810		logger, name := r.log()
   811		spent := s.Delivered > 0 && s.Delivered >= r.cfg.Backoff.MaxDeliver
   812	
   813		if err := r.capture(ctx, msg, s.Cause, reason); err != nil {
   814			if spent {
   815				// Out of deliveries: a Nak is dropped by the broker, so saying
   816				// "retried" would be a lie. Leave it unsettled and name the state.
   817				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   818				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; dead-letter capture failed with no deliveries left",
   819					slog.Any("error", err),
   820					slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   821					slog.String("reason", reason),
   822					slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   823					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor))
   824				r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   825				return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:stranded: %w", err)
   826			}
   827			// Deliveries remain — fall back to the ladder so the capture is
   828			// retried. Preserve the cause: the terminal branch was reached and
   829			// could not complete.
   830			naked, nakErr := r.nak(ctx, msg, s)
   831			naked.Cause = s.Cause
   832			return naked, errors.Join(err, nakErr)
   833		}
   834		s.Captured = true
   835	
   836		// DoubleAck, not Ack: a plain Ack is fire-and-forget, so a lost one leaves
   837		// the floor pinned with nothing reporting it. Waiting for the server's
   838		// confirmation is what makes the settlement a fact rather than a hope, and
   839		// it costs one round-trip on a path that only runs when a message is being
   840		// given up on.
   841		ackCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, dlqAckTimeout)
   842		defer cancel()
   843		if err := msg.DoubleAck(ackCtx); err != nil {
   844			if spent {
   845				// The copy is safe in the DLQ, but the original is unsettled and
   846				// no further delivery is coming: it will pin the ack floor until
   847				// the stream's retention expires it. Captured distinguishes this
   848				// from a stranding with nothing captured — the data is recoverable,
   849				// the consumer is not.
   850				s.Outcome = OutcomeStranded
   851				logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": message stranded; captured to the DLQ but the ack failed with no deliveries left",
   852					slog.Any("error", err),
   853					slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   854					slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   855					slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor))
   856				r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   857				return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
   858			}
   859			// A delivery remains: the message redelivers and is captured again.
   860			// A duplicate in the DLQ beats a pinned floor.
   861			s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
   862			r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   863			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_ack_failed: %w", err)
   864		}
   865	
   866		s.Outcome = OutcomeDeadLettered
   867		r.forgetFailure(streamSeq(msg))
   868		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": dead-lettered",
   869			slog.String("cause", string(s.Cause)),
   870			slog.String("reason", reason),
   871			slog.Int("delivered", s.Delivered),
   872			slog.Duration("failing_for", s.FailingFor),
   873			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", s.Floor),
   874			slog.Duration("floor_stalled_for", s.FloorAge))
   875		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   876		return s, nil
   877	}
   878	
   879	// DeadLetter captures msg to the DLQ and Acks it immediately, for a failure
   880	// the handler knows no redelivery can fix — an unprocessable payload, a
   881	// reference that will never resolve. It is the non-lossy replacement for a
   882	// bare Term: same terminal effect on the consumer, but the raw message and
   883	// its headers survive in the DLQ.
   884	//
   885	// As in [Settle], a capture failure Naks rather than dropping, and returns
   886	// the error.
   887	//
   888	// This is also the seam for an adopter that wants the stall signal without
   889	// the library's automatic disposition: build a [FloorMonitor], leave
   890	// RetryConfig.Monitor nil, and call DeadLetter from your own quarantine rule.
   891	func (r *Retry) DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) (Settlement, error) {
   892		var floor uint64
   893		var age time.Duration
   894		if r.monitor != nil {
   895			floor, age, _ = r.monitor.FloorStall()
   896		}
   897		delivered := backoff.NumDelivered(msg)
   898		return r.terminate(ctx, msg, Settlement{
   899			Cause:      CausePermanent,
   900			Delivered:  delivered,
   901			FailingFor: r.noteFailure(streamSeq(msg), r.clock()),
   902			Floor:      floor,
   903			FloorAge:   age,
   904		}, reason)
   905	}
   906	
   907	// streamSeq is the message's stream sequence, or 0 when metadata is
   908	// unavailable (a synthetic message). All such messages share the zero key,
   909	// which is harmless: they cannot satisfy the breaker's above-the-floor
   910	// condition anyway.
   911	func streamSeq(msg jetstream.Msg) uint64 {
   912		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
   913			return meta.Sequence.Stream
   914		}
   915		return 0
   916	}
   917	
   918	// capture republishes the raw message and headers to the DLQ subject, tagging
   919	// the reason with its cause.
   920	func (r *Retry) capture(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, cause Cause, reason string) error {
   921		if err := natsmsg.DeadLetter(ctx, r.cfg.Publisher, r.cfg.DLQSubject, msg, string(cause)+": "+reason); err != nil {
   922			logger, name := r.log()
   923			logger.ErrorContext(ctx, name+": settle:dlq_publish_failed",
   924				slog.Any("error", err),
   925				slog.String("dlq_subject", r.cfg.DLQSubject),
   926				slog.String("cause", string(cause)))
   927			return fmt.Errorf("settle:dlq_publish_failed: %w", err)
   928		}
   929		return nil
   930	}
   931	
   932	// nak schedules the next delivery on the ladder and completes s.
   933	func (r *Retry) nak(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg, s Settlement) (Settlement, error) {
   934		s.Outcome = OutcomeRetried
   935		s.Delay = r.cfg.Backoff.DelayFor(s.Delivered)
   936		err := msg.NakWithDelay(s.Delay)
   937		r.observe(ctx, msg, s)
   938		if err != nil {
   939			return s, fmt.Errorf("settle:nak_failed: %w", err)
   940		}
