   334	// Start creates/updates the durable consumer on nc and begins delivering
   335	// messages to onMsg, returning a Runner that Stops when ctx is cancelled. The
   336	// stream must already exist (provisioned declaratively); callers whose cells
   337	// opt in per-stream gate Start behind that opt-in so a cell without the stream
   338	// doesn't error at CreateOrUpdateConsumer.
   339	//
   340	// Consume errors are logged at Warn, except a drain/close during shutdown —
   341	// both the core nats.go sentinels ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]) and jetstream's
   342	// own connection-closed error — which is a clean exit rather than a fault.
   343	func Start(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) (*Runner, error) {
   344		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
   345			return nil, err
   346		}
   347		js, err := jetstream.New(nc)
   348		if err != nil {
   349			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): jetstream.New: %w", cfg.Name, err)
   350		}
   351		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, cfg.Stream, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
   352			Durable:           cfg.Durable,
   353			AckPolicy:         jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
   354			AckWait:           cfg.EffectiveAckWait(),
   355			MaxDeliver:        cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(),
   356			FilterSubject:     cfg.FilterSubject,
   357			FilterSubjects:    cfg.FilterSubjects,
   358			InactiveThreshold: cfg.InactiveThreshold,
   359			MaxAckPending:     cfg.MaxAckPending,
   360			// Always sent, so an update carries it: with Config.Retry set this is
   361			// nil by validation, which CLEARS a server ladder an earlier
   362			// deployment left on the durable. Adopting Retry without that clear
   363			// would leave the two schedulers composing exactly as ENT-1535 found
   364			// them, with the library believing it owned redelivery.
   365			BackOff: cfg.BackOff,
   366		})
   367		if err != nil {
   368			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): create consumer %s/%s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, cfg.Durable, err)
   369		}
   370		consumeOpts := []jetstream.PullConsumeOpt{jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {
   371			if isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx, cerr) {
   372				return
   373			}
   374			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume error", slog.Any("error", cerr))
   375		})}
   376		switch {
   377		case cfg.KeepInProgress:
   378			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(1))
   379		case cfg.MaxMessages > 0:
   380			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(cfg.MaxMessages))
   381		}
   382		cc, err := cons.Consume(onMsg, consumeOpts...)
   383		if err != nil {
   384			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): consume %s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, err)
   385		}
   386		watcherDone := make(chan struct{})
   387		r := &Runner{cc: cc, closed: cc.Closed(), watcherDone: watcherDone}
   388		if cfg.Retry != nil {
   389			cfg.Retry.attach(cfg.Name, cfg.logger())
   390		}
   391		if mon := cfg.floorMonitor(); mon != nil {
   392			mon.attach(cons, cfg.Name, cfg.logger())
   393			pollDone := make(chan struct{})
   394			r.pollDone = pollDone
   395			go func() {
   396				defer close(pollDone)
   397				mon.pollFloor(ctx, r.closed)
   398			}()
   399		}
   400		go func() {
   401			defer close(watcherDone)
   402			select {
   403			case <-ctx.Done():
   404				r.Stop()
   405			case <-r.closed:
   406			}
   407		}()
   408		return r, nil
   409	}

   120		return OutcomeNak, nil
   121	}
   122	
   123	// DelayFor reports the redelivery delay the policy applies after delivery
   124	// number numDelivered (1 on first delivery): NakDelay for a flat policy,
   125	// NakDelay × Factor^(numDelivered-1) capped at MaxDelay for a growing one.
   126	// numDelivered ≤ 1 — including the 0 that [NumDelivered] reports when
   127	// metadata is unavailable — reads as the first delivery. Exposed so a caller
   128	// can log or meter the delay it is about to apply.
   129	func (p Policy) DelayFor(numDelivered int) time.Duration {
   130		if p.Factor <= 1 || numDelivered <= 1 {
   131			return p.NakDelay
   132		}
   133		d := float64(p.NakDelay) * math.Pow(p.Factor, float64(numDelivered-1))
   134		if p.MaxDelay > 0 && d >= float64(p.MaxDelay) {
   135			return p.MaxDelay
   136		}
   137		if d >= float64(math.MaxInt64) {
   138			// Uncapped growth outran time.Duration; saturate instead of wrapping
   139			// negative (a negative NakWithDelay would redeliver immediately).
   140			return math.MaxInt64
   141		}
   142		return time.Duration(d)
   143	}
   144	
   145	// NumDelivered reports the JetStream delivery count of a [jetstream.Msg]
   146	// (1 on first delivery), or 0 if metadata is unavailable (e.g. a synthetic test
   147	// message).
   148	func NumDelivered(msg jetstream.Msg) int {
   149		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
   150			return int(meta.NumDelivered)
   151		}
   152		return 0
   153	}
   154	
   155	// IsFinalDelivery reports whether this is the last delivery before JetStream
   156	// stops redelivering (NumDelivered has reached MaxDeliver), so a transient
   157	// failure here is terminal rather than another Nak-and-retry. A non-positive
   158	// maxDeliver means unlimited redeliveries (the jetstream.ConsumerConfig
   159	// semantics), so no delivery is final — without the guard the zero value
   160	// would read every delivery as final and Term on the first failure.
   161	// Unavailable metadata also reads as non-final: the safe default is another
   162	// retry, not a Term.
   163	func IsFinalDelivery(msg jetstream.Msg, maxDeliver int) bool {
   164		if maxDeliver <= 0 {
   165			return false
   166		}
   167		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
   168			return meta.NumDelivered >= uint64(maxDeliver)
   169		}
   170		return false
   171	}

    16		// before [FloorMonitor] reports it, when FloorMonitorConfig.FloorAge is

    29		// wedge the poll loop — and, through it, [Runner.Stop], which joins it.

    33	// FloorMonitorConfig describes a [FloorMonitor].
    34	type FloorMonitorConfig struct {
    35		// FloorAge is how long the floor must be stalled before [FloorMonitor.Stalled]
    36		// reports it and the stall is logged. Zero uses DefaultFloorAge.
    37		FloorAge time.Duration

    39		// FloorAge/10, clamped to [1s, 30s]. Must be shorter than FloorAge — a

    41		Poll time.Duration

    49	// FloorMonitor is an advisory health signal for one durable consumer: it polls
    50	// the durable's ack floor and reports how long that floor has been STALLED.
    51	//
    52	// It is deliberately separate from disposition. Ack-floor state is
    53	// consumer-global and read here from a client-side snapshot, while the
    54	// decision to give up on a message is message-local — so this type observes
    55	// and reports, and something else decides what that is worth. [Retry] can
    56	// consume it to drive its circuit breaker; an adopter that would rather keep
    57	// that judgement can use the monitor alone, publish [FloorMonitor.FloorStall]
    58	// as a gauge, and call [Retry.DeadLetter] on its own terms.
    59	//
    60	// [Start] attaches the live consumer and runs the poll; [Runner.Stop] joins
    61	// it. A monitor belongs to exactly one durable consumer.
    62	//
    63	// # Stalled is not stationary
    64	//
    65	// The distinction is the whole correctness of anything built on this. A
    66	// caught-up consumer's floor sits still because nothing arrived, and a floor
    67	// that has been still for four idle hours says nothing about the next message
    68	// to arrive: crediting that message with the idle time — and quarantining it
    69	// on its second delivery — would be a false positive of exactly the kind this
    70	// signal exists to avoid. So the clock runs only while the consumer has
    71	// delivered past its own floor, the same floor-versus-last-delivered
    72	// comparison the incident runbook makes by hand, and it restarts the moment
    73	// the consumer catches up.
    74	//
    75	// The age is measured from the first observation of a stall, so a freshly
    76	// started process under-reports an already-old one rather than over-reporting
    77	// it: this signal can be late, never early.
    78	type FloorMonitor struct {
    79		cfg FloorMonitorConfig
    80	
    81		mu     sync.Mutex
    82		cons   jetstream.Consumer
    83		name   string
    84		logger *slog.Logger
    85		// clock reads the current time; a package-internal seam so tests can
    86		// drive the stall clock without sleeping.
    87		clock func() time.Time
    88	
    89		stalled     bool
    90		floor       uint64
    91		floorSince  time.Time
    92		stallLogged bool
    93	
    94		// polls counts live pollFloor invocations, and maxPolls the high-water
    95		// mark. A monitor belongs to one consumer, so two concurrent polls means a
    96		// caller reattached it while an earlier poll was still running — an
    97		// in-flight consumer-info reply from the OLD consumer can then land after
    98		// the reattach and overwrite fresh state with stale. It is a lifecycle
    99		// bug rather than a data race, so nothing else would catch it; [Run]'s
   100		// recreate path is the one that has to get this right.
   101		polls, maxPolls int
   102	}

   104	// NewFloorMonitor validates cfg, applies its defaults, and returns the
   105	// monitor.
   106	func NewFloorMonitor(cfg FloorMonitorConfig) (*FloorMonitor, error) {
   107		if cfg.FloorAge < 0 {
   108			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: FloorMonitorConfig.FloorAge must not be negative, got %s (omit the monitor entirely to disable it)", cfg.FloorAge)
   109		}
   110		if cfg.FloorAge == 0 {
   111			cfg.FloorAge = DefaultFloorAge
   112		}
   113		if cfg.Poll < 0 {
   114			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: FloorMonitorConfig.Poll must not be negative, got %s", cfg.Poll)
   115		}
   116		m := &FloorMonitor{cfg: cfg, clock: time.Now}
   117		if p := m.pollInterval(); p >= cfg.FloorAge {
   118			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer: FloorMonitorConfig.Poll (%s) must be shorter than FloorAge (%s): a stall that is never sampled cannot be resolved", p, cfg.FloorAge)
   119		}
   120		return m, nil
   121	}

   123	// FloorAge reports the configured stall threshold.
   124	func (m *FloorMonitor) FloorAge() time.Duration { return m.cfg.FloorAge }
   125	
   126	// pollInterval is the effective poll cadence: Poll, or FloorAge/10 clamped to
   127	// [minFloorPoll, maxFloorPoll].
   128	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollInterval() time.Duration {
   129		if m.cfg.Poll > 0 {
   130			return m.cfg.Poll
   131		}
   132		return max(minFloorPoll, min(m.cfg.FloorAge/10, maxFloorPoll))
   133	}

   135	// FloorStall reports the durable's ack floor (a stream sequence), how long it
   136	// has been stalled there, and whether it is stalled at all. Publish it as a
   137	// gauge — it is the signal the ack-floor monitor pages on, available from
   138	// inside the process rather than by polling consumer info a second time.
   139	//
   140	// See the type doc for what "stalled" means, and why it is not the same as
   141	// the floor merely being motionless.
   142	func (m *FloorMonitor) FloorStall() (floor uint64, age time.Duration, stalled bool) {
   143		m.mu.Lock()
   144		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   145		if !m.stalled {
   146			return m.floor, 0, false
   147		}
   148		return m.floor, m.clock().Sub(m.floorSince), true
   149	}
   150	
   151	// Stalled reports whether the floor has been stalled past FloorAge — the
   152	// condition worth acting on, as opposed to any stall at all.
   153	func (m *FloorMonitor) Stalled() bool {
   154		_, age, stalled := m.FloorStall()
   155		return stalled && age >= m.cfg.FloorAge
   156	}

   158	// observeFloor records one reading of the durable's ack floor against its
   159	// last-delivered sequence, starting the stall clock when work is outstanding
   160	// below the delivered mark and clearing it when the consumer catches up.
   161	//
   162	// delivered <= floor means every delivery this consumer has made is settled:
   163	// there is no blocked message to age, whatever the floor has been doing. Note
   164	// this stays true while a blocker waits out a ladder rung — it has been
   165	// delivered, so Delivered stays above the floor even though nothing is
   166	// ack-pending at that instant, which is why NumAckPending is the wrong gate
   167	// here.
   168	func (m *FloorMonitor) observeFloor(floor, delivered uint64, at time.Time) {
   169		m.mu.Lock()
   170		defer m.mu.Unlock()
   171		caughtUp := delivered <= floor
   172		sameStall := m.stalled && m.floor == floor
   173		m.floor = floor
   174		switch {
   175		case caughtUp:
   176			m.stalled = false
   177		case sameStall:
   178			return // still the same stall; the clock runs on
   179		default:
   180			m.stalled = true
   181			m.floorSince = at
   182		}
   183		m.stallLogged = false
   184	}

   225	// pollFloor reads the ack floor until ctx is cancelled or stop is closed (the
   226	// consume loop winding down). It samples once immediately so a long-lived
   227	// stall is observed at Start rather than one interval later.
   228	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollFloor(ctx context.Context, stop <-chan struct{}) {
   229		m.mu.Lock()
   230		m.polls++
   231		m.maxPolls = max(m.maxPolls, m.polls)
   232		m.mu.Unlock()
   233		defer func() {
   234			m.mu.Lock()
   235			m.polls--
   236			m.mu.Unlock()
   237		}()
   238	
   239		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
   240		defer cancel()
   241		// Cancel on the consume loop closing too, so an in-flight consumer-info
   242		// request cannot hold Runner.Stop open for floorPollTimeout. The watcher
   243		// exits with ctx via the deferred cancel.
   244		go func() {
   245			select {
   246			case <-stop:
   247				cancel()
   248			case <-ctx.Done():
   249			}
   250		}()
   251	
   252		m.pollOnce(ctx)
   253		t := time.NewTicker(m.pollInterval())
   254		defer t.Stop()
   255		for {
   256			select {
   257			case <-ctx.Done():
   258				return
   259			case <-t.C:
   260				m.pollOnce(ctx)
   261			}
   262		}
   263	}
   264	
   265	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollOnce(ctx context.Context) {
   266		m.mu.Lock()
   267		cons := m.cons
   268		m.mu.Unlock()
   269		if cons == nil {
   270			return
   271		}
   272		infoCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, floorPollTimeout)
   273		defer cancel()
   274		info, err := cons.Info(infoCtx)
   275		if err != nil {
   276			if ctx.Err() != nil {
   277				return // shutting down; a failed read here is the wind-down, not a fault
   278			}
   279			logger, name := m.log()
   280			logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor poll failed", slog.Any("error", err))
   281			return
   282		}
   283		m.observeFloor(info.AckFloor.Stream, info.Delivered.Stream, m.clock())
   284	
   285		// Report a stall past the threshold once per stall. This is the signal
   286		// ENT-1535 had none of in-process, and it stays visible whether or not
   287		// anything acts on it.
   288		floor, age, stalled := m.FloorStall()
   289		if !stalled || age < m.cfg.FloorAge {
   290			return
   291		}
   292		m.mu.Lock()
   293		first := !m.stallLogged
   294		m.stallLogged = true
   295		m.mu.Unlock()
   296		if !first {
   297			return
   298		}
   299		logger, name := m.log()
   300		logger.WarnContext(ctx, name+": ack floor stalled past FloorAge",
   301			slog.Uint64("ack_floor", floor),
   302			slog.Duration("stalled_for", age),
   303			slog.Uint64("last_delivered", info.Delivered.Stream),
   304			slog.Int("num_ack_pending", info.NumAckPending))
   305	}

   284	// isShutdownConsumeErr reports whether a consume error is the benign result
   285	// of the connection going away during shutdown. [nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]
   286	// covers the core nats.go sentinels, but the jetstream consume loop surfaces
   287	// its OWN [jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed] — a distinct value that wraps
   288	// neither — so it must be matched separately or a clean rollout drain still
   289	// logs a warning (the COR-923 noise this suppression exists to remove). As
   290	// with the root classifier, it is only "clean" when ctx is already done; a
   291	// mid-run connection loss is a genuine fault worth logging.

   294			(ctx.Err() != nil && errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed))

   297	// Runner is a live consume loop. Stop halts it and is idempotent.
   298	type Runner struct {
   299		cc jetstream.ConsumeContext
   300		// closed is cc.Closed(), captured while the subscription is live (the
   301		// same channel is returned on every call, so capturing once avoids any
   302		// post-Stop race) — it closes when the consume loop has fully wound
   303		// down, including an in-flight handler.
   304		closed <-chan struct{}
   305		// watcherDone closes when Start's context-cancellation watcher exits. It is
   306		// intentionally internal: callers synchronize on Stop, while tests pin that
   307		// an explicit Stop does not retain a goroutine until the parent context ends.
   308		watcherDone <-chan struct{}
   309		// pollDone closes when the Config.Retry ack-floor poll exits; nil when no
   310		// breaker is armed. Stop joins it, so the connection the poll reads
   311		// through is safe to drain the moment Stop returns.
   312		pollDone <-chan struct{}
   313		stop     sync.Once
   314	}
   315	
   316	// Stop halts the consume loop and blocks until it has fully wound down —
   317	// including an in-flight handler — so a caller may tear down what handlers
   318	// use (stores, publishers, the NATS connection) the moment it returns: the
   319	// cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering (COR-923). Safe on a nil or
   320	// never-Started Runner, idempotent, and safe for concurrent use — an
   321	// explicit Stop can race the context-cancel stop armed by Start. Must not be
   322	// called from inside the handler; it would deadlock waiting on itself.
   323	func (r *Runner) Stop() {
   324		if r == nil || r.cc == nil {
   325			return
   326		}
   327		r.stop.Do(r.cc.Stop)
   328		<-r.closed
   329		if r.pollDone != nil {
   330			<-r.pollDone
   331		}
   332	}

   334	// Start creates/updates the durable consumer on nc and begins delivering
   335	// messages to onMsg, returning a Runner that Stops when ctx is cancelled. The
   336	// stream must already exist (provisioned declaratively); callers whose cells
   337	// opt in per-stream gate Start behind that opt-in so a cell without the stream
   338	// doesn't error at CreateOrUpdateConsumer.
   339	//
   340	// Consume errors are logged at Warn, except a drain/close during shutdown —
   341	// both the core nats.go sentinels ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]) and jetstream's
   342	// own connection-closed error — which is a clean exit rather than a fault.
   343	func Start(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) (*Runner, error) {
   344		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
   345			return nil, err
   346		}
   347		js, err := jetstream.New(nc)
   348		if err != nil {
   349			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): jetstream.New: %w", cfg.Name, err)
   350		}
   351		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, cfg.Stream, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
   352			Durable:           cfg.Durable,
   353			AckPolicy:         jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
   354			AckWait:           cfg.EffectiveAckWait(),
   355			MaxDeliver:        cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(),
   356			FilterSubject:     cfg.FilterSubject,
   357			FilterSubjects:    cfg.FilterSubjects,
   358			InactiveThreshold: cfg.InactiveThreshold,
   359			MaxAckPending:     cfg.MaxAckPending,
   360			// Always sent, so an update carries it: with Config.Retry set this is
   361			// nil by validation, which CLEARS a server ladder an earlier
   362			// deployment left on the durable. Adopting Retry without that clear
   363			// would leave the two schedulers composing exactly as ENT-1535 found
   364			// them, with the library believing it owned redelivery.
   365			BackOff: cfg.BackOff,
   366		})
   367		if err != nil {
   368			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): create consumer %s/%s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, cfg.Durable, err)
   369		}
   370		consumeOpts := []jetstream.PullConsumeOpt{jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {
   371			if isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx, cerr) {
   372				return
   373			}
   374			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume error", slog.Any("error", cerr))
   375		})}
   376		switch {
   377		case cfg.KeepInProgress:
   378			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(1))
   379		case cfg.MaxMessages > 0:
   380			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(cfg.MaxMessages))
   381		}
   382		cc, err := cons.Consume(onMsg, consumeOpts...)
   383		if err != nil {
   384			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): consume %s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, err)
   385		}
   386		watcherDone := make(chan struct{})
   387		r := &Runner{cc: cc, closed: cc.Closed(), watcherDone: watcherDone}
   388		if cfg.Retry != nil {
   389			cfg.Retry.attach(cfg.Name, cfg.logger())
   390		}
   391		if mon := cfg.floorMonitor(); mon != nil {
   392			mon.attach(cons, cfg.Name, cfg.logger())
   393			pollDone := make(chan struct{})
   394			r.pollDone = pollDone
   395			go func() {
   396				defer close(pollDone)
   397				mon.pollFloor(ctx, r.closed)
   398			}()
   399		}
   400		go func() {
   401			defer close(watcherDone)
   402			select {
   403			case <-ctx.Done():
   404				r.Stop()
   405			case <-r.closed:
   406			}
   407		}()
   408		return r, nil
   409	}

   411	// isRetryableStartError classifies the narrow set of failures that can become
   412	// healthy without changing Config or replacing nc. Everything else returns to
   413	// the owner so a bad deployment cannot stay alive indefinitely with no
   414	// consumer. Unknown server-side 5xx responses are retried, except known
   415	// permanent JetStream configuration/account errors whose API happens to use a
   416	// 5xx status.
   417	func isRetryableStartError(err error) bool {
   418		if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) ||
   419			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrNoResponders) ||
   420			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) ||
   421			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrDisconnected) {
   422			return true
   423		}
   424	
   425		var jsErr jetstream.JetStreamError
   426		if !errors.As(err, &jsErr) || jsErr.APIError() == nil {
   427			return false
   428		}
   429		apiErr := jsErr.APIError()
   430		switch apiErr.ErrorCode { //nolint:exhaustive // unrecognized 5xx codes are deliberately retryable; all other unknown codes fail closed
   431		case jetstream.JSErrCodeBadRequest,
   432			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerCreate,
   433			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerNameExists,
   434			jetstream.JSErrCodeMaximumConsumersLimit,
   435			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabledForAccount,
   436			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabled,
   437			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerAlreadyExists,

    54	// non-positive value disables the delivery cap). The zero value means the same
    55	// thing; the named constant lets a caller say so on purpose.
    56	const UnlimitedMaxDeliver = -1

    58	// Outcome is the disposition NakOrTerm chose, for the caller's metrics and
    59	// logs.

    64		OutcomeTerm Outcome = "term"

    67	// Policy is the redelivery envelope a consumer applies to transient
    68	// failures. MaxDeliver must match the consumer's on-server MaxDeliver — the
    69	// policy detects the final delivery by comparing against it.
    70	type Policy struct {
    71		// NakDelay is the base delay before redelivery, and with a zero Factor
    72		// the whole envelope: flat suits failures expected to clear on their own
    73		// timetable, with MaxDeliver bounding the total.
    74		NakDelay time.Duration
    75		// Factor is the optional multiplicative growth per prior delivery: the
    76		// Nth delivery naks with NakDelay × Factor^(N-1), capped at MaxDelay.
    77		// Values ≤ 1 (including the zero value) keep the flat envelope. Growing
    78		// envelopes suit failures that get cheaper to wait out than to retry —
    79		// a downstream in a crash loop, a rate limit — where hammering on the
    80		// flat cadence spends MaxDeliver too fast.
    81		Factor float64
    82		// MaxDelay caps the grown delay; it does nothing for a flat policy.
    83		// Zero with a growing Factor leaves growth bounded only by MaxDeliver
    84		// ending the redeliveries (the computed delay still saturates rather
    85		// than overflowing).
    86		MaxDelay time.Duration
    87		// MaxDeliver is the consumer's redelivery cap
    88		// (jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver). Non-positive (0 or
    89		// UnlimitedMaxDeliver) means unlimited redeliveries — matching the
    90		// jetstream field's semantics — so no delivery is ever final and NakOrTerm
    91		// always Naks.
    92		MaxDeliver int

    94		// work-queue message is removed cleanly rather than orphaning un-acked
    95		// (COR-762). Callers with a DLQ capture before calling NakOrTerm.

    99	// NakOrTerm applies the policy to a transiently-failed [jetstream.Msg]
   100	// delivery: NakWithDelay (see [Policy.DelayFor]) for redelivery, or — on the
   101	// final delivery with TermOnExhaustion set — Term. Without TermOnExhaustion the
   102	// final delivery still Naks; the broker drops the Nak at MaxDeliver and the
   103	// stream's retention decides the message's fate.
   104	//
   105	// The returned Outcome reports which disposition was chosen, for the caller's
   106	// metrics and logs. A disposition error is worth a log line but nothing more:
   107	// a failed Nak redelivers via AckWait expiry anyway, and a failed Term on a
   108	// work-queue stream means the message lingers exactly as it would have without
   109	// the policy.
   110	func (p Policy) NakOrTerm(msg jetstream.Msg) (Outcome, error) {
   111		if p.TermOnExhaustion && IsFinalDelivery(msg, p.MaxDeliver) {
   112			if err := msg.Term(); err != nil {
   113				return OutcomeTerm, fmt.Errorf("term on final delivery: %w", err)
   114			}
   115			return OutcomeTerm, nil
   116		}
   117		if err := msg.NakWithDelay(p.DelayFor(NumDelivered(msg))); err != nil {
   118			return OutcomeNak, fmt.Errorf("nak with delay: %w", err)
   119		}
   120		return OutcomeNak, nil
   121	}

   123	// DelayFor reports the redelivery delay the policy applies after delivery
   124	// number numDelivered (1 on first delivery): NakDelay for a flat policy,
   125	// NakDelay × Factor^(numDelivered-1) capped at MaxDelay for a growing one.
   126	// numDelivered ≤ 1 — including the 0 that [NumDelivered] reports when
   127	// metadata is unavailable — reads as the first delivery. Exposed so a caller
   128	// can log or meter the delay it is about to apply.
   129	func (p Policy) DelayFor(numDelivered int) time.Duration {
   130		if p.Factor <= 1 || numDelivered <= 1 {
   131			return p.NakDelay
   132		}
   133		d := float64(p.NakDelay) * math.Pow(p.Factor, float64(numDelivered-1))

   135			return p.MaxDelay
   136		}
   137		if d >= float64(math.MaxInt64) {
   138			// Uncapped growth outran time.Duration; saturate instead of wrapping
   139			// negative (a negative NakWithDelay would redeliver immediately).
   140			return math.MaxInt64
   141		}
   142		return time.Duration(d)
   143	}

   145	// NumDelivered reports the JetStream delivery count of a [jetstream.Msg]
   146	// (1 on first delivery), or 0 if metadata is unavailable (e.g. a synthetic test
   147	// message).
   148	func NumDelivered(msg jetstream.Msg) int {
   149		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {

   225	// pollFloor reads the ack floor until ctx is cancelled or stop is closed (the
   226	// consume loop winding down). It samples once immediately so a long-lived
   227	// stall is observed at Start rather than one interval later.
   228	func (m *FloorMonitor) pollFloor(ctx context.Context, stop <-chan struct{}) {
   229		m.mu.Lock()
   230		m.polls++
   231		m.maxPolls = max(m.maxPolls, m.polls)
   232		m.mu.Unlock()

   234			m.mu.Lock()
   235			m.polls--
   236			m.mu.Unlock()

   242		// request cannot hold Runner.Stop open for floorPollTimeout. The watcher
   243		// exits with ctx via the deferred cancel.
   244		go func() {
   245			select {
   246			case <-stop:
   247				cancel()
   248			case <-ctx.Done():
   249			}
   250		}()

   252		m.pollOnce(ctx)

   254		defer t.Stop()

   256			select {
   257			case <-ctx.Done():
   258				return
   259			case <-t.C:

   261			}
   262		}
   263	}

   266		m.mu.Lock()

   276			if ctx.Err() != nil {
   277				return // shutting down; a failed read here is the wind-down, not a fault
   278			}

   286		// ENT-1535 had none of in-process, and it stays visible whether or not
   287		// anything acts on it.
   288		floor, age, stalled := m.FloorStall()

   302			slog.Duration("stalled_for", age),
   303			slog.Uint64("last_delivered", info.Delivered.Stream),
   304			slog.Int("num_ack_pending", info.NumAckPending))

   298	type Runner struct {

   310		// breaker is armed. Stop joins it, so the connection the poll reads

   322	// called from inside the handler; it would deadlock waiting on itself.

   326		}

   480	func Run(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
   481		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
   482			return err
   483		}
   484		delay := runRetryInitial
   485		for {
   486			// Each attempt gets a child context so the cancel-watcher goroutine
   487			// Start arms is released when the attempt dies, instead of one
   488			// accumulating per recreate for the life of the process.
   489			attemptCtx, cancelAttempt := context.WithCancel(ctx)
   490			r, err := Start(attemptCtx, nc, cfg, onMsg)
   491			if err != nil {
   492				cancelAttempt()
   493				if ctx.Err() != nil {
   494					return nil //nolint:nilerr // a Start error during shutdown is a clean, ctx-driven exit, not a fault to report
   495				}
   496				if !isRetryableStartError(err) {
   497					return err
   498				}
   499				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": start consumer failed; retrying",
   500					slog.Any("error", err), slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
   501			} else {
   502				started := time.Now()
   503				select {
   504				case <-ctx.Done():
   505					r.Stop()
   506					cancelAttempt()
   507					return nil
   508				case <-r.closed:
   509					// Join before recreating, not just cancel: the attempt's
   510					// ack-floor poll may still be in an in-flight consumer-info
   511					// request against the OLD consumer, and the next Start attaches
   512					// the same monitor to a new one. Without the join that reply
   513					// can land after the reattach and overwrite fresh state with
   514					// stale. Stop is cheap here — the loop has already closed.
   515					r.Stop()
   516					cancelAttempt()
   517					if ctx.Err() != nil {
   518						return nil //nolint:nilerr // the loop closing during shutdown is the expected wind-down, not a fault
   519					}

   521					// fresh envelope; a flapping one keeps escalating.
   522					if time.Since(started) >= runRetryMax {

I re-reviewed the updated tree at `143ec67` with diff hash `80e53d…`. The earlier delivery-count inference and missing configuration validation are fixed, but I still recommend changes.

- **[P1] Failure clocks survive successful recovery.** [`noteFailure`](</Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/retry.go:584>) retains the first failure for each stream sequence, but normal success directly calls `msg.Ack()` and never informs `Retry`. If that message is replayed—after an ack loss or durable recreation—a fresh failure inherits the old age and can be dead-lettered immediately. Records below 4,096 entries are not even TTL-swept. I reproduced a recovered message being quarantined on its second fresh delivery with `FailingFor=20m`.

- **[P1] Stale floor observations remain enforceable.** [`pollOnce`](</Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/floor.go:265>) leaves the previous observation active when consumer-info polling fails, while [`FloorStall`](</Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/floor.go:142>) continues aging it. I reproduced enforcement from a 20-minute-old snapshot with no successful polls during that period. Automatic disposition should require a recent observation or disarm while polling is unhealthy.

- **[P2] `RecoverBy` is never enforced at runtime.** Its contract says a message must retain its recovery window, but [`shouldQuarantine`](</Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/jsconsumer/retry.go:672>) checks only `MinDeliveries`. A valid configuration with `RecoverBy=4` quarantined on delivery 2 after sufficient wall time. Runtime eligibility needs to include the recovery boundary.

The README also still says failure age comes “from its own delivery count” at [README.md:170](</Users/nodo/work/tasks/floor-age-circuit-breaker/go-nuts/README.md:170>), contradicting the new measured-clock implementation.

All existing validation passes: uncached tests, race tests, vet, build, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`. No remote CI applies to this uncommitted tree.
